The thing that makes Vindictus so dissapointing is that somewhere amid the tedium and endless grind for items in the late game and the boring mindless hack n' slash of the early game areas, there's something that's actually worth playing. It's hard to recommend because anyone playing it will be forced to spend their first ten hours just mashing their mouse buttons - completely mindlessly - while killing through a slew of enemies that have about as much chance of posing a threat as a limbless toddler. Their last ten hours will be spent running the same five bosses over and over again in the hopes that they get drops decent enough to actually play more of the game before they finally quit. But it's the five to ten hours somewhere in the middle there that are worth talking about.
The gameplay (when you manage to get to it) is actually great. Much /much/ better than any other action MMO I've ever played (and I've played a lot of them.) It's challenging, fast-paced, and has the highest skill-ceiling of any game of its type, including more single-player oriented games like Dark Souls. It's incredibly fun and rewarding, and completely blows games like Tera, GW2, Blade and Soul, and Dragon's Nest away. Like, its so much better that there's just genuinely no contest. It's the kind of gameplay I can't help but think other games would emulate, if the rest of Vindictus wasn't absolute trash.
Getting on a boat and riding somewhere instanced (with multiple semi-long loadscreens in-between) would be bad enough; but add to that the worst difficulty curve of any game I've ever played, and there's an even more serious problem. I've seen more than one review on here talking about the game being a boringly-easy hack n' slash because they quit after five or so hours and never hit the meat of the game. Which is completely understandable considering I did too the first 2 or 3 times I ever played it. Then I'd see youtube videos of someone fighting a giant boss that actually seemed hard, and I'd think, 'wow! That looks awesome! Where the hell was that when I was playing?' Leading to a re-download.
See, there are really cool bosses in Vindictus that eventually get extremely hard, but unfortunately they're all hidden behind 10+ hours of dungeons full of trash mobs that the average player could kill their way through while blindfolded. The worst part is, there's very little in-between. It's straight from too-easy trash mobs to 'THIS GUY IS GONNA WRECK YOU!!' It's like playing hours of tutorial level content, only to suddenly hit the final boss who promptly pushes your♥♥♥♥♥♥in.
Ultimately though, the thing that really kills the game for me is the end-game. You're cruising along. You managed to slog your way through the boring early stuff and get to real bosses, and suddenly the game is fun. The last five or so hours have been a totally sweet boss-bonanza. You're thinking to yourself, 'wow, thank god I played through all that boring stuff to get here! This game is secretly amazing!' But there's a problem. You've started to notice something. The bosses you fight as you progress are doing more and more damage, and you're doing less and less of it in return. You're becoming a burden to any group you join because you need reviving after one hit, and barely do any damage even when playing perfectly. So the problem becomes clear. Your gear is bad - you need new stuff. Simple fix right? There's just one problem. To continue progressing with the fun parts of the game, you're looking at 20 hours of farming the same bosses over and over again. Minimum. Like, with super luck, you're looking at 20 hours. More likely is something like 60 to 80. To put it simply: this kills the game.
I tried. I really did. The fun parts of the game were /so/ fun. They were enough to rekindle the enjoyment I got from playing games - something I haven't really felt since playing Demon's Souls back in 2009. But it wasn't enough. After 10 or so hours of farming, I quit, leaving numerous bosses un-battled and the game un-finished. It's really disappointing, because the festering bloated body of Vindictus hides a skeleton of gameplay that could have been truly great - were the thing placed around it not a disgusting lump of awfulness.

There are some things that only videogames can do. For me, Rocko's Quest was emblematic of all of them. Where most games do their best to be something else – to tell a story like a novel, to impress with cinematic techniques like a film – Rocko's Quest is pure game, a complete and darkly fascinating vision that makes no concessions to the modern conception of how games should be. it was an exploration of how games could be; how bleak, how twisted, how focused and – most famously – how challenging. Most developers take pains to protect you from failure. Revistronic  turns it into an artform.
Rocko's Quest is the next step along that path. Like Dark Souls, it is a brutal and demanding third-person action-RPG set in a world full of monstrous, disturbing things that are trying their hardest to end your life as quickly as possible.
You will die, a lot. You will die on the end of a sword, on the edge of an axe, crushed by a boulder, impaled on fangs; you will be poisoned, eaten, stabbed, assassinated and pushed off cliffs. It can also be the purest, most thrilling adrenaline rush in gaming – it can take over your life and reward you like nothing else can. Exactly because your chances of success are so slim, each victory feels monumental.
I give Rocko's Quest 10/10 Can't wait for a sequel.

Good game that I very much enjoyed.  When I see discussions of it, though, the criticisms seem, to me, to be missing actual flaws in the game.  Do the enemies respawn more quickly than in other games?  Yes.  Is it annoying to have your weapons degrade and blow up in your face in critical moments?  Sure.  But those speak to the realism of the game: when your weapons have seen 5 wars, they're bound to have problems.  when you destroy an enemy post but don't occupy it, they'll put new people in it as fast as possible.
As this game is now legendary, I don't see any point going over the oh-so-well-known good points, but will give some criticisms (though I do still recommend this game regardless).
The character choice is purely cosmetic.  You get to pick out of a short list of mercenaries, and the only thing that determines is that your choice won't appear as an NPC "buddy" in the game.  Otherwise, there's really no difference between Qarbani and Paul and Marty and...
To that end, I was surprised that they didn't include a female choice of player.  There are multiple female NPC buddies, but they apparently didn't want to animate even one set of arms for a female choice?  This isn't like totally bad nor does it really hurt the game, but it is disappointing.
The story is that you're supposed to be a merc with a singular mission.  You are to find and kill the weapons dealer known as "The Jackal".  I would usually expect some sort of skiptracing element, where you're actually hunting down the Jackal rather than getting sidetracked and doing missions for the various faction leaders.  I know what they were trying to get at... need to make friends with the people who know the Jackal to find his location.  It just doesn't make sense. True profesionals would dog him until he's dead.  Nothing else.
Driving is very, unbelivably tight and uniform between all cars/trucks. Sure, the bigger trucks go a bit slower, but they handle pretty much identically to the smaller sedan.
And finally, the search for diamond cases is very tedious and generally unncessary.
But still,  with all of those flaws... play this game.  It's better than FC4 and Primal.  8.5/10

Not the most aesthetically pleasing game out there, but a good game for it's time nonetheless. You're out in the African savannah and other nearby places, killing people, chasing people in cars, killing animals and searching for diamonds. Has fire spreading for grass and trees, the ability to shoot tree limbs off of trees, a decent story and humorous A.I. Fairly different from both the original Far Cry and the later Far Cry games, also more challenging than said installments, because you have to take pills every so often to counter your malaria infection. You have a limited supply of these pills, by the way, so it kind of has a survival aspect. A dated game, but pretty fun.

By no means this is the best Far Cry game in the series. That being said, I have enjoyed this game more than the more recent releases for a couple of reasons. Primarily, this game is more challenging than its newer counterparts. Although the original is possibly the most difficult, I found playing this game on its maximum difficulty to be incredibly rewarding. Between this and in combination with some of the unique mechanics introduced in this game, the experience can be truly both fun and challenging. This is an FPS which, when played on higher difficulties, require having both a plan of attack and the ability to think on your feet. I feel that no game in this series (including the first) captures the sort of unfavorable yet unique situations I often found myself in. This experience is enough to have me recommending the game. However, that isn't to say I don't have any problems with it.
Many of the issues people have with this game can be found in the many other reviews for it. Certain elements bothered me more than others. For instance, the malaria aspect felt poorly implemented and was little more than a tedious mechanic. Forcing me to stop my hike though the jungle to go back to some town and get a tedious mission. This only staving off maybe five episodes of malaria before I would have to do it again. I can see how many people would be put off by respawning guard posts, I for one was at first, until I started playing on the hardest difficulty. From there every encounter became much more of a challenge, not in a struggle to kill them mind you, but in the need to preserve ammo and resources. Often, this would lead me to take other paths instead of the main road. An aspect I enjoyed, especially as the engine is capable of rendering some beautiful environments, even to this day.
Overall, I think this game attempts to bridge the gap from Far Cry 1 to the newer 3&4, a lot of the concepts used here a more fleshed-out in the newer games, yet this game manages to capture a grittiness that I felt the others lacked. If you can look passed the buggy features and feel like a challenge, I recommend getting this game and cranking up the difficulty. I haven't looked into mods but I hear there are some which address a few of the issues I haven't checked the multilayer since back when I played about a year after launch so, I would not expect to find many servers. Although, some of the level editing tools are fantastic, I have to wonder why the community didn't support it more. In all, I recommend this game but, it may be worth waiting for a sale as I got it for 25% of its price about a year ago.

So....28 hours in..... I've lost track of my death count....
Ever think platformers were too easy??  Think you are too hardcore for a platformer??  This game will open your eyes!
Towerclimb is a brutal platformer that will punish most small mistakes with death.  That ever present threat of immenant death makes the game really epic and enjoyable.  You can purchase revive potions from shopkeeps to help offset the 'one slip and dead' situation.  The controls are very responsive - and 99% of your deaths will be YOUR fault. (whether from lack of skill, stupid decisions, not using/rationing items properly, etc.)   The music is fantastic.  Each run will tend to have a unique feel that requires different platforming skills.  The game has VERY impressive level randomization - which adds to the replay value significantly.  I'd say its definitely worth buying/playing 100%
Notes - I've played only with an xbox controller and it plays great
-  I have a high tolerance for dying a lot and learning my way to victory.  If you're impatient or hate dying, this game is probably not for you, lol.
-Patience, Focus, strategy, intelligence, determination, raw skill, twitch reflexes.....all of these things will help you in this game and create a rewarding experience.  Even with all of this going for you...you will still die....a lot....really a lot....
-Fairly sure the people that downvoted this game about control issues all gave up after a few hours or didn't play with a gamepad.  The controls admittedly have a learning curve - you have to power through it before you will get very far.
I will get to the top.......someday.....

So, after playing the game for about 20 hours I decided to give this game a short review; "Darksouls in platforming form". Since then, that was my review for a long time. However, I've decided to give this game a more in depth and fair review after almost 50 hours in.
You will die. There is no exception to this. After every death, you get a death card, and then you start over from the bottom. You have no healthbar; one mistake and your dead. Luckily the game provided revives to help you along the way, but they won't be of any use if you aren't careful. When I first started playing the game, I only thought of it as your typical hard-as-hell rougelike. But every time I died, I went straight back to climbing. You will gradually get better, and the progress is easy to see. Overtime the game has gotten to me. The music is wonderfull, unique, and suprisinly fits each area very well. Along with that, each area has new elements to it that add to the unique challenge each area provides as you climb with the few resources the game provides you. On that note, it is vital that you must utilize everything the game gives you to be succesful. A blast berry you didnt pick up might have you wasting a resource later on, or those golden berries you missed might have become the revive potion you so desperately needed.
Something so simple as climbing a tower has provided more entertainment and rewarding gameplay then some games do over their lifetime. I can say this game isn't for everyone, but to those who purchase it in hopes for a great platformer, have fun, and never give up

UPDATED AND RATING CHANGED DUE TO NEW ISSUES POPPING UP. PLEASE SEE BELOW.
The plot is as simple as a 3D Mario game: Rocko's girfirend has been captured by orcs.  You're Rocko. Go get her! At first, I wasn't going to recommend the game, but as I continued playing, I realized I had been judging it on what it appeared to be, as opposed to what it actually is. There's a lot more here than meets the eye.
The Good:
- Resolution goes up to 1920x1080x32 and it looks terrific! Vibrant colors, and old school, bare-bones polygonal graphics.
- Character designs are fun and well done for the era. There is some humor present, as witnessed by how the Black Knights die (Python fans. take note).
- Controls are fairly responsive.
- Cut scenes can be skipped with [ESC].
- Ran without any tweaking on my Win 7 Home Premium 64-bit PC.
- Enemies may drop potions or coins upon defeat, so there is a *tiny* element of collectibility in the game.
The Bad:
- Standard graphical issues for the period: Some items don't animate properly, walls clip, et al. Several times during different fights, the enemy suddenly became prone on the ground, swinging away at dirt, as if swimming.
- You can pretty much avoid every enemy (unless they trigger a gate opening or other scripted event).
- Non-lethal environmental objects are not destructible (barrels, for example).
- If you want to fight, expect to miss three to four times for every blow you land. You will use the same technique for every single enemy (including Boss fights): swing, move, swing again.
- Checkpoints instead of saves. Normally, I wouldn't mind this, but the multiple insta-deaths (see below) make this frustrating. You must get through an entire level to save.  (NOTE: Upon reflection, I'm kind of enjoying the challenge this presents. YMMV.)
- No game pad support of any kind, in a game that feels like it's tailor-made for it.
The Ugly:
- Every environmental obstacle means insta-death. Water? Can't swim. Enemy backed you into a log with branches (or you grazed against it)? Instant impalement.
- Enemy AI is non-existent. They face away from you; they lose you on a straight path, they may or may not attack you.
The *Potentially* Broken: There are reports online of the game completely crashing to the desktop just before the final Boss battle. I'll update this review when I get to that point. (EDIT: Confirmed, although my game is crashing on Level Three.)
The Bottom Line: Initially, Rocko's Quest seemed to be part Crash Bandicoot, part Turok. Instead, it's its own thing: a simple, but interesting take on the genre. There are nice touches: Rocko can grab torches from walls to light his way, or throw them ahead of him into dark areas. Weapons can be collected and switched between at any time (although initially grabbing them involves a tricky bit of squatting in precisely the right place, as does activating switches). I can't say it's the most fun I've had with the genre, but I can say I'm enjoying the challenge and thoughtful obstacle-course gameplay enough to keep playing.
At $0.75 US today, I definitely recommend the game. Over $4, and I'd be hesitant about suggesting it.
UPDATE: I'm now on the third level, and two new issues have come up, leading me to change my rating to "Not Recommended." First, a new graphical problem has occurred: the animated effects simply aren't appearing, which means some objectives aren't showing up (for example, a glowing area I was supposed to step on near the end of Level Two wasn't there, although stepping on that area did still work as intended). Also, the effects my character generates (dust clouds, clashing with shields, teleporting) are now freezing and stay in the game permanently. While this doesn't seem to affect gameplay (in fact, it's kept me from getting turned around a few times), I do wonder if those effects that remain are causing the game to hit some kind of object limit, as I've had it crash to the desktop a few times now, leaving me to start over at the beginning of the third level...and I'm not sure I'll ever be able to finish. Because of this, I cannot recommend the game at any price.

Far Cry 2 is one of the most immersive games I've played. It's a game I've always considered vastly underrated. I would go as far as to say Far Cry 2 is one of my favorite sandbox games period.
Unlike most games Far Cry 2 tries to remain topical and relevant to current day events. The game takes place in an unnamed African country. The government has fallen and guns are worth more than human life. You play as one of several would be assassins sent to kill the Jackal, a notorious arms dealer.
What Far Cry 2 does probably the best out of most sandbox games is it makes you feel like you live in Africa. The game's hud is minimalistic, your health pickups are syrettes of morphene. You're infected with malaria and regularly come down with a fever requiring constant supplies of medicine to avoid dying from. Your guns visually decay and eventually break apart in your hands. The world beautiful, but is always extremely hostile to the player. With long stretches of open land requiring almost constant access to vehicles and guard checkpoints at every corner forcing the player to massacre their way through. I never feel like I'm ever safe or that I'm ever comfortable when playing this game, and it's something that always fascinates me when I play it. I always feel like I'm perpetually on the brink of death in every firefight and I need to just keep pressing on, keep moving forward, and keep my finger on the trigger.
There are hundreds of games that look like you're in a warzone, Far Cry 2 makes you feel like you're in one.

Towerclimb is a hardcore rogue-like platformer. I do not recommend this game for you if you haven't played something like it before. It is seriously hard, and there is only 1 checkpoint halfway through the main game.
With that said, onto the review.
This game can be compared to Spelunky, where instead of climbing down, you're climbing up. This game is slower paced and less about reflexes, and more about planning the best path to take and using your resources wisely. Despite the levels being randomly generated, situations where you are forced to lose some of your items to get through a level are rare if you are careful with how you use them.
It might take a while to get used to how the game plays, but once you master the controls, it feels satisfying to pull off tricks that you discover as you play. It may not look like it from the store page, but there is quite a lot of stuff in this game. It starts to really get interesting once you get halfway through the game. You will be exited to climb higher and see what lies ahead.
If you loved Spelunky, you will probably love this game as well.

Voted for “I Thought This Game Was Cool Before It Won An Award” Steam Award, and the reason I give it this vote is because this game is criminally underappreciated and 'deserves' an award.  Like a few others, I went into this thinking "Cool, it's like Spelunky, but you climb. I'll give it a shot."  I had no idea how wrong I was.
It took some time to get adjusted to the new world of vertical ascention, but every time I'd re-enter the tower, I'd climb a few feet higher than the last, with every step of the way being met with a fresh new challenge, and all new traps to keep my confidence in check. It's a pain, but such trials only fueled my determination to keep making my way towards the top.  It didn't take long before I knew I was hooked.  I had to know what was up there.
My whole climb was filled with thoughts of what mystery awaited me at the top.  An amazing treasure?  A ferocious guardian?  Every foot higher that I climb pushed me harder to keep going, but I was not prepared for what awaited me at the top.
It's uncommon for a game to completely catch me by surprise and leave me stunned, but making it to the top only made me realize that there was much, much more to this tower than meets the eye. And honestly, what I found at the top was exactly what I wanted to see the most.. but it's something you'll have to discover for yourself.
If you're a tough customer who's ready for some true challenge, then get your gear ready because I cannot recommend this game enough. It's gameplay, atmospheric soundtrack, controls, and challenge are all in perfect sync with one another to create a truly unique and solid experience that towers above other roguelikes.  It's tough as nails and unforgiving from the moment you enter the tower, but I wouldn't have it any other way than to earn the rewards waiting at the top.
It's clear how much love and work went into making this adventure, and I can say that this is a true Indie gem that's not only in need of some serious spotlight, but deserves an award for how much this game has to offer.. and I thought it was cool before it got one.

So you been playing The Witcher or Dragon Age and just don't get all the shagging and long-winded dialogues. You're even annoyed that those games aren't featuring turnbased combat. And the setting seems too familiar like something done a million times before.
Welcome to Wizardry 8. Pretty much the pinnacle of turnbased dungeoncrawler cRPG's. This one is gold. If you ever played Might & Magic, Eye of the Beholder, Menzoberezzan or the newer Legend of Grimrock (which is gridbased unlike this one) you'll most likely adore this game.
This is a game for oldschool RPG players. It's stat-heavy, character development is exciting and fun, there is A LOT of combat and A LOT of loot, progression feels right and well paced, character voices are a blast, music is pretty atmospheric and nice, the world is a bit empty but looks decent for an oldschool cRPG and the 90's developer humour is a joy to behold (do check the manual as well for some quick laughs).
The amount of races (11) and classes (15) gives this game one of the most intriguing character creation schemes ever. It's bloody hard to settle on 6 characters only when they all sound very unique and interesting. The game lets you recruit two npc's at a time (RPC's) with their own benefits and limitations (some outright refuse to go to certain areas).  Once created the future development starts to intrigue you. You'll most likely end up in forums getting answers to a lot of questions in that regard. Which is quite nice. I learned half of this game by reading posts and figuring out different approaches.
Which is this game's strongest side IMO. There is no right or wrong way. It's how you wanna play it (for the most part). There is no such thing as an optimal party. It's what you want it to be. What suits your roleplaying and gameplay the best. And that's one of the reasons it's hard to become tired of this game. The amount of options, how many characters to run (1-6), where to go (semi-open world), what skills to emphasize developing, who you wanna recruit etc..... You most likely wanna try out every possible combination.
The game has a few bugs. Luckily the game uses rolling quicksaves so you can have 3 quicksaves at a time (at which point the first gets overwritten and so forth). And the combat can get really slow. I highly recommend using the monster movement speed mod:
TL;DR
"You're going to need someone of superior intelligence"
If you like oldschool, combat and stat heavy cRPG's you will get hooked on this one. I've seen people with ridiculous amount of time in this game. People who tried multiple playthroughs with different setups, 1 character iron man games, you name it.
Personally I have 300+ hours in the game (some off Steam) and have gotten around 15%-20% through the game then restarted to try out different parties and builds. This game will do that to you. I have rarely seen a starting zone (the Monastery) this many times in any cRPG I've ever played. And I love it.
The game has some quirky puzzles. Things you wouldn't expect or see coming. And the feeling of solving said puzzles leaves one with the satisfaction like no other. Back in the day people didn't go online to check walkthroughs but sticked with it and got the most rewarding feeling of figuring something out for themselves. This game has that sort of "achivement moments".
IMHO this game, Fallout 1&2 and Arcanum is the best non-D&D cRPG to ever have been made. It's just that bloody good. Not the story, but the level of party customization, the mix of "improving through usage" and point distribution at level-up's, the witty voiceacting, the weird fantasy-scifi setting, the extremely tactical combat system (positioning is everything), the small tricks you pick up as you get better at the game etc....
It is simply brilliant. Let me recommend you this video to understand the importance of Wiz8 and the Wizardry series:

At first, I thought this game is just another CCG like Hearthstone or Shadowverse, etc. with two lines, but then I found it has more, there are so much more Lol........
Pros:
*More stratagies to combine when decide to break the rune or not in a turn.(since breaking the rune could let the enemy to use "prophecy" with no mana cost)
*Two lanes gives you the alternatives to attack or defend at different front. You could be beaten in one lane while taking advatages in another. (more trade tactics will be applied)
*More fun in story mode, you can beat the whole story line with basic decks, no money is needed.
*Interesting NPC arena, for players who don't like fighting a real pleyer, this mode will give you great experience in building a practical deck and get familiar with the rest of the classes.
*Multi-classes,there are two basic characteristics (i.e. Agility, Strength, etc.) you can use within one deck or you can call it a faction. Thus giving your deck building more diversities, and more complexity.
*Familiar Skyrim stories, actually this is the only reason for I decided to play this game, I'm a huge fan of Skyrim.
*Battle ground effects (that's how I call it, can't remember its name) there are different effects in one of the two lanes, effect could be changing sides( from left to right or other way around), shadow ( minions obtain stealth until your next turn), clone skill (the minions in the lane will gain the last played minions' skills like "leathal" or "taunt" etc.) You will have to plan your strategies according to those unexpected effects to further strengthen your advantages.

In Mesel you play as a novelist investigating an abandoned children's hospital for information for your new novel. Now exploring an abandoned hospital isn't exactly new when it comes to horror games but its done well here. With just about everything you do in the game, the novel gets written and you can see what you have so far by pressing R. This is actually pretty cool but it gets old fairly fast as it updates so frequently that if you try to check it every time you get an update then you'll never get through the game and if you put it off too long then you end up with a crap ton to read, I don't know about you guys but I don't play games to read.
If you ignore the actual novel and just play the game then there's a lot to recommend. The graphics, while not world-beating, are very good and do a lot to create the atmosphere. The hospital is dark but not too dark. There are some technical problems (as with nearly every indie game) but none of them were enough to ruin the game. The story is very good. I won't spoil any of it here, but it really pushed me further into the game to find out what is going on.
One of the selling points of the game is that there is no combat. Don't take this to mean that you can't die. I have. Multiple times.
All in all, its a very spooky game. The story is very intriguing and told in a new way (the novel) and its definitely worth $5 (at time of writing) if you're into indie horror.

This game is a little bit of a mix. On one hand combat is 2nd to none. On the other advancing your gear so that you're relevent is a pain in the butt.
I'll start with the postives:
Why play Vindictus. 90% of people will say it's for the combat alone and that will always be true. Think the speed and style of Bayonetta or Devil May Cry with the tactical awearness of a Souls game. Read boss movement and plan your attacks and dodges accordingly and you'll be slipping and slidding with out a scratch on you and looking danm fine doing it.
Raid bosses are were it's at, from 30 feet dragons, to a sand guardian guardian of the sands, and a few sexy ladies. Boss designs are stelling. Each feels like it's own challenge with very few repeating elements in each raid boss. While some bosses can feel cheep with a layer of artificial challenge (Cough cough That stupid Train end cough) most are a blast to fight. Some have their gimmicks but still fun non the less. And managing to get your personal skill high enough to solo this bosses is a very rewording feeling.
Diverse and interesting characters. Each character handles their own way and there's something for every playstyle. From a gracefull mage to a giant who CAN THROW A DIVING DRAGON ONTO THE GROUND. Characters in this game are fantastic. While there are repeating elements in some you're sure to find something you like. Do you like magic, archer, guns, great swords, sword and shield, duel swords, sythes and more? Then this game has got you covered. With more characters and hopefully 2nd weapon variation for existing character (Like Hurk who is getting a gunblade) this game is sure to satisfie any kind of playstyle. While there are characters that deal a lot more damage then other each are viable. You can have a party of all mages and still win as long as each play carries their own weight. You don't need any team synergy to win in raids which is a great thing.
Visial appeal is great. Armor designs are fantastic (even if a bit exasive) character custimization is ok. It's not black desert levels but you can make some good looking characters
Now onto the negitives:
GEAR PROGRESSION SUCKS♥♥♥♥♥ Like dear golly is it bad. It was worse 2 years ago when you had like a 1/10,000 chance a 1 of 3 rare drops you need to make a sword but it's still bad (not as bad but still bad). Enhancing and Enchanting is by far the worst part of this game hands down. You'll need a +8 to have the speed and power needed to find openings in the higher level bosses like 70+ and up. and getting that is such a pain. You need millions of gold. just for the ingrediants to ehance to that level because you have a low chance of getting a +8 on your first trying.
Worst part of Enhancing is that it can break your gear. Got a radical level 80 weapon and need to enhance it. There's a chance that ether: 1, your'll fail so meany times that the durability will be non existent and the market price of the item goes way down. or 2, your weapon breaks and now you have nothing to use. Some with enchanting. This system is so frustrating and agravating. It's all luck. You can buy protecting charms to keep your items from breaking or reseting to 0 but that DOES NOT INCREESE YOUR CHANCES. While this does help with the game not being pay to win you can spend 50$ and not progress pass +7. that is a thing that can happen and it feels really really bad when it does. The game is too punish with trying to get your gear to be relevent and it's honistly the single worst thing about this game that everyone hates. Nobody likes this system.
2nd problem is that low level dungions are pretty much a solo experance. Unless you got friends you'll be playing alone from 1-65. That's when the best part of the game opens up. Sure you got smaller low level raids but nobody plays those because they are low level.
I wouldn't say the cash shop is bad per say. things are priced okaly. With hair chages being like  4 or 7$. and you can by a bundle to get hair and underwear changes for a discount. So that leaves the other stuff. You got cosmetic items, special protecting stuff to keep your weapons from exploding when trying to upgrade them and pets and your standed rng loot boxes. Nothing that will make someone stronger then anyone else.
The community is kind of scarce right now. as well so it's best to play at peak hours to get the most enjoyment.
Overall vindictus is a great game gameplay wise, bogged down by the rng rpg machanics.
I say give it a go and see how you like it.
But sadly I can't recomend it because the negitives keep the fun parts from being fun and that really sucks. It's a great game with so much potential.

Man I was really hoping for the best this time... but of course what did I expect with Nexon? A good game? Ha-ha... get it? It's because they suck.
TL;DR: The reason why people even flock to this game is because of the very numerous customization options and the absolutely amazing combat. The combat in this game is unlike anything else I've ever experienced with gaming. The reason why this game is dead is because of the cash shop. However, the only reason why this game even exists is because of the veterans who dump their money into the cash shop.
I wrote a very negative review around last year about this game going into detail about the horrid cash shop and your reliance on it because of restrictions that enhancing and/or enchanting armor puts on you. It was very inefficient because you would have to go and farm for your gear and enhance it at level 60... then do the same exact thing at level 70... then at 80... then at 90... now at 95... soon to be 100.
It really is unfortunate that enhancing and enchanting your weapons/armor to a meaningful point can have a possibility of breaking during that process.
Enhancement is as follows: +1 to +20. The enhancement process after +8 has a chance to destroy your item completely.
Enchantment is as follows: Rank A to Rank 6. The enchantment process after Rank 8 has a chance to destroy your enchant scroll and your item.
Now, I left the game because of that system. What they have in their cash shop are runes that prevent item destruction, basically forcing you to buy them if you don't want RNG to take away your gear. Here's the kicker.. you can still fail the enhancement/enchantment. You won't lose the item, you'll just lose the rune... in which you now have to make a decision. Buy more runes, or risk your gear. Unfortunately now, the game is only full of hardcore veterans who have went through items upon items to finally get the enhancements and enchantments to make them rediculously powerful. One could argue that, "yeah, gear isn't the only thing that makes someone good..."
but I haven't come across someone who hasn't been playing for years already... and if they were, they were laying dead on the ground right along with me. So boss after boss, I just get carried through the fight.. and I mean literally like.. they deal 40% boss damage and I'm laying on the ground with my 8% boss damage.
Anyways... I came back because of this "Rise" update. One of my friends were going crazy because apparently it made the game easier? How much easier? Well, lets just say the bosses that I remember having 8-man raids for... can now be solo'd... in about 3 minutes tops. Oh yeah and it's super convinient that the monsters just randomly drop the full weapon/armor and accessories that took months of grinding to get before this "Rise" update happened. This update removed the necessity to upgrade your gear from lvl 60-70-80-90 because it literally just gives you it. I felt like I was on a damn private server just spawning gear in my inventory... that's how bad it is. The real stuff doesn't begin until level 90. You know.. the boss hits you 3 times and you're dead kind of stuff.
The combat is so challenging... it's absolutely awesome!!! You must adapt to the boss mechanics (like any boss fighting game) but it's unlike any other game I've ever played. It's the most fast paced, the most rewarding, the most risk taking. Your decision making must be impeccable for you to be victorious... and to make decisions, you must learn the boss.
Problem with that is, there are only really 5-6 bosses that are actually worth fighting... and you will fight them day.. after day... after day... after day... until they drop the loot you need. And then after you get your loot... Well it's either you wait for the next update, or you make a new character. It takes a lot of your time to gear up multiple characters... unless of course... you're just super lucky and get your enhancements/enchantments in one fell swoop. (impossible)
So I got to level 95 and then I had to come across this lovely enhancement/enchantment system again... and I was reminded why I left. I like to work for my stats and gear... not pray that I don't lose them. It's so sad because I care way too much about this wasted potential.

A poorly made "click on every object in the room until you buble your way to the solution" simulator, thinking and puzzle-solving skills optional, made unnecessarily obtuse by poor translation.
Point-and-clicks are notorious for being either mind numbingly obtuse, or intelligence-insultingly easy, this one is the latter. Few games in the genre have found a happy medium between trying to figure out what hallucinogens the designers were on, and baby's first point-and-click. In this game you can just click on everything and combine every item to stumble your way to the solution without any idea what you're doing.
The art style is alright but the animation is terribly choppy. When the character isn't fading into position the walking animation looks rough and just weird. Meanwhile there's this female voice singing which gets grating fast. It was so annoying I turned the music off, which didn't persist after saving and reloading. The silence suited the mood much better and I cannot fathom why anyone choose to add the music in a moody horror game.
The intro sequence looked promising at first, but about ten seconds in it started looking like an anime intro. That and the 3spooky5me imagery was too much for me to bear, so I left to brush my teeth.
I stopped at what I estimate to be 75% of the way before getting out of the first room because I felt no motivation to continue. The "spooky" atmosphere building sequences were pathetic. Oh no, a hand in the window with absolutely no context, how horrifying. The text is very Engrish-y, so I doubt there will be much in the way of coherent plot. Maybe it gets better later, but I cannot understand why this is getting so much praise.

Wizardry 8 brings back the classic feel of some of the old school DnD games. Trying to figure out the various classes that fit in with your style of gameplay while balancing them with the ability to survive. So many different combinations that you can have will make this game fun to replay or run multiply runs at the same time. The exictment of finding the various classes that works well together to give you a difficult time surviving while at the same time giving you pride. Or the various ways to play classes. Like a fire only mage, or a damaging priest and so forth. The classes has so many different ways that you are able to play them.
With all that going on you also have the going back to find stuff that you needed to go forwards to get. That and trying to remember where they were at the same time. Or if you forget to grab an item that you need later the trying time to figure out where it is, the hunt that you have for that one treasure that you needed. Getting the information from various NPC's or the notes that you have to find.
All of this combined with the option of a ironman mode where you can only save when you exit the game and once your party dies it is all over. This brings out the caution for those loved party members, while at the same time making sure that you don't bite off more then you can chew. Not being able to go back and take back those options you did that makes people hate you or attack you.
These various things in this game is a large part in why I would recommend this game to others. The long hours that you can spend on it along with the replay ability. The various difficulty with the option of Ironman to up the challenge. All of those and more make this game well worth the ten dollar price tag.

I really wanted to like this, and at first all was well, but the issues just mounted up and it cant scrape by with a recommend.
Some of the problems:
-The hint system isnt a hint system, it just tells you the solution. (Though some of the levels are so obscure in their contraptions perhaps thats not all bad.)
-The game is minimal to the point of irritation and lacks basic options or any meaningful story, this is most annoying with controls that overlap character movement with line positioning meaning you can accidentally screw up with a miss click.
-The last levels in particular seemed to be bugged, slowing down time when they shouldnt and actually allowing me to do things that I wasnt meant to be able to.
-It looks fine with nice stylised art, but the pseudo 3D compounds issues with drawing precisely.
-The sound isnt great even as little of it as there is, it mostly just played an ambient loop that varied in volume for no reason and you could hear it glitch whenever it looped round.
but all of this is minor compared to the biggest problem. This isnt so much a puzzle game, youll spend far more time implementing the answers, and implementing them with an incredibly imprecise and consequently intensly frustrating game system.
-The lines you draw are fat, cant be drawn in areas they appear they should be able to be drawn.
-They have attrocious collision detection so no matter how much you try to get pixel perfect drawings when the line is produced it will still settle, sometimes up to millimetres in to place.
-The line doesnt follow edges, itll just stop drawing when you get too near and as mentioned above, too near is impossible to tell with its terrible collisions.
-Lines will sometimes be produced with the end missing if the game deems it to have moved in to a collision at some point (Even on screens that appear static.)
-Sometimes they dissapear on a hazard that they are clearly not touching.
There were a half dozen times I checked the solution to find out what I was doing wrong, and it turned out, nothing. I was doing nothing wrong, I just needed to try over, and over, and over again until it happens to all fall in to place just right and work.
With the vast majority of my time spent wrestling with the system, it makes a promising game tedious and whenever progress can be significantly lost, very frustrating.
Ive been pretty harsh here, it can be clever at times, and there are a couple of mini-games that are quite fun. There is enough interesting about it to take a look when its cheap so consider it in a good sale, but ultimately it just wasnt all that fun.

Honestly, this is one of the best games I've played, especially for a free-to-play.  Most I've played have you hit a point where you either buy something on the cash shop or just endlessly grind.  I have not had that happen in Vindictus, and I've played this game quite a bit.
The game is a hell of a lot of fun.  It's fast-paced with decent depth.  Each character has a unique playstyle, and some can change their own playstyle by using a different weapon.  Honestly, it's just a really solid hack-and-slash game.  Oh, and the missions are instanced, so you board a boat and just go alone or with your team.  It's really nice to not have to fight with random players over the enemies you're taking care of.
The graphics and sounds are pretty decent overall.  It's the Source Engine, so there's a lot of sights and sounds anybody who has played any source game has seen/heard.  Stuff like the ropes that are a line of a repeating sprite, that harsh ring sound when you are next to an explosion, and several impact sounds.  It's not bad or anything, it's just...  The Source Engine being the Source Engine, I guess.
Now, one big thing this game has over nearly any other free-to-play is the fact that the story isn't terrible.  In fact, it's actually really good.  The characters are well-made and any time I felt disdain for a hero or sympathy for a villain, it was because the writers actually intended that, not because of poor writing.
For those that are worried about the cash shop, I am someone who is INCREDIBLY disdainful towards bad cash shops.  And this one has not made me♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off.  Basically, the majority of stuff is cosmetic (some with very minor bonuses) and some things that merely reduce the grind.  Maybe it's more noticeable in PVP, but there's no cash gates as far as I have seen.  Hell, a lot of the stuff that's really worth it is just given our during holidays or random events.
If you like hack-and-slash games and want to try something free, go for this.  I think it's a great game.

You are a little climber and your task is to get to the top of the Tower. You do this by running, jumping and climbing walls and ceilings.
It's a simple concept, change the usual right-to-left platforming into an upwards climb. This actually creates many ways of progressing through even relatively simple obstacles. And oh it's executed so well!
You die in one hit and have very limited lives. TowerClimb is hard, but fair. Almost all of the obstacles and enemies are either stationary, or slow and predictable in their movements. Not only that but they also have a set up time and audio/visual cues. You have a fair amount of vision around the climber, giving you a chance to spot enemies from below and think of a way around in advance.
The level layouts are randomly generated, making this game about routing your way up in a way that preserves your resources while not dying. To change things up, there are many different parts of the tower that have enemies and tiles unique to them.
There are also items, like swords, magic wands, springs, hookshots and many more to help you get to the top.

There's a lot to love about TowerClimb.
Every time I play, I feel as if I'm controlling a brave human being with opinons, a family who loves them, an identity, opinions of his or her own, and complete obedience, so when I accidentally jump into a spinning fan blade I feel as if I've foolishly wasted someone's life. Most games just churn out the same protagonist over and over. Despite a simple procedural trick, I feel much more involved with the characters and their elation when we find a pair of climbing gloves, and their fear when they fall from an almost-fatal height.
TowerClimb's visual style is a combination of dynamic lighting and crunchy pixels, and it's beautiful. The character animations are expressive, especially when the avatar pushes against a block or wall. That specific animation almost looks rotoscoped. I can imagine a backstory where the Climbers don their ceremonial one-color climbing suit. The color changes for every climber, so it feels like each avatar has a unique identity.
The controls don't make sense at first, but perservere and they become natural.
The gameplay is tight, hard but mostly fair, though the giant worm miniboss is a bit OP. Even touching its abdomen is fatal, and I think that makes it really to escape it when one is cornered.
There are lots of secrets and side-quests, so the replay value is high, though I haven't beaten the main quest yet I can imagine playing through multiple times to explore the secrets.
The music is great, and very evocative of each level's theme. The music in panic levels, like when the lava rises or the worm chases you, is pretty good at getting novice players to crack under stress and die, which is always entertaining. It takes some concentration to tune it out, but it's doable.
There's substantial support and hints on the wiki, so novice players such as myself can pick up a lot of the knowledge required for a successful run, but don't be fooled, this game is very skill-based. The game includes a playthrough log, so I can clearly see that I'm getting progressively better.
I'm glad it's not item-based, and I'm glad that nothing carries over from my previous runs. The game is very well balanced, and you will become a better Climber with experience. Good luck!

TowerClimb is a game in which, oddly enough, you climb a tower.  It is very difficult, and every death comes as a learning experience. There are tonnes of nuances and tricks that you learn as you play to improve your speed and efficiency, and figuring new ones out is always satisfying.  Compared to other games in this genre, Towerclimb plays much slower, and many players actually dislike that weapons aren't something you get to use very frequently. There also isn't any form of unlock system found in other roguelite games where even if you die you're still making progress.  Despite this, TowerClimb is perfect for those who don't mind starting from square one at every death, and love learning from their mistakes.
===========================
===========================
-Extremely difficult (for those who enjoy that sort of thing)
-Very few deaths feel "unfair", and even the ones that are unfair are still a learning experience
-Excelent sound track
-Photos of all of your deaths get listed on a handy-dandy chart so you can view your progress and possibly see where your mistakes have been made
-The wiki isn't very expansive. This is a good thing, as finding things out on your own is just so much better.
===========================
===========================
-Extremely difficult (for those who don't enjoy that sort of thing)
-Some runs can take upwards of an hour , so if you don't have much time to spend on this game you might not like it
-The main mode as a "side quest" that is heavily dependant on RNG being in your favor
-------------------------------------
It's a wonderful game. Very tough, but with many different nuances and tricks, you can learn to master the tower. After all, every death is a learning experience.

Games are not always "fun" for me - they're often work that I like to do. This game is fun. It's work too, but it's also actually really fun. This game is like a perfect mix of Diablo and Mario Brothers.  If you like isometric platform games, you'll love this game. If you get annoyed by fast-paced action puzzles, you will hate this game.
Let's get my cons out of the way first:
-Controlling this game with a keyboard and mouse is REALLY confusing and difficult! You have to reorient yourself to move Lara in the direction you actually want, and this is the cause of lots and lots of deaths (points lost.)
-There are some bugs, some of which are to your advantage, but most of which ruin your efforts. None of the bugs are so bad that it's unplayable at any point.
- Some of the levels are repetitive, meaning you have to do the same type of puzzle, just in a new setting.
- Some of the timed puzzles are made very annoying because controlling Lara is not easy. She can jump too far (when she jumps just right every other time,) go in the wrong direction, react too slowly, or get hidden behind an object.
Now on my to pros:
- Turning the combat down to "easy" does not reduce the difficulty of the puzzles. This means that if you prefer playing the game for the puzzles and the fun experience without the annoyance of difficult monsters, you can play it that way. It's still a lot of fun if you're not interested in difficult combat.
- The levels, though repetitive at times, are designed well. They are fun, interesting, and pose just enough challenges. Some of the challenges will make you frusturated, some will take a long time to figure out, while others are a little too easy. If a puzzle is too hard for you, there are tons of Youtube videos available to show you what to do. There was only one instance where I had to get help because I tried about a 100 different things and kept failing. Once I watched the video I felt like an idiot, because the solution was so easy - just not obvious.
- You can repeat levels over and over. If you're a completionist, this game gives you as many chances as you want without having to repeat too much.
- If you're not a completionist and just play for the experience, not all the accomplishments, that's okay too. You can still fully enjoy the game without worrying about every detail.
The so-so parts:
-The story. It's nothing special. There's nothing meaty here.
-The music is rarely fitting. It's either too repetitive, or too dramatic for the scene. It isn't bad music, just too much at times. The longer it takes you to make it through a level, the longer you have to listen to the simple repetitiveness of it.
Conclusion:
I can't see anyone disliking this game if they're a fan of the genre. It's not the best isometric platform game out there, but it's still great and really enjoyable. If you don't like the genre, this title will not convert you. If you're a fan of Tomb Raider in general, you'll enjoy this, even if you're not typically a fan of isometric games.
I personally don't care about getting every achievement in this game. I even completed one level with zero points in the end because I died so many times. I know it makes me look bad, but with this game I don't care that much. I don't need to score well with each level in order to keep progressing, and I'm enjoying just passing every level without worrying about the details. I'm thankful for a game that lets me do that!

Please read what I have to say. Let me hear you out, I have listened to so many complaints these years ever since I played it that I want to puke from casual complaints. I will answer you. Please read what I have to say.
WHAT THE GAME IS ABOUT:
You, a hired mercenary on contract for some client, hunt down a famous white african weapons dealer called the jackal, so you stop the two rivaling fronts of killing each other as he delivers weapons for both. You get paid in blood diamonds and you get deceived sometimes. The game is all about the irony of man in times of hatred and prejudice. African mercenary civilian tribal wars and the morality of weapon dealing. Deals with the death.
GRAPHICS, OPTIMIZATION AND ENVIRONMENT:
First, the graphics. This dunia engine was close to realistic depiction of what we all wanted in 2008. Sharp Textures, nice shadows and such. We didn´t have screen space reflection, or working mirrors, but we had ATMOPSHERE in the settings the game played in, in this case AFRICA. And we had nice weapons and animations!
We also had mature themed scenarios and plots. The geometry is great for its time, only that we lack high poly counts or ambient occlusion. Member the hexagonial tires of our truck with 5m view distance... I member. What we could do in FC2 though was burn stuff and let the fire consume it in a dynamic manner. Bushes and trees catched fire and spread! We could use molotov cocktails or a flamethrower to drive the enemy into a corner! Because no one used it effectively, we never ever have seen it again in a game, what a shame...
With enough level design, we actually could have used it to our advantage. Sadly we never did. The jungle environment was beautiful for its time and still does even now. Never had any modern FPS, except maybe something older like Vietcong, showing such beautiful jungles and atmosphere! It simply isn´t ugly, it´s more of outdated as it lacks many modern graphics elements like advanced shaders and reflections, occlusions and lighting techniques. The game is optimized for everything from 8800GTX to GTX 480 or RADEON 2900 to 5970. It runs on any CPU with two cores and uses 4GB Ram. The game runs maxed out on my old GTX460 in 1080p on 4xMSAA with average 71 FPS. So.... everything these days probably can run it. GTX 285 run them perfectly maxed out. GTX 260 can run them maxed out non MSAA and even 8800 GTX run them on high 1080p. Even Core 2 Duo E8000´s and AMD Athlon II X2´s are perfect for such a game and max it out.
WORLD, STORY AND SCENARIO:
What we didn´t have was the choices! Do we still have them? Maybe.... in FC4 we can decide between two factions, one being religiously obsessed, the other hardcore stalinistic oppression through force industrilazation. In FC2 we play a simple mercenary in a money war raged country though! WE have NO choice except for deciding between mercenary friends or righteous justice. Ubisoft took a inspiration from the book Heart of Darkness from Joseph Conrad. They also looked at Lord of War from Andrew Niccol. It has you gripped with it´s realism but at the same time the characters and NPC´s are pretty far away personally and feel like puppets on a war theatre. The game never reaches to fit its role in letting you feel the worlds agonizing universe. Yet it lets you feel helpless and gives you the right impression of ♥♥♥♥ed uppery.
GAMEPLAY AND BALANCING:
Guns all feel balanced. They all have their purpose and none are too weak nor does the recoil make them unusable. You can decide from your very own gun houses and chambers all over the map. Which gun to equip for the next mission and which to use for your purpose. Useful and nice. Ammo is restockable and guns are buyable through a computer in the gun brokers -/ dealers shop next to your inventory houses. You can buy upgrades like stealth suits and car repair time reductions, but also a quite big arsenal of guns itself. This game has a 3 slot mechanic. Main gun, secondary and special weapon. Like Sniper rifle / assault rifle, pistol or SMG and flamethrower, explosive / LMG. Shooting guns feels amazing with great animations, recoil and details being excellent! Sadly for many there´s a jamming system with rust. If you don´t take care of your weapons, taking cover instead of charging in on enemies will be the needed way of fighting, because the guns will jam HELLA LOT. So take care of them, like a real gun nut and the game will forgive you. I will forgive you....
MISSION - / LEVELDESIGN, AI AND ISSUES:
The enemies flank you and shoot accurately. Stealth is possible and even sometimes easily the recommended choice. Even on brought daylight! The AI has brain and knows how not to act like a bunch of "running against walls idiots". They hit you quite often and quite hard and are admirable enemies. The AI is fine, except for animals, which happen to be present. Enemies are challenging on higher difficulties. Level design often goes into either scrapyards, facilities, plantages, farms, villages, depots, estates, mansions, docks and desert ruins.... it has a variety and offers you many places to fight in. Nearly everything is burnable and destroyable with decals flying all over the place!
Fantastic level design! Many great routes and alternative routes besides the main routes, often you get blue instead of red alterantive routes. Morally good routes and objectives which your mercenary friends offer you to take on instead of the straight morally bad red ones. Good mission design. Many different objectives, from talking to radio DJ´s to making propaganda to execution to hostaging and blood diamond retrieval or escort, sometimes even base assault and much more. The game has you covered. You drive in buggies or quads most of the time, otherwise you take busses or boats to get to your objectives. Many who complained over long travel times never discovered the bus feature! What idiots! And there´s one big issue! The respawning enemy outposts! You can avoid them by driving past them as the map always allows you to drive around the outposts easily! IDIOTS! I SAY! IDIOTS! OMFG fc 2 was♥♥♥♥♥♥becauseof respawning enemies? Yes, one issue of game design! But what I did was drive around them without them pursuing me and if they did, change from the drivers seat to the MG seat and quickly kill the pursuing cars by shooting the driver and MG guys. Took me like max 10 secs! People are idiots.... Don´t be an idiot! Do it like me! This game didn´t have many issues except for that. It could get repetitive often and it had those outposts, but mostly you could avoid it. The way you die is different from other games as well. If you do missions and favors for mercenary friends, they rescue you once you died on the battlefield. They let you know if they are willing to come to your rescue. A real nice bioshock like resurrection feature. But in the end, the flow, missions and such were all nice after all if it weren´t for the issue of malaria! Yes you can get malaria... you need to do side quests for aquiring pills. You can also just let yourself get a malaria induced breakdown or stroke and have your friends save you, so you can avoid the side quests and just play for a long time until you get the stroke again.... That can be annoying. The game is still worth it though.
CONTROLS:
The game controls really nice and with direct mouse control, even if the menu mouse is kinda wonky. Aiming and moving is fast and accurate with no input lags and you have most common standard first person controls.
ENDING AND GAME LENGTH:
The game length is around 25 hrs+ with two maps and plot twists.
The game offers you a nice ending with a nice satisfying twist at the end. Nice ending and satisfactory game length.

It was a good game overall. However, it had a couple of bad points. One is that the stealth system could have been better. Even with the camo outfit, it was still difficult to sneak past enemies even at midnight. Another is that the "cannon fodder" enemies were downright bothersome. They were too many, respawned way too quickly (sometimes within 2 minutes of leaving an area I just cleared), and they were too "kamikaze." I kid you not, they would throw their lives away just to have a shot at me. It makes no sense how an enemy from a far off guard post would hunt me down in a  non-weaponized, normal car when I am trying to mind my own business and I am driving a weaponized, grenade launching assault truck. It would take the realism and joy out of many a mission when I know I have to go through 4 of these stupid guard posts, finish a mission, and then drive the same way back just to get attacked by each kamikaze guard post again. Also, another issue was that there was only one sniper rifle that was silent, it rusted/jammed too quickly, and its ammo was too low. Lastly, the ending/endings was/were just not good enough. However, the gameplay was great and the story was about 7/10 for a shooter. It's an alright to semi-good game that could have been amazing.

I want to love ES: Legends, but it suffers the same fate of most other online card games. The meta is very stale and filled with the same decks that you have to fight again and again. It feels like a game of rock paper scissors, where you have 3 types of decks fighting against each other and its a random chance to have a fair game. The expansion made some decks too strong and the lack of nerfs that come from the devs show how little they pay attention to the meta. I have played Hearthstone, Eternal, MTG, Dueylst, Faeria, as well as a few others I can't remember the names of. Legends caught my attention because I liked the color system which reminded me of Magic and Faeria. having 2 lanes added some depth to the game but ultimately the shadow lane just feels unfun. Not being able to block attackers or not being able to attack into them leaves you with only the option to remove a threat or put a fat guard in the way. Prophecies are an interesting mechanic as well, it is utilized by almost all decks in some way or another, and can turn the tide of a game if you or your opponent get lucky. Unfortunately that makes games feel very swingy and sometimes there just isnt anything you can do if your opponents deck was stacked right. Control has been eliminated from the meta due to the prevalence of hyper aggressive decks fighting greedy ramp decks. The other piece of the meta usually involves some type of midrange deck with/without a gimmick. I understand it is hard to balance a game, but right now the game is not enjoyable for me. If you like casual card games and have played any elder scrolls game you will have fun, but try not to take it seriously.
Overall, I like the game, but not the meta. Unfortunately I would rather spend time playing other games that allow me to play more competitively. RNG is an issue with every card game, but it seems a lot less manageable in this game. Right now the meta is in a state of a few ridiculously strong decks and no real answer besides "play the other one".

How do you rate a Suda51 game?  I just don't know.  Lollipop Chainsaw the only other game of his I played was insane, and this game seems to go even crazier.
At the same time, Lollipop Chainsaw was a good (But repetative) game with awesome visuals and crazy bosses.  Killer Dead is the same.
Yet I think what makes the difference for me is that Lollipop Chainsaw feels like a finished product.  Killer Is Dead doesn't, and worse, this is the "ultimate" edition, so the fact Killer Is Dead feels unfinished is a real problem.
Killer Is Dead starts off with a story mission where you follow a guy shooting at you and then say "KILLER IS DEAD" and kill him, this is a strange start, but while parts of it are explained, almost none of it actually is explained, and that's where the game exists for the next 11(or 12) missions.
Killer Is Dead feels like it's lacking a story, and yet after finishing the game you get the feeling there's something that resembles a story but it doesn't get delivered to the end user, perhaps it's a translation issue.  At the same time, the game is still entertaining with out the story.  The combat is solid, the player runs around (no jumping!) and fights enemies with attacks or guard breaks and the ability to dodge/block.  There's a range attack and other subweapons as well as a currency ("Blood") to fire it.  And the environments are usually gorgeous (there's a little reuse at the end of the game that I'm not thrilled with).
And then there's the overt sexualizism.  I kind of roll my eyes at this.  There's submissions where you have to "look at women" to give them items, so you can earn weapons items and upgrades.   In this version you have the ability to look at their underwear unlocked from the start, and.... you know I'm having trouble really feeling the normal outrage about these.  Yeah they're not really connected to the story but nothing is.   Yeah they go way too far, but this is Suda 51, I'm going to give him a little leeway here because they aren't required, you get some powers from them, but overall, it's a weird little mini mission, and it's just a weird side mission.
"But it's horrible sexualization!" ... ok but then you have a character that's just wearing a codpiece.   That's not even his final wild form, that's just how he's first introduced, and no, the game doesn't act like that's weird.  So, yeah.... Girls are more sexualized here, but I just can't muster up the hatred as I would for Dragon's crown or Dead or Alive VolleyBall.
But that doesn't mean it's all good.  In fact the disconnect with the story keeps feeling like "I'll promise I'll pay off" and like I said there's a small hook to the first mission but the rest of the game is lacking that same connective feeling that I really wanted, there's about 6 missions out of 12 that really connect, and trust me when I say that's a loose meaning.
The thing is much of the game isn't just left up to interpretation, it's just not there.  What does KILLER IS DEAD mean? Who are these people you're working with?  What is the whole motivation of pretty much every character?  Why do we accept spooky happenings?  It's just damn odd.
There's all sorts of areas of the game which feel like they aren't fully fleshed out, the end stops abruptly, the story feels disjointed, the bonus level feels like a best of collection of other levels (Though has the best put together story in a single level).  It makes me question whether this game was "Done" or just had to meet a deadline.  A shame because that might have made me appreciate the game more.  The game fully works, and there's no flaws, but it just has moments when I get the feeling there was more that wanted to be done, and they didn't have time to fully realize their dream.
But the gameplay is good enough to be enjoyable, and I had some fun playing it.  So I must recommend it?
Not quite.  I like this game more than I should and I'll defend the Ecchi aspects of it.  But there's really one flaw with this game.   There's FAR better games out there.  This is the only Suda 51 game on Steam, and if you must play one of his games... well you could play this but I might call this his weakest game, and it seems the fans agree.  This is the only one on Steam.
But Bayonetta, and Metal Gear Solid Rising: Revengence are both on Steam and they're not the only games with similar combat styles.  The fact is both of those games are a bit better and cohesive than this game.  I'd say both of those games are better.  If you want to look at women's body, Bayonetta lets you do it in a slightly more contextual fashion (And similarly over the top).  If you want great action both of those games have it.  If you want a convoluted story, Revengence has that.
So what about Killer Is Dead?  Well if you've played both of those games, or want something by Suda 51, grab this game.  It's not a bad game, it's just not a great game, and the more games I've played I realize I really want to recommend the best. Towerclimb is an incredibly well designed roguelike, it's challenging, and all the mechanics in the game really work together to create a lot of depth. The game is also quite fair, and very rarely puts you in no-win situations, if you know what you're doing.
That said, the game has a lot of mechanics that need to be learned early on, so it may seem frustrating to new players, my suggestion is to stick with it, and possibly read a few guides. This is the kind of game where players with 100s of hours in the game still die frequently at the game's harder levels, so don't feel bad if you die a bit early on. Spend enough hours in the game, and you'll be breezing through the early levels.

TowerClimb is a skill-based 2D platformer. This game is a work of art. It's flawless and unforgiving. It can and will make you hate yourself, but it will feel extremely rewarding when you develop the skills you need. Gamepad is a MUST! Good Climbing!

For a brief summary of the game:
You are a tiny man. You must climb the tower. The tower and its denizens will kill you. Lots.
This game is incredibly fun, and infinitely replayable. Levels are randomly generated with each character, and death is permanent (save for limited revive potions you can obtain). The challenge is always new, and always tests your skill.
There is so much love and attention to detail packed into the game. The core mechanics and progression are solid, and optional, hidden areas provide plenty of additonal challenge. The community is open and friendly (the devs and players *will* stop by if you stream)
In all, this game is fun. With yourself, with friends in co-op, with Zardo chasing after you. If you like platformers and want a challenge, this is the game. (plus, with talks of a level-creator to be released eventually, there's no worry of you ever running out of things to do)

I won't bother writing a long, detailed review as to why this game is so great, seeing as others have already done so.
What I will do is say this; Every other roguelike game I've played has felt like just that - a game. I fire up the game and play it with an emotional investment similar to that of a game of chess or Minesweeper. They just feel like games, no more and no less.
But this game is different. It doesn't feel like a game. It feels like an ADVENTURE. The music, the atmosphere, the imaginative level, monster, and character designs all make this world feel like more than just another rearrangement of the same levels. It's a roguelike, but every time I play it feels like something more than "just another run." Maybe this sounds too corny, but Towerclimb brought to the table something I've wanted in roguelikes for quite some time. I honestly didn't think these kinds of games could get this good.
In sum: If you like roguelikes, platforming, and want a game that really tries to be more than just a game, then you should totally give this game a try.
Although quite unforgiving, and with a bit of a learning curve, this is my go-to game to kill some time. You will die a lot, but you'll get better and go further with each play.

Wizardry 8 is a great game if you are not a guy keen on crisp graphics.
It's a classic dungeon crawler rpg where you can make your whole party in every detail which is part of the fun. You'll meet many incredible monsters, some easy to beat, some hard to beat, some even impossible to beat - (you might have to run from them).
The story is continued from its predecessors and now your party can even ascend and become gods (or cosmic lords, as the game calls it). Which is incredibly fun!
So it's not an easy game at all. It can be a challenge. And you can build your characters wrong so they may be useless in the endgame. But it's an incredibly rewarding game. For every new player, I'd recommend to make yourself familiar with the game on normal or easy settings, then go for the 3rd and highest difficulty for an amusing game where you'll sometimes have to run but where XP flows steadily and challenges come galore.
Just for fun, I have started a speedrun to share my hundreds of hours I have played this game - not only on steam, but before too. I'm so happy about this version as my old DVDs didn't work with Windows 7 anymore.
You can read newbie tips about the game here:
- and you'll have access to my YouTube from there too.
And there are, of course, many Playthroughs on YouTube for the game. Some of them really funny if new guys play it blindly. You will experience some of the fun if you buy and play this game just like that.
And for the speedbumps, you can go to e.g. my blog and get some starting help :-)

Finally! Here's an old-school RPG that has at least some of the modern conveniences that we've come so heavily to rely upon. Streamlined combat, graphics that are good enough to let you know what things are, and just a generally playable experience. The voice quips by your characters are a lot of fun. This is the only Wizardry game I'd recommend (though even so, only if you're into the genre...)

Well, I think I've spent enough time in this "game" to review it.  It's Very Positive because there's not a lot negative to say.  It's free (+), You can buy plants like microtransactions (-) but they're really inexpensive (+) and actually not even required since you get one freebie per week(+).  So far that's more +'s than -'s.
You can't sell the seeds you get but you CAN trade them so if you don't feel like spending 9 cents to get a plant, you can hit the trade forums and look for people who have the plant you want.  Some people will just give it to you (because after a certain point you'll get more plants than you need).
Another reason to pay money to the developers would be the existence of multiple pots/backgrounds.  I have personally purchased the Cat house AND the Apartment pots.  I could have just stuck with the default pot if I wanted though.
So what exactly do you do here?
Answer: you name your pot, you get a handful of starter plants, and a snail doing laps around the edge of the pot.  You water everything and listen to the music for a while.  If you focus on one plant you'll "sing" to it apparently.  I don't know if this really helps the plant grow or not, but it's not like it takes a ton of effort.
You could potentially let it sit and have it grow in real time (meaning you'd need to wait hours to see results) but after I've watered everything I just exit and come back the next day.  I nearly forgot: you also have to pull weeds that will appear daily, but I'm likewise unsure if letting the weeds grow actually hinders the other plants in any way.
After keeping everything well watered, eventually it reaches maturity and if you keep it in good health, it blooms.  You can overwater or underwater everything obviously but the game is pretty forgiving so if you accidentlally overwater a plant, it's not the end of the world.
So anyway, after the plant has reached maturity and bloomed, you can keep going or you can take the plant and throw it into the garden (which is a nice way of saying "be free plant...be free!" as you throw it away) and that makes room for more plants.
The game is also somewhat educational as you can see a variety of succulent plants by their Scientific name (though occasionally they also have more common names like "Aloe Vera").  I've never seen an Aloe plant bloom in real life so it's really educational there.
So yeah, as I said, there's no harm in trying it out, and if you feel like you just can't take 5 minutes a day to water your plants, you can put it in "vacation mode" and just never come back...though really, if you plan to never come back, why bother with vacation mode?
Answer: You WILL be back... if you liked it enough to play it once, you'll start it up again.  The one thing that might make me put mine in Vacation mode is when I hit 100% achievements.   Considering one of those achievements is for throwing out a ton of plants, I think it'll take me a while to get there.
