Grim Fandango is brilliant. Grim Fandango is terrible.
Is there a point to reviewing a 20-year old game at all?
Grim Fandango is by no means a bad game, but I must sadly admit it's not the best either.
I almost gave it a thumbs down in this review, but then I had to admit that despite all the negative aspects of the game now that I have finished it I am happy to have played it nonetheless. It's frustrating however that the game could have been a hundred times better if the developing team had paid attention to a few crucial details that would have elevated Grim to true cult status such as the Monkey Island series.
Puzzles are often strange and require trying items you have collected with characters and background interactive objects that have no reason or hint to be made working together (eg giving a bottle of drink to someone to make them puke). There's a lot of backtracking, camera angles and pathing are awkward, some puzzles require waiting and repetition (the worst culprit involves waiting for someone slowly walking around in a large circle to try catching him again if you fail the first time) and sections that involve fast vehicles are not fast at all.
But the worst flaw of Fandango is the probably the lack of detail of the Land of the Dead. The first act is set in a city called El Marrow during the Day of the Dead. There is a carnival in town, but this is shown only in the distance, behind a few tents. The second act is set in another city called Rubacava, where there is a place where giant cats race. No giant cat is ever really shown, they are only talked about. Why oh why would LucasArts waste such opportunities like these?!
Manny Calavera is a likeable enough protagonist - sassy, flawed, sometimes goofy, but never lacking spine (pun much intended). His sidekick Glottis is absolutely lovely, and the friendship the two of them develop is one of the best parts of the game. I wish there had been more of that.
Catch this Remastered version in a Steam sale if you love old-school point and click adventures.
In these times of sequels and reboots, is it too much to hope for a better remake of this visionary classic?

At first I came here for the money that could be made. But over the weeks, months, years... With the horrors I've seen, and done, guilt gradually took over. I tried to change things, I did. Tried to do right when I could.
For a long time then, I believed my moral choices would make a difference... but who were I kidding? I can see it now.
I'm as responsible for this mess as anyone here. Having lived and fed on this conflict day after day.
The guilt I once felt is only a faint memory now. Emptiness, bitterness, these are the only things left.
I'm feeling old and tired. This is what I've become.
There's no morality, no happy ending, not even the single hint of sense in all this.
I feel no more alive than all the people I've killed.
I ♥♥♥♥ing hate this war.
Who am I...? I am this war.

Real mixed feelings about this one. I cannot say that I don't recommend this game, but then...there are SO MANY WTF design choices here that made me wanna tear whatever hair I had left out! Let's explore!
7/10
Pros:
-African setting; haven't played many games with one of those!
-Graphics, flora and fauna, sunrises were especially gorgeous in the desert
-Sound effects, voice acting (I'm a sucker for African accents), music
-Variety of vehicles and weapons and characters
-Some missions offered multiple points of entry and exit, a lot of create-your-own-fun gameplay
Cons:
-ATROCIOUS driving physics and collision glitches. Fast-travel points were for the most part useless so there's a lotta frustrating driving back n forth.
-Buddy concept started off interesting but quickly became more of an annoying chore; ended up going for my mission objectives head on. I'd like to point out that the chore was highlighted by the fact that you had to do extra driving in order to accomodate your buddy!
-Enemies were designed to be more resilient than cars. Seriously, you can empty a sidearm clip into an enemy and they will still get up and fight. I've never seen such bullet-sponges before. Coupled with really bad hit boxes and aiming glitches and you've got one monster of a balancing issue - I played the game on easy! Ooh, and let's not forget that enemies can hit you with a shotgun from literally miles away.
-Stealth and the camo-suit are a joke.
-Enemy cars would always drive faster than you. Even if you were both driving the same type of vehicle.
-No auto-saving after mission updates or weapon unlocks etc... Keep your finger on that F5! Well, credits at least for a quick save option! ;) Though I have to say that regular saving kinda defeated the point and urgency of the safe houses.
-Story started off well but went nowhere pretty fast. More back-stabbings and double-crossings than a Mexican soap opera! Though it did end on a strong and interesting footing that had me thinking way past the credits.
-Lots of audio and graphical glitches. Very bad audio spatialization for one. I could hear enemy conversation from far away as if I was right up close to them.
There are some memorable moments and missions here and there. I ended up enjoying the gun store side-missions the most actually. For the price that you can get it nowadays, I'd say definitely give it a whirl.

If you are a fan of the Tomb Raider series, you will love this. It's like a top down approach to a classic Tomb Raider game. Good action, a range of weapons, puzzles ranging from easy to hard, etc.
There are optional puzzle rooms which will give you more powerful weapons or artifacts that will increase your stats. These are usually more challenging but are worth the reward.
There is a high replayability factor as each level comes with a number of challenges, such as finishing the level within a certain time frame, finding hidden blocks or areas, finding all ten red skulls, et cetera. These also reward you with better weapons or artifacts, and sometimes new costumes.
The game has a good difficulty curve, starting off relatively easy and becoming more difficult, with the last two or three levels being quite challenging (I played on hard combat difficulty).
In essence, good combat, good puzzles, relatively mediocre story (although that fits in perfectly with the original Tomb Raider series before the reboot) and plenty of replayability. Definitely worth it for a Tomb Raider fan. I'm looking forward to the sequel.

Lara Croft and the Guardian of light is an action game reminiscent of the Diablo games, where the camera is placed in a top-down perspective. You can play as Lara or Totec either alone or with a buddy.
Graphics-wise, the game is sharp, colourful and varied. There are many landscapes which show the great graphics of this game, including the inside of a temple, a lush forest and a living volcano.
On the gameplay-side, the game is fundamentally a twin-stick shooter where you use the left stick to move Lara, the right stick to aim your weapon and the right trigger button to shoot. It is a different and fun way of playing action games and I believe the controls are tight.
There isn't much emphasis on story in this game as it is a spin-off in the Tomb Raider series. Basically, you are tasked with chasing an Aztec God known as Xolotl  to retrieve the Mirror of Smoke and save humanity.
Overall, I would give this game a 7.5/10.

I remember playing the orginal Tomb Raider back when it as released on the original PlayStation.  Over the years, it seems more has been written about Ms. Crofts ever expanding bust than on the actual games themselves.  This changed with the release of the last Tomb Raider (which I haven't played as yet, though it is in my library to download).
I picked up this title as the description reminded me of the original in some way, but also cause I'm a sucker for a good action/adventure game.  And I'd just finished playing Shadowrun Returns, so the isometric view felt like a good fit.
This game holds the tenents of the series close.  As Lara, you must run, jump, shoot, bomb, swing, climb and puzzle your way though the temple with the Totec running point as you hunt down an ancient artifact and try to stop a catastrophe of epic proportions.  Lara quips with the best of them as well.  The puzzles require a bit of thought, some quick reflexes and when played in co-op mode, good communication to ensure you can make the most of Lara's and Totec's abilities.
While it may not be a "true" Tomb Raider title, Crystal Dynamics have crafted a game that takes the Croft name and does it justice.  I've thoroughly enjoyed playing through this and look forward to playing the second installment when my budget allows.

Steam tells me I have a bit over 200 hours in this game. Compared to some who play, that makes me still a newbie. Nonetheless, I can't quite believe all the negative reviews. So I've felt compelled to review a game for the first time.
Simply put: This is my favourite survival game. I've played a number of others, but this is the only one still on my computer. In some ways, it's a standard survival game: you crash-land on a planet, need to find resources to build a shelter, obtain food and water and make vehicles to explore. But that's just a surface description. I find this game incredibly absorbing.
What I find so compelling about it is how immersive I find it. Some may be put off by the fact that the only ways around the planet right now are vehicles with wheels or hovercraft. You can't just jump in a spaceship and fly around in two minutes. Exploring the planet is a real task and adventure. It feels like a real accomplishment to finally make it the poles.
The fact that the planet you are on has logical biomes is another big plus for me. The environment changes as you travel north or south. I've always been bothered by how so many games seem to just 'desert planets' or 'ice planets.'  PN has some thing like you'd expect a planet to be like.
I'm not much of a builder - my vehicles and buildings tend to be borderline functional, rather than anything else. But check out the forums. What some people manage to do with the game is simply amazing.
Is there anyone who might not like this game?  Yes - if you insist multiplayer is the only way to have fun. Or if you need to shoot things a lot.
The game is still EA, but, as I said, it is a favourite of mine. The devs are active, the community is friendly, and I can't wait to see what the future holds for Planet Nomads.

I had a copy of Wiz 8 back when it first came out, thanks to my dad. I was so enthralled whenever I watched him play it because of the gameplay and the character-creation. When I played it after I got older and was able to better grasp the mechanics of the game, I was still in love.
The first part of most RPGs, character creation, is an experience itself. With many races and classes to choose from, there is plenty of variety because you not only create 1 character, but you create 6. The races range from the Tolkienesque races to some really cool and unique playable races (Dracon. Faerie, Lizardman, Mook to name a few)There are plenty of different classes to choose from also. Developing your characters throughout the game is also great. There are many spells to use too.
The game plays like many of the old school RPGs like M&M in a FPS type. Just watch the video to get the idea. Wiz 8 was the last of a dying breed when it came out, but I personally enjoy the gameplay. Combat is turnbased while exploring is free roam.
The story of Wiz 8 is actually pretty fascinating and proves to be enagaging at times. I'll leave it there and let it unfold for you because I had the story spoiled for me and I will never forget it. I wish it wasn't spoiled.
All in all, I can praise and review and talk about how fun Wiz 8 is til I'm blue in the face. For 10 bucks its a steal (comes fully patched and the graphics are improved compared to the original release.) considering to get a CD copy is about 50 bucks. (They don't make it anymore and not many were made). Get it, play it, and enjoy the experience of Wizardry 8.

I first played this when it was state of the art 10 or so years ago.  I loved it back then, and it fills a place that not many more modern games have filled since: turn-based RPGs where you control a whole group of characters.  Like a table-top RPG, you can pause and think about the spell you want to cast next or which monster you want to kill first.  *gasp!* You can use strategy!  Comparable games from the time would be Might and Magic 7 & 8.  If you enjoyed either of those and never played a Wizardry game before, this is a good option, with slightly better graphics than either of those two (yes, they're all dated.  Get over it.).  What sets Wizardry 8 apart from similar style Might and Magic games is the unique story, non-standard character classes, and a science fiction edge you don't normally get in fantasy games.  In fact, some of the playable character races are aliens!
If you like oldskool RPGs, I'd definitely recommend picking this one up at a good price.

Take this review with a grain of salt. It's a good game, really, but it's just missing something for me. I'm a big fan of Spelunky and, to me, this just feels like a reverse Spelunky with less to offer. I may give the game another shot in the future, but for now I just don't have the patience for it.

As Vinny puts it, it's Reverse Spelunky. You play a pixel man (or rather, series of ill-fated pixel men) attempting to ascend a 100-floor tower. Of course, where gravity would generally work in your favour in Spelunky, climbing UP a maze of deathtraps makes for a fairly different experience.
It's an excruciatingly hardcore game. It's permadeath, and where Spelunky gave you a health system, roughly everything in TowerClimb will eviscerate, bifurcate, detonate, devour, or melt you upon contact, whereby you had better still have a revival potion on you if you want to continue. Apparently the game is divided into chapters, but I've never made it past the first one. I get the feeling I haven't made it even halfway through the first one. That being said, the random levels make for good replay factor and the hazards change up pretty regularly as you progress. Just don't expect it to be as forgiving as Spelunky.
Only real complaint is lack of a pause function, you only get to take a breather between floors.

Beside Gwent my favorite card game. I haven't ever imagined to like games like this, but things change obviously when getting older and grayer :D
The first thing to mention and and the biggest difference compared to Gwent: The match system. You got a two-lane-system and every card can attack either the enemy cards or the life pool of your opponent.
First of all the two-lanes: One allows you to place units, which are covered from attacks for a round until they attack. This offers some great (game changing and) funny matches.
Beside that, the game comes along with the well know daily-reward system, you know from other free to play titles. You have 1-3 quests to fullfil to get gold and this can be used to get card sets. There are themed sets and regular ones. Themed ones cost 500 gold and contain 50 cards. Regular contain 6 random cards at the cost of 100 Gold.
If you cannot wait, cuz you are an whinning baby, that wants everything immediately, you also have the opportunity to buy cards for real money. Beginning at 2 EUR for 12 cards and upwards.
That how to get cards by the ingame currency or your own wallet. You also get new cards by leveling up your character like in an RPG. Also RPG-related are the race-connected traits. The different races offer a better opportunity to collect specific card types more quickly, e.g. High elves get a higher drop rate for magic related stuff, Imperial ones for building up mass armies on the battlefield etc. - this race can be changed if you want, e.g. when looking for specific card types for your collection.
A great idea from my point of view.
When it comes to the cards themselves, as you progress through the game, defeating opponents and earning rewards, will give you an upgrade to cards you already own, e.g. turn an attack into a guard, which must be destroyed first by the enemy, to break through to your life pool - except this attacker has a "break through" ability.
These and other mechanics make this game awesome to me.
In the end, you should know this game offers cross-play too. So when having Android or iOS you can play vs. all other plattforms too - that's what I am missing at Gwent (up to know). So if you are looking for something on your way to work, for your morning coffee or morning toilet sessions, you should give this game a try. It is free and offers great fun and matches.
So stop wasting your time and reading reviews like this, download it, it is free! ;)

What an excellent game! I'll preface this review by saying that I'm an OLD-school player. I  enjoy an honest-to-goodness sandbox game, and played EvE for years. I have been looking for a game like EvE but more suited to my personal tastes, and Perpetuum is perfect. The skill system is similar to EvE, but is different in one important aspect: points are based on playtime instead of simply time. There are skill point rewards you receive while you do certain tasks, and then these points can be awarded to the skills you choose. That's more satisfying to me than EvE's platform, and it moves much quicker because the point system is pretty generous, and is not fixed. Point bonuses are random, but you have to play to earn them.
Another improvement is the fact that the mechs are land-based, and line-of-sight along with terrain becomes very important in PvP. The mechs can be specialized in great detail, much like the ships in EvE.
Fair warning about this game. If you like complexity, depth of gameplay, and the rewards that come with a player-driven economy, you'll enjoy Perpetuum. If you are used to theme-park games and are looking for constant action, this is not what you're looking for. PvP is expensive, and finding a good corporation early in order to teach you the ropes is essential. There's a lot of repetitive play involved, but this is rooted in old-school game philosophy.
I've recently played Xyson (good game but no one plays), Albion Online (too commercialized for me), Anarchy Online, TERA, SotA, and a bunch of others looking for a good crafting-based game that also has PvP. Perpetuum is it. The sale right now makes it extremely worthwhile to pick up, and the optional DL's add huge value to the package. For less than 10 bucks you can get enough points to be competitive in-game.
Most people giving a thumbs-down are simply not interested in the type of gameplay Perpetuum offers. As a genuine sandbox game, there's very little in the way of competition on the market. (Especially if you enjoy EvE, but want some interesting differences in mechanics and the way skills work.)
Lastly...in a game like this, graphics are secondary to gameplay. However, the game is beautiful, and the graphics are pretty damned good tbh. They just aren't cutting-edge. Some games have great graphics and no gameplay at all. NO MAN can argue with that, yeah?
2 BIG thumbs up!!

Under no circumstance should any human being subject themselves to experiencing this game ever. I know that it was made by someone who has feelings, and probably put at least two hours into coding this game, but there is no possible way any real person could say one good thing about this game. Let's get into it:
"Story":
You play as a man named "Pears" who has to live through a never ending nightmare of collecting fruit on straight platforms. At the beginning of each level you talk to a "Witch" who is just a girl in gray shorts who talks in broken english about fruit or something, I'm not entirely sure as the story didn't immediately entice me.
Gameplay / controls:
The main character controls like a drunk guy with cerebral palsy. Sprinting physically moves your character from side to side, so if you sprint on a thin platform you immediately fall off. Jumping is attrocious, it is floaty and it seems to be random what direction exactly you jump in, especially while sprinting. Also, the mouse is perpetually on the screen and just floats around when you play, so that is really fun to look at.
Level Design / environment:
Each level looks like it was designed by a 10 year old in Roblox. They consist entirely of straight platforms that are green. Thats literally it. The "challenge" in this game is being able to walk on a straight platform for 10 minutes straight without scraping out your eyeballs. Also, after attempting it for about 45 minutes, I think level 7 is LITERALLY impossible. You have to perfectly time a jump over a chasm 10 times without dying, but collecting the apples falling from above you does not increase the amount of apples in your inventory. I think there's some secret way to beat it as well, but there are absolutely no landmarks so it's probably an invisible trigger somewhere in a tree. Fun.
Overall Opinion:
There is literally nothing good to say about this game. Terrible story, gameplay, and levels. Not worth one cent, let alone 5 dollars. The only semi redeemable factor is that the attrociously bad writing can be funny sometimes. But I use "redeemable" VERY loosely. It's like leveling up from the holocaust to the columbine shooting.
The thing too is that I usually love bad games, but this game is clearly untested, unfinished, and I would definitely say unplayable. My first ever 0/10.

Grim Fandango is a brillantly written game directed by Tim Schafer(The first two Monkey Island games & Broken Age). The game is set in the Eighth Underworld or the "Land of the Dead" focusing on Manuel "Manny" Calavera. Every human who has died in the land of the living immidiately comes to the Eighth Underworld in skeleton form. Each newly deceased human is welcomed by a travel agent of the Department of the Dead(or D.O.D. for short) that pose as grim reapers with black cloack and slythe. The reaper's job is to look up the life of each client and see which packet they deserve the most. The Those who lived a great life can immidiately travel to the Ninth Underworld via a Double Nine Ticket. However those who didn't live a good life or committed a sin of some kind have no choice but receive the second hand offer or end up doing some work in order to earn the right to go to the Ninth Underworld. Manny Calavera was unfornate to not get a Double Nine ticket so he ended up working for the D.O.D. as a reaper to assist as many premium clients as he could find in order to earn the ticket to his final destination. In the beginning of his career, he was getting tons of clients that were elgible to go to the Ninth Underworld. But lately he's been stuck with second rate clients that don't come close to getting their own tickets. To make matters worse, Manny is being pressured by his boss to either find a premium client or risk being fired for failure to improve. This leads Manny to breaking some rules in order to find a lead client who is qualified to get a Double Nine Ticket. And he may of found more than he bargained for once he greets himself to the newly deceased Mercedes 'Meche' Colomar. A woman who just might be the key to help Manny out. Grim Fandango is a classic that succeeds in story, characters, and art. This was one of LucasArts' earlier 3D rendering games as all of the characters are designed with polygonic graphics. But despite the limitations of the technology, they manage to create a colorful and imaginative world. The world itself is massive and draws inspiration from film noir, art deco, mexican/mayan arcitecture, and the holiday of Día de Muertos(Day of the Dead). Which is what this game's theme is, is the celebration in honoring the dead on the day after Halloween. The time period is ambigious, I think that helps the game feel timeless as this story could of happened during any decade. The acting and the dialoge is on par, I loved all of the one liners and to this day I find myself quoting the game almost everyday. The majority of the characters are voice by Spanish actors to help fit the theme of the game. This Remastered edition offers the options of either playing the game in the Remastered form which has smoother graphics and better drop shadow effects as well as the option to play the game in its original form. With hours of different dialoge options it's recommended to play the game multiple times. Cause after all these years I am still discovering new quotes and events in this game. Overrall this game has class and created a lasting impression to me, anyone reading this review I hope will have the same experience as I did. Cause Grim Fandango offers an adventure story that you won't ever forgot.

Far Cry 2 is one of the best shooters of all time. Like any good story, it's loosely inspired by Heart of Darkness. And believe you me, the story, barebones as it might seem (no traditional cutscene until the very very end), is shocking and incredible. Trust no one, shoot everything that moves, you will be friendlier with your ingame buddies than your real life ones, all that good vidyagamey stuff.
Far Cry 2 avoids many of the flaws of its successor - a game I would best describe as Robinson Crusoe for somebody who wants a power trip. Not knocking its many successes (the animal system, etc), but many RPGs make the mistake of letting the player get away with pretty much anything in the lategame. Far Cry 2 is not an RPG. You will make decisions, but you're not in search of XP: you're in search of a better chance at survival, and if you're feeling lucky, maybe you'll try to keep your buddies alive too.
Far Cry 2 is an experience.I chose to disable the crosshair because muh immersion (note the presence of ironsights makes that decision slightly less punishing compared to, say half-life) and I highly recommend you do the same as well, because this game, despite having questionable graphics from the mid-2000s, works best when you're immersed and twitchy and prepared mentally for the worst.
Far Cry 2 gives you nothing. You have to earn every buddy, hoard every high quality weapon you own, build your reputation with the factions brick by brick. Regardless of your choice of APR or UFLL - pick your own lesser of two evils - your greatest enemy is the jungle itself. Your guns will jam and even break (usually when you need them most), the harsh terrain and many, many faction guard posts means that even a trip between two safehouses a mile apart must be planned and taken with the utmost caution, and don't even get me started on malaria. If you play Far Cry 2, prepare to be challenged.
Far Cry 2 is a first person shooter that does not encourage combat. Even one soldier is a very valid threat of death. You do have a safety net in the form of your buddies, but don't rely on it. It's almost always better to detour around or sneak past a guard post than to plow through it. Stealth is encouraged but not rewarded - you can stealth kill, but guards will almost always scream out upon death, meaning that a kill threatens you more than helps you. Even carrying a sniper rifle at all times (highly recommended) and engaging from a great distance carries great risk, from multiple guards jumping in jeep and running and gunning you down, or mortar strikes, or a random patrol invalidating 90% of your hard work. Recommendation? Be ready to move, always keep your health high, and your life is worth more than anything else, even (especially?) the mission.
Far Cry 2 will not leave you in the same place you began it. Many (most?) video games place you as the most important person in the world and give you all the tools to your success. This is not a power fantasy. This isn't even an underdog fantasy. This is hard work, and any reward will be in your head alone. You will be beaten down and beaten up, but if you beat the game, you will genuinely feel accomplishment and success unlike any game out there.

Even at this early development of the game, I have to say it is very good.  I have had no performance problems since starting to play and I have over 30 hours of play time.  The build system is as good as I have seen for most games and it is still pre-alpha.  The variety of structures you can build is litterally up to your imagination.  As far as the vehicles are concerned, the physics are good and the reward for exploration is adequate and maybe a little too easy.
The biggest challenge in the beginning will be food and water (of couse).  Like any survival game, water, food, and shelter will be the priorities but the game is generous by providing the escape pod from the beginning.  Once water, food and shelter are under control, you will have plenty of time to experiment.  I highly recommend using the creative mode to experiment with vehicles because you are restricted at first by the materials you have access to.  That said, even with the basic materials, you can build almost any wheeled vehicle you can imagine.  I am looking forward to watercraft and aircraft.  I have seen video of a monorail system which looks great and would be a real challenge (all of the components have to be made from the available building blocks).
The concept of a mobile fortress is a great concept as well.  The player will have to find enough Xaenite but that is part of the fun and it can be done if you manage your resources with that in mind.
Jet packs can be upgraded as can the multitool; there is also a rifle now which is handy for the wild life that is entirely hostile and will react to your presence if you get too close or disturb its protected habitat.
Pros:
The build system has a fairly steep learning curve but creative mode is a great place to get used to it.  Once you get used to the build system, you should be okay in Story mode.  This cannot be overlooked and if you want to drastically reduce your frustration level, you should definitely use Creative mode to learn the game mechanics. Creative mode is a plus and without it, the frustration of the learning curve might be too much for some; creative mode is a ;us.
Swimming is a thing and your vehicles can move underwater so you sort of get watercraft if you accept that; just watch out for crevaces.
Multiple energy sources give you the flexibility to keep weight to a minimum which helps when designing vehicles.
The conveyor system is nice but it does require a lot of resources so be ready for that.
Cons:
I would like to see a vehicle design function where you can save designs and export those for use in Story mode.  That would save a lot of time and only be stricted by the available matierials which you would still have to collect.
I have had no hangs or crashes during game play with the current build; however, the game did hang once when loading from a saved game which was easily rectified by restarting the game..
There is no way to raise the terrain in order to level the ground out by building it up in some cases.  Being able to build up and/or smooth the terain would make a lot of sense in a game like this considering some of the advanced technology.  I expect this later and would be surprised if it wasn't added.
The graphics are not state of the art as yet but still very nice and I appreciate the fact that they are what they are which allows for better screen rendering of distant objects and better video performance overall.
By far my biggest complaint (and not that bad really) is the reduction of frame rate.  After playing for a few hours whithout stopping, you will likely notice a declining frame rate.  This is not a big problem as you can save the game and reload to resolve it.  I am sure the developers know about this and will optimize the game to account for this.
I would like to see an away-from-keyboard (AFK) feature because you will die if you leave the game for an extended period of time; starvation and dehydration are real concerns and will kill your character.  AFK mode would prevent that.
Multiplayer:
I am not sure if this will be a thing in the game but it is not an issue for me.  I understand if it is for some because multiplayer would add a considerable amount advantages with regard to resource collection and planet exploration.
Conclusion:
I realize the early game had a lot of problems (I did not play it before the current release 0.7.4) so bear that in mind.  The reviews prior to the last two version updates seem bad but the game has seen remarkable improvement (if the early reviews are accurate).  The price, 19.99, is not a hardship and for early access, well worth it.  I have purchased much, much worse for more money (a certain ******sky comes to mind).  Give Planet Nomads a try.  If you keep the fact that this is pre-alpha, I don't think you will be disappointed.  Each new update holds the potential to make this game even greater.

A fun game, with a unique style and flair.  Ultimately, while I enjoyed Killer is Dead, I'm not sure if I can say it's a Good Game.  It's certianly not a bad game, but KiD's is a story of a death by a thousand cuts; numerous small--if not trivial--problems that ultimately come together to sour an otherwise entertaining game.
I think, fundamentally, Killer is Dead suffers from a lack of polish in almost every regard.  The art style, while nice, can sometimes come across as muddy and, perhaps, overly busy at times.  The story is pretty straightforward, but some attempts at humor seem dramatically out of place, as are some of the minigames.  Some of the mechanics of the game aren't explained very well.  Menus have lag.
Lastly, but most importantly, is the gameplay.  I'm not super versed with Character Action games, for whatever reason I've never really spent a lot of time grinding them out, despite playing many of them, so I'll try to leave comparisons to the experts, and speak to my general experience with Killer is Dead's gameplay.  The game is a little simple and button mash-y.  Many of the enemies feel like they cheat, breaking out of stun locks while you're in the middle of a combo and sucker-puching you.  Either the game queues inputs, drops inputs, or lags at times, if not a combination of the above, leading to some frustrating hits and deaths.  Hitboxes are wonky, and occasionally linger.  Enemies often hit larger areas than they seem like they should, and overall the combat just feels clunky enough to feel like you aren't always responsible for when you mess up.
A handful of enemies in particular, included some bosses, exemplify these problems.  They attack quickly, sometimes with very little wind-up, and punish mistakes heavily.
None of these are intrinsic problems, but it's hard not to feel like there's not a mismatch between the gameplay and the enemies you play against.
Still, overall, I found that I really enjoyed the time I spent with Killer is Dead.  I try to be reasonably indepth with my criticisms, but most of what I've listed are annoyances, for the most part, especially if you are playing at the lower difficulties (which I recommend).  The fact that I'm still playing the game despite already completing the main story should testify to the fact that the game is, at the end of the day, something worth spending time on.  In my opinion, at least.
If you are looking for a game to play casually, I think Killer is Dead can satisfy, as most of it's frustrations only really show themselves in full if you are committed to getting the best ranking on all the missions.  However, if you are a fan of Character Action games looking for a new title for the library, you might be dissappointed.  Ultimately, Killer is Dead lacks the finesse to really compete with it's brothers and sisters in the genre.

TL:DR:
If you're curious, give it a shot! Interesting unique, and extremely fun!
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I came in expecting a Hearthstone clone, but was shockingly suprised at how unique and genuinely fun the game is.
It is a great blend between the streamlined Hearthstone and complexity of Magic the Gathering. There are a lot of unique effects that aren't present in HS. Alternate win-cons, effects similar to enchantments, and theres even a Graveyard! The graveyard matters too!
Nice F2P model, Spending money will obviously help you get to the cards you want for high tier play, but by no means necessary. Watching streams on Twitch gives you items in-game if your account is linked, like legendaries, coins or soul gems to craft cards with. Getting cards is easy as well, as you are guarenteed a card every 3 wins, on top of 15 to 50 gold for 3 wins.
If youre wary of playing online card games, theres a solo arena where you can learn the game, as well as an introductory story that does a good job of teaching the game as well.
You can spend 500 in-game gold (5 packs worth) to get decks that are well worth the investment, and are very playable. You get one of the 6 decks for free on completing the story too!
Ladder is a bit easier to climb, and doesnt knock you down as far as HS does at start of new seasons.
I think the only downside is that theres not a ton of info  out there on how most of the game stuff functions. Most of it ive found were asked in subreddits.
Seriously, the game is worth a shot if youre curious at all.

I was aware of Grim Fandango when it first came out, but never got a chance to play it then.  So I was pleased to see it available, and I was most happy to find it was as fun as I had hoped.
The first question I like to consider for point-and-clicks relates to the puzzles as gameplay.  In this regard, Grim Fandango scores well.  The chain of logic behind solutions usually holds together, at least once you've explored enough.  There are also plenty of efforts to go beyond "find the thing to put on the thing", where you have just a couple of items and need to do something clever with them.  There are certainly puzzles that I didn't like (that forklift can go burn), but on the whole the gameplay was pretty good.
Next question is how well the puzzles serve the story.  This is done reasonably well here.  The need to get to know the NPCs for solutions helps; quite a few puzzles rely on the quirks of your sidekick Glottis, for example.  The good chain of logic helps too, as it is clear what your goal is and why it makes sense within that point of the narrative.
But the big question is always the strength of the story, and Grim Fandango has a pretty good one.  There are some elements of the setting that don't actually make sense if you think about it, and Manny's quest lacks motivation to begin with.  He also seems to be the master of the off-screen moment of awesome, which at times is incongruous with how he behaves under your control.  These are minor nit-picks, though, swamped by the likeable, believable characters; genuine humour and emotion; imaginative world; and cleverly-woven plot.  There are plenty of moments of foreshadowing only apparent on a second play, and lots of little call-backs throughout.  The climax is a little weak, but even this is compensated by a satisfying ending cinematic.
I've played quite a few adventure games in my time.  I'm not sure if Grim Fandango is my favourite, but it's definitely up there among the best.

Far Cry 2 is one of the best shooters of all time. Like any good story, it's loosely inspired by Heart of Darkness. And believe you me, the story, barebones as it might seem (no traditional cutscene until the very very end), is shocking and incredible. Trust no one, shoot everything that moves, you will be friendlier with your ingame buddies than your real life ones, all that good vidyagamey stuff.
Far Cry 2 avoids many of the flaws of its successor - a game I would best describe as Robinson Crusoe for somebody who wants a power trip. Not knocking its many successes (the animal system, etc), but many RPGs make the mistake of letting the player get away with pretty much anything in the lategame. Far Cry 2 is not an RPG. You will make decisions, but you're not in search of XP: you're in search of a better chance at survival, and if you're feeling lucky, maybe you'll try to keep your buddies alive too.
Far Cry 2 is an experience.I chose to disable the crosshair because muh immersion (note the presence of ironsights makes that decision slightly less punishing compared to, say half-life) and I highly recommend you do the same as well, because this game, despite having questionable graphics from the mid-2000s, works best when you're immersed and twitchy and prepared mentally for the worst.
Far Cry 2 gives you nothing. You have to earn every buddy, hoard every high quality weapon you own, build your reputation with the factions brick by brick. Regardless of your choice of APR or UFLL - pick your own lesser of two evils - your greatest enemy is the jungle itself. Your guns will jam and even break (usually when you need them most), the harsh terrain and many, many faction guard posts means that even a trip between two safehouses a mile apart must be planned and taken with the utmost caution, and don't even get me started on malaria. If you play Far Cry 2, prepare to be challenged.
Far Cry 2 is a first person shooter that does not encourage combat. Even one soldier is a very valid threat of death. You do have a safety net in the form of your buddies, but don't rely on it. It's almost always better to detour around or sneak past a guard post than to plow through it. Stealth is encouraged but not rewarded - you can stealth kill, but guards will almost always scream out upon death, meaning that a kill threatens you more than helps you. Even carrying a sniper rifle at all times (highly recommended) and engaging from a great distance carries great risk, from multiple guards jumping in jeep and running and gunning you down, or mortar strikes, or a random patrol invalidating 90% of your hard work. Recommendation? Be ready to move, always keep your health high, and your life is worth more than anything else, even (especially?) the mission.
Far Cry 2 will not leave you in the same place you began it. Many (most?) video games place you as the most important person in the world and give you all the tools to your success. This is not a power fantasy. This isn't even an underdog fantasy. This is hard work, and any reward will be in your head alone. You will be beaten down and beaten up, but if you beat the game, you will genuinely feel accomplishment and success unlike any game out there.

It's not quite accurate to say Perpetuum is Eve-Online-but-with-mechs, but it's a good place to start.  The games share a GREAT deal in design and general layout.
There are a few things I've really enjoyed so far about Perpetuum.  There's basically always something to do, because running missions is actually a viable source of income.  If you want to get engaged you can choose a combat mission, or if you want to run the game in the background, you can do a transport mission.
There are 3 levels of PVP - none, all, and some more.  You can play on the "alpha" islands without danger of PVP, or risk a trip to the outer islands for higher rewards, or a chance for a fight!
Combat is meaningful because losing bots removes them from your inventory - and you have to buy a new one.  But the prices are aligned fairly well in my opinion, so that losing a bot doesn't feel like the end of the world.  It makes me much more willing to risk something for some fun.
The game has a multi-level crafting system that can be shared at the corp level, 3 primary factions and 1 other faction that is still being added, and a lot of opportunity for player-created content.
Key Feature: No subscription.

Have you ever been a gym junkie? Well I have found the game for you. It’s our second day of running 89AM Studio’s games and today’s game is Lift It. If you’re a recovering gym junkie or want to experience that life style then you may want to check this game out… That is until you wear out your up key. You see, shout out to Xavier Woods of WWE fame, this is the game that is all about the up up but not the down down. Every task you perform at the gym is a race to see how fast you can press the up arrow key. Every single bloody task.
You see you can lift it, you can bench it, hell you can even tread mill your way to glory and fame but every single one of those will be a repetitive press of the up key. The game may have been a quality game – well at least better than what it is – if there was any thought put into the game design. Why not have the tread mill be a combination of left and right arrows signifying the moving of your feet. Weight lifting could could be up and down to signify the fact that you’re raising it and lowering it, squats could be an arrow key and a down key to signifying an action of bending, etc. It wouldn’t take much thought but the monotony of the actions would be decreased and you may want to play further than ten or twenty minutes into the game.
I had to laugh when I saw that the first non-player controlled character was ‘old master.’ He looks like what I would imagine a 20-year old Asian gang member to look like. Quite funny and no disrespect at all meant at all to the gang members. The graphics appear to be straight out of the very first year of Information Technology programming class’s programming language and it plays similarly too.
Given that it’s still in early access it’s too early to earmark this one down as a dud but a lot of work will have to go into raising its level. Given that the developers have worked on and released 3 Coins at School since putting this one out into early access it is doubtful that it will receive the attention that it desperately needs.
Short and sweet...  Save your money.
Not worth the money.

Launched the game. Spent ages ignorantly mining for minerals.  Assembled something like a hovel.  A techno-hovel.
Built a vehicle.  It was terrible; bad center of gravity, bad design, flipped, rolled, got stuck.  Started gathering resources at a faster rate.
Built a second vehicle.  It was terrible; too slow, got stuck, flipped.  Was a bit better though.   Resource rate went up further.
Built my third vehicle.   It was fast, it had a high wheel base, it never flipped.
Drove straight to the north pole.
An hour or so later, I was dying from cold and toxins on the edge of a mountain at the magnetic north. I managed to survive, headed for home, heavily laden with precious metals and optimism.
On the way back I discovered a beautiful hidden valley amongst the cold and ice.  Decided this would be my new home.
Upon my return to home base I refueled my scout vehicle, manufactured supplies, upgraded my equipment.  It was time; I proceeded to carefully plot out the ideal route to the valley for a very heavy vehicle. Using my scout car I carefully placed a dozen solar way-beacons along the ideal route.  I couldn’t risk any flipping or forced abandoning for what would come next.
This was the biggest vehicle yet- ten wheels, four for steering, a massive container for all my worldly goods.  Over two stories in height, she was huge. I Disassembled my sprawling base, all my items. Apprehensively I even tore apart my trusty scout car.
Everything was loaded into this one giant vehicle.
I have about an hour of frustration and driving ahead of me, I will get back to that valley and start my new life.
Recommended for people with imagination, people that like to build things and people that want to support growing projects.

A very good game with a lot of potential. Still early access obviously but it compares well to the competition. It's SP only and I have no issue with that - actually bought the game specifically because the developers said they were abandoning MP. MP requires a whole different approach to balance and almost universally degrades the SP experience. Take Conan and ARK as examples; both need mods or significant changes to make them playable SP because the balance is geared towards MP.
There's numerous biomes on the world and travel is neccessary. There's no one ideal place. Resource gathering is a good balance, it doesn't feel like a grind. Combat is still developing, currently you have no real way to fight any of the serious enemies save running them over - which they can't fight back against. There's only 1 weapon you can create and it's like 3 clips per enemy for anything challenging enough you'd need to shoot it - and clips are very resource intensive. By the time you kill all the beasties in a nest with the gun the first ones you killed have probably respawned making it pointless.
Base building is excellent already, which is a very good sign. All in all it's a good entry into the field and it's starting out with a point - build a starship to get off the planet. The whole 'why' aspect of it is missing from many games still.
If you're good with early access and want a good 'stranded on an alien planet' survival game, this is an excellent choice and the developers have clearely laid out goals and have kept up with the updates. Good odds on this one being a finished game. IMO, worth the buy.

First off, don't listen to the bad reviews.  They are all pissy because of no multiplayer.  This game is in the Alpha state and it's VERY playable.
The Devs decided that it was going to be a single player experience and not a multiplayer one.  It's THEIR game!
It could change in the future but after Space Engineers’ growing pains trying to make it multiplayer I'd rather play a game that works instead of it being broken for months because they got pressured into multiplayer.
Ok, that said, the game starts you out on a planet.  This is Alpha so there's only one planet for now.  I'm ok with that because there is lots to do.
You get out of your pod and try to survive which is very doable because you have planets to eat until you want to go after meat.
The weird looking creatures are (imho) placeholders for now.
After finding/mining iron, and minerals, you can build a base.  This consists of separate floors, walls and ceilings, kind of like Fallout 4's building system.
Next you add a generator and connect it to several machines you can build.
If you want to get a feel for the game, Kage848 over on YouTube has done a few lets plays.
Randomise User over on Youtube can teach you how to get started.
Of go read their forum pages to see that they are updating the game almost weekly.
It does has some frame rate issues that are present in any new game.
All in all, I'd recommend this game if you're looking for some fun.

TL:DR - "Towerclimb is one of the most engaging, menacing and downright tense games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. It will make you want to throw your controller across the room and then desperately reassemble it to keep playing more. It's atmosphere and music are big highlights alongside the tense gameplay."
Long form - This game is recommended for persistant, dedicated, patient players. It is *very* old school tough and it does NOT cater to people who are looking for a game with all the (cough) "features" of modern rogue-lites like constant saves, several lives,  and character building mechanics that make successive runs easier; this game gives you none of that. This is 80's-90's tough, at least when you are starting out. Then you play more, get a bit farther, learn what things to watch out for, learn how far you jump and the way you can move in the air. You begin to understand how the monsters and traps work. Then, gradually you can get to floor 8, then 10, then 19 and finally you beat chapter 1. And when you do reach the top for your first time your heart, I gauruntee you this, will feel like it is about to explode with a mix of anxiety, fear, and joy. Then your baloon ride up puts you into chapter 2. You can relax a bit at this point because you can now access chapter 2 content without having to beat the tower again. Which BTW...
**Acessing chapter 2 is done by picking-up the "2" to the right of the Tower Entrance and bringing it to the portal during the new game scene. The skull, if brought to the portal, activates Centurion Trials.**
On the negative, a downside faced by new players is that It has *very* nuanced and subtle mechanics and "tricks" that are not laid out clearly. Almost none of these tricks are required for beating the first chapter but knowing them and using them well makes the climb to the top significantly safer.

Grim Fandango is a masterpiece.
I have always loved this game because I played it throughout my childhood, and so nostalgia means that I will always love it for the feelings that flood back to me each time I load up the game. However, this does not discredit this amazing work of art.
You are transported to another world, a dead one to be specific, where film noir and mexican folklore entwine pefectly to tell a compelling story. Not only is the story interesting, but the characters are witty and sharp, the dialogue is hilarious and the artwork is enjoyable to look at. I genuinely believe this to be one of the greatest adventure games of all time and I would strongly recommend it to anyone who loves adventure or puzzle games.
One particular aspect I love is that you get to choose the topic of conversation when interacting with characters. Though you will inevitably end up discussing everything in order to get the information you need, it's fun to have the little extra control of choosing what to talk about.
One downside which I think is worth mentioning is that this game does not hold your hand. The puzzles are hard, and sometimes downright obscure, which means there will be a lot of trial and error (trying to give characters all the items in your inventory, trying to combine a ton of items, running back and forth to various places etc). In my opinion, being stuck on the puzzles and eventually finding the answer is incredibly rewarding and the game is so special that it's enjoyable figuring it out.
It should also be taken into consideration that there may be glitching, I recommend saving multiple copies of the game often, and that the controls aren't enjoyed by everyone. Personally, I really love the tank controls and enjoyed completing the game with them.
Sadly, a lot of people I have recommended the game to haven't enjoyed it as much as me, so I do recommend perhaps watching a playthrough first or just be willing to be open minded and try out a new game. My advice is to be patient and don't expect instant gratification, enjoy using your brain on some puzzles or testing out random combinations.
Overall 10/10 game and will likely be replaying it for the rest of my life.

An inspired take on a hearthstone-esc card game. But ultimatly it is how they try to differ from hearthstone that makes it fail. The reason I wouldnt reccomend isnt because "hurr durr dis hearthstone clone", its much more complex then that.
The game itself obviously draws alot of influence from hearthstone, which isnt a bad system to learn and expand upon, or at least try to do. Let me explain: The actual battles revolve around 2 Lanes of combat, these lanes can come with special bonuses that cater to a certain playstyle, but for the most part you'll be fighting in a game with a standard lane and a "shadow lane" (Stealths any creature played in it). Now while the randomness of the lane system can sometimes mean that a player playing a sup par guard(taunt) heavy deck might win a game they shouldnt have won, it does mostly just add a fun twist to the format.
The game also offers another unquie and IMO terrible system of Runes, 5 to be exact. Players start with 30 hp (which can be expanded upon, i love this feature) and for every 5 dmg that is lost from the initial 30 hp, said player draws a random card from their deck. Meaning that the player attacking is forced to give thier opponent card draw if they want to drop the enemy below 26 hp. This core feature is beyond frustrating, it breaks the meta in so many ways.
For example, lets say player A is rocking his favorite zoo style deck, its a mix of Red and Yellow. Player B has gone with a ramp style deck, in which he quickly tries to gain magika(mana) to play big creatures. Obviously player A will win the early and maybe even mid game, as far as board presseence. However, lucking just behind that next rune lays a card that will wipe most if not all of player A's board. Player B didnt choose to place that card behind that specific rune, the game randomly chose for him.
Runes inherently ruin a would be perfect take on a very good system. The original hearthstone game in beta offered very little RNG, meaning skill was a determining factor behind a win. However the rune system is exactly that, complete and utter randomness. If a player is attacked beyond 26hp then its a complete crap shoot if they win or not. Yes this is technically how card games are meant to be played. The card you draw next turn will always be random, however that is much MUCH diffrent from the Runes in this game. With standard card draw every player is given 1 random event every turn, they can build a deck around this known factor and overcome the randomness through many MANY ways. With Runes... its up to the enemy when you get that extra draw, so the best way to midigate the risk of losing because of 5 dmg is to not dmg the opponent at all.
You see this constantly, players will get the enemy to 26 hp and then stop. Build up 26 dmg on the board or in hand and try to OTK an enemy. Cards that excell at this stratagy are chosen over ones that would suite a more agro or mid game focused meta. Meaning the best deck is the one that can get 26+ dmg on the field fastest... thats not stratagy... its complete luck.
Yes there are many positives to the game. Amazing single player content, the story/tutorial is fun, the extra campaighn is enjoyable, and the single player arena is a blast. But the extra built in RNG kills any form of diverse meta/stratagy within the ranked mode. At least Hearthstone took awhile to get stupid with RNG, this game has had it from day one. I'll proably still play it for the arena mode and any other stories that get added. But beyond those features I sadly cannot reccomend putting any money into a game that otherwise would desserve it.

Very enjoyable isometric strategy / shooter / puzzler. Definitely recommended if you're a fan of Tomb Raider even though it deviates from the 3d norm. I'm not particularly a fan of tomb raider and I enjoyed it.
The story is that a curse/god is released and you play as Lara adventuring your way through many levels then do a boss battle to put the boss back into his prison.
The game consists of shooting, dodging and solving puzzles in roughly equal measure. If you rush the game without the extras you'll have it done in 3 - 5 hours. These are 3 - 5 very enjoyable hours and well worth the price.
The levels offer a challenge but aren't too hard and you can generally figure out what you have to do quickly. This is no hardcore puzzler, it's a casual puzzler. In the levels there are lots of optional puzzles which reward you with various things. There are also optional tombs containing puzzles that reward you with very nice extra things.
There are a few things to help you along, and this is where the strategy comes in.
You can hold 3 weapons plus unlimited low-damage bombs and your spear (which despite being the weakest damage weapon will be required quite often for puzzle solving).
You can hold 2 artifacts and 1 relic, which change the attributes of things like defense, speed and attack in varying ways.
The relic is only activated after you've killed enough enemies without being hurt, or after picking up enough diamonds and when you take another hit, the relic effects are gone.
The ammo is very simple. It's an ammo pool for all weapons (except spear which takes no ammo) and the more powerful weapons use more ammo per shot, simple as that.
This is all introduced gradually, and does sound confusing, but it's easy to master once you've been playing a little while and the artifacts and relics allow you a few options that can turn a battle where you haven't got a hope around.
Checkpoints are frequent which is great. And you can quit the game and it'll resume from your last checkpoint next time.
The graphics get a bit repetative - lots of beige and brown rooms with stairs and pathways. But the action flows nicely and you're so busy either battling or figuring out where to go next that you don't really care.
Lastly the boss fight was thoroughly enjoyable. It wasn't particularly challenging on normal difficulty, but it lasted a few minutes and didn't get stale or boring.
There are four gripes I have.
1. There are times when the aim-assist (you'll need it, really) can let you down, this is especially frustrating with the weapons that take lots of ammo per shot, but mostly it was very good.
2. Jumping gaps can also be slightly irritating if you misjudge the direction of the controller.
3. The mission briefing pauses the game to pop up on screen. This can break a nice flow you have and left me saying "I know, I read it before, just let me play damnit". However, these are necessary so you know what you're doing.
4. It's too easy on normal difficulty.
One last thing. In one screenshot you see spiders. There are many spiders in this game. Nothing really pounces and there are no jumpscares.

note: SAVE OFTEN.  It is enraging to spend half an hour doing things only to die and have to do it ALL over again.  Quicksave is your best friend, trust me.
I had way too much fun with this game.  It does require a good amount of patience and diligence, however.  I think it is safe to say that this is the most hardcore Far Cry game.  It is a tough game, and I loved every second of it, so much so that I played through it multiple times.  Each character has a different first person look to them, so that kind of adds to the replay value believing that you are someone completely different...not some richy rich kid looking for his stupid friends over and over and over...
You choose a character and set out in Africa to take down an arms dealer by the name of The Jackal.  Upon arriving you contract malaria and this becomes a constant worry throughout the game.  You will be blowing stuff up when all of a sudden you need to take cover and recover from the disorienting effects of the malaria.
Pros:
- two open world maps (the second map unlocks after you get through half way of the story)
- beautiful graphics, atmosphere and locations make for great immersion
- enemies are smart.  if they become injured, they will take cover or hide in a bush.  you can hear them panting sometimes.  so be careful.  you might think you killed all the guys...
- gun fights are intense.  don't get cocky.  use cover when you can.
Cons:
- the stealth isn't that great
- you spend A LOT of time running if you are not able to find a car, and you only have so much stamina (remember, you have malaria!)
- no predatory animals
- some people hate the malaria you contract
- an enemy can take a whole AK47 clip to the chest and not die (always aim for the head)
Some of the cons listed above can be improved with a mod called Dylan's Mod.  It improves stealth and enemies should die easier.
If you played Far Cry 3 or anything newer, there is a good chance you might not like this one.  It's slower going and doesn't really hold your hand.  In my opinion though, it is way better than the 3rd.

Pros:

TowerClimb is an action platformer that changes every time you die. The controls are solid, and at first glance, seem extremely simple. However, with enough experimentation and practice, you'll slowly realize a whole spectrum of mobility options available to you. With each technique you learn, new paths to traverse the difficult terrain will unfold before your eyes.
Although most of the story is inferred, this is a game rich with music, ambiance and theme. The slow ardous task of climbing could have made for a very dull game, but each floor offers out new and exciting challenges to overcome. Throw in some different random events and variations, and you'll be thankful for just an extra second to plan your next move.
The core themes of this game are mastery and discovery. Each set of three floors you surpass will lead you to a new "zone" which will have a different visual theme. Watch the trailer if you want to see some of those in more detail. In addition to the mechanics that must be mastered to progress through each zone, each zone has a sort of philosophical theme that you must master as a person, as well. For example, some zones test your ability to plan ahead, whereas others will test your ability to think quickly.
One thing to note is that this is a very difficult and punishing game. Normally, sessions only take less than 30 minutes. By my first 30, I had died probably 25 times. However, as you learn, you will blow through the early stages very quickly. Reaching the first and only checkpoint takes about a 30 minute session, once you've mastered the controls and concepts.
Currently, there is no way to save any progress inside of the Tower. Once you unlock the checkpoint, that's it. People have suggested a save/quit feature, and we may see it in a future patch.
Regardless of whether another checkpoint is added or save/quit gets added, I still fully reccommend this title. There is so much to enjoy and there are tons of unlockables that take quite a bit of effort to achieve.
Easily one of the best features is the local co-op; this game is a blast if you have some friends around to play it with.
If you've read this much of my review and you're on the fence about making the purchase, just buy it. This is one of my absolutely favorite video games ever made, and I know I've been talking about it non-stop for the past three years.

If you like permadeath games, you need to give this game a try. An HONEST try. You will probably feel a little turned off in the first hour or so since it takes awhile to get used to the controls, but trust me, this game is awesome.
I was skeptical when I purchased this game, but I'm extremely glad I did. There's so much content, and it's absolutely brutal. The theme seems to change every three floors, and there's A LOT of floors.
The only downside I know of is that currently, some controllers are a bit wonky when binding the Dpad for movement.
Anyway, buy this.

This is quite clearly the sleeper Indie hit of 2015.
I have been absolutely demolishing myself trying to get past level 12, and have already sunk hours into this game with no sign of stopping. Humbled at the hinted length of this (I hear there are well past 100 levels!?), this game makes Spelunky feel kind.
Kudos to those skilled enough to progress in this game. It's a true test of patience and ability. I would say the game is practically CRUEL in its difficulty, and loves to throw you curveballs just when you feel like you've mastered your current run.
I have the distinct feeling that I will be playing this for years to come.
Purchase this if you share affection in the masochism of the indie scene's most challenging entries. The faint of heart need not apply.

Very hard but very rewarding roguelike platformer. Has very tight controls and well thought out mechanics. You will catch yourself thinking "just one more run" all the time and then see that hours have passed. Very recommended to anyone that likes platformers or roguelikes.

I played TowerClimb quite a bit during its development. I bought it two years ago after seeing KY from Vinesauce stream it on Twitch, and now that it's completed, I can't recommend it enough. It's challenging, but every mistake you make is your fault. It will take a few runs to get a hold on the controls, but they're easy to master. The spritework is bright, colorful, and detailed, but never gets in your way. The random level generation always keeps you on your toes. There's never a dull moment.

While this game does fit the description of a roguelike, there simply doesn't feel like there is enough variety to the content or mechanisms to make the gameplay rewarding enough for the price (especially given the alternatives).  There is no character progression (as far as I observed), no overall growth or goals (aside an album of death types to complete), and once you understand the basic jumping patterns, it all feels awkwardly sterile and repetitive.
As a secondary complaint, the pixel-style graphics, while charming, are a bit muddy and have a fairly limited color palette, leaving a number of enemies and objects very difficult to tell apart.
The music, however, is truly excellent.

What do you get when you throw Spelunky, Kid Icarus, and Dark Souls in a blender?  TowerClimb!
If you like hard games, progressing towards an incredibly difficult goal, precision platforming, rogue-like elements, great music, and charming graphics, then this is your game!  TowerClimb is not for the faint of heart, and that is why I love it.
7/13/16 UPDATE:  This game has only gotten better with time!  Although it's criminal that more people don't love and appreciate this gem, I take solace in the fact that word-of-mouth will only continue to spread.  It's just too good of a game to go unnoticed.
If you're on the fence about the price, just buy it.  Trust me - it will become one of your new favorites.
7/26/16 SECOND UPDATE:  You guys.  This game is so good to start with, but once you make it to the second chapter, your mind will be blown.  Holy ****.  Next level stuff!  I think I like this game as much as I like Spelunky, and I have played Spelunky for about 200 hours in total.  If that tells you anything.
11/27/16 FINAL UPDATE:  This is going on the all-time list for me!  I love it.   The fact that this game is getting no coverage at all is one of the greatest mysteries of our time.

We are talking robots and mechs, baby!  Big ones, little ones, scampering ones -- all shapes and sizes.  All set on a futuristic planet where you are remotely controlling one to do whatever you want.
They start you off with a really nice tutorial and a tease.  The tutorial guides you through all the game areas and lets you try out everything.  You can max out all your skills, buy any 'bot or mech in the game, trick it out, etc.  The catch is, once you're done, everything resets back to zero and then you actually start the game.  If you do the whole tutorial they give you two robots (one that you really shouldn't be piloting yet) and enough modules to get decent starter configurations.  The tease is that they let you drive mechs you won't be able to use effectively for at least a couple of weeks.
You progress through the game primarily by improving your skills.  Skills are initially purchased for a token fee (only really a barrier for the first week or so) and skill points (called EP) and then improved up to a maximum of 10 levels with more EP.  EP are earned over time (so long as you log in every 3 days).  If you're in a huge hurry, you can pay them money to get it to accumulate 50% faster, but it still isn't instant gratification, so most people don't bother.
To start you off, they give you a months worth of EP.  That is enough for a decent start in one area of endeavor, for example, combat or harvesting/production.  If you make mistakes, you have 30 days to undo your skill choices (with some restrictions) and, in time, you'll accumulate enough EP that it won't matter anyway.
If PvP is your thing, there are whole islands with open PvP.  Even if you're not into PvP, it can be worth it to take a risk and mine, harvest, mission, etc in those areas for enhanced rewards.
If PvE is your thing, there are plenty of areas where you can not be attacked unless you take a hostile action.  So, you can ignore the PvP altogether if you want.
There is a death penalty in this game, though.  You won't lose any skills, but you will lose whatever you were piloting and everything it was carrying.  You can insure your ride, but, that really just serves to lessen the blow.  As in real life, they will only pay a faction of what a new one costs.  Again, money comes pretty easily, though, it can take a while to put the configuration back together the way you like it -- of course, that
part of the fun.
The developers are actively working to improve the game.  They release an update every couple of months or so and fixes as needed in between.
Overall the online community is friendly and helpful.  They come across as a little sleepy simply because most people are paying more attention to what is going on in their own corporations (guilds) rather than the public channels.
I do see a few negatives with this game:

The recent 50% off sale must have brought in a wave of people that thought they were getting something other than what was advertised.
Yes, the graphics aren't the best, this isn't EVE or MWO.  They are on par with a RTS game like Supremacy or Command and Conquer.  The system is grindy, but so is every single other MMO.  The UI, once you understand it; and perhaps even do the whole tutorial, is easy to manage at first.  It also gets easier with the ability to remap keys.  The latest patch that allows you to gain EP (skill points) by doing tasks such as mining or fighting, allows people to gain EP pretty quick,
My suggestion is to get in the game, mess around a bit to get your feet under you, and then find an existing "corp" that will help you learn the rest.  There are typically plenty of people willing to answer a question in general or help channel.  This isn't a blockbuster AAA game, and it isn't priced like it either.

Pac-Man makes a huge return in the recently released Smash Brothers.

Good news: It's a great formula, and a great game! Also, nice music!
Bad news: Expecting the mazes from the original arcade games? Too bad, have time trials instead!
WORSE news: The leaderboards are HACKED! For example, for Time Trial leaderboards, I saw a total time for all courses of 00:00.13, in first place! 2nd place was the same, 3rd place was 32 seconds, and 4th place was 11 minutes. You think that's bad enough? Well, you can check leaderboards for the individual courses, and those come with replays! Watch ANY of the top 10, any you'll notice the major difference between the replays and the scoreboard. They should keep an eye on the replays more strictly to make sure the scores match, but they don't. This is blatant proof that there are hackers, and people that just don't want to see anyone else at the top.
TLDR, If you want to be at the top 10 in this game, you're up against hackers, so good luck with that! Just consider yourself lucky if you make it to the A rank. :/
Overall, don't worry about leaderboards (See minirant above for reasons why), but it's an addicting time-waster if you need one!

(This review has been edited following updates to the game which fixed some significant problems)
Originally there was a problem with the game.  There were several scenes missing from the game, at least in the English version.  I was unable to recommend this game at the time because of this flaw.  However, that has now changed, and assuming you're playing on the latest (at the time of this review, which will not be updated again) patch I can recommend this game with only some minor caveats.  This review will focus pretty hard on those caveats, but do remember that they are just that.  Problems, but not game ruining issues, at least for me.
The main draw of this game is definitely its artwork.  Simply put, it is gorgeous.  It has a distinctly anime style to it, though it certainly isn't the super cute "moe" aesthetic that this might bring to mind in some people.  If that isn't your thing than you might not agree, but certainly the artwork is pretty incredible, especially for a free to play game.
Gameplay wise this is a pretty barebones point and click adventure game in an "escape the room" style.  The puzzles aren't very numerous or difficult.  For the most part the task is to just click on items with something selected in your inventory (the interface for this is weird, giving very little indication that an item is selected before you try to use it, but you will get used to it quickly).  Most of the time these puzzles are well designed, as you can either intuit what is meant to be used based on common sense or a clue found in the game.  Such clues range from a literal "clue mechanic” (in which you find information about the "mystery" of the game which you are then tasked to connect the dots on, which are usually obvious), to some cutscenes (especially in the latter half of the game).  So as you can imagine in my original review I had some harsh words at the removal of certain scenes, which made the puzzles into pure guesswork.  This has (apparently, according to the patch notes alone) been resolved, and should no longer be an issue.  Overall though, I would say the gameplay is at best "serviceable."  There's nothing especially revolutionary or interesting to be found her, and almost no real challenge.
The second biggest draw of the game is probably the story.  I have mixed feelings about this.  The game itself is about two hours long at most, and while most of this is spent "discovering" the story through various clues, you don't get very much in the way of exposition until the end.  With the scenes restored the story is simple and easy enough to understand, though you may be left with a few details missing even so.  Nothing to scratch your head and frown over.  However, despite the game presenting its story as mysterious (there's even a previously mentioned mechanic for piecing together clues from your environment to get more exposition, which btw is not optional) a savvy player familiar with these kinds of ghost stories will probably figure out at least 90% of the big twist within the first fourth of the game, about fifteen to twenty minutes.  This isn't helped that, despite adventures games like these often being driven by plot, this game is simply so short that there really isn't room for any kind of plot twists other than the "big reveal" at the end, so most of the information you do get isn't really misleading you into being shocked by the ending.  Nevertheless I like the story.  It’s sweet, in an appropriately disturbing way.  It’s a tragedy the player can see coming, but wish they didn't.
If you had to pay even a dollar I don't think I'd recommend this game.  Everything about it is just shallow.  The mechanics are shallow, the puzzles are easy, and if you want a good story in the same amount of time you're better off watching a movie.  But as a free game (truly free!  It is unfair to compare it to a game with a cash shop!) this game has much higher production values than you would expect.  The writing for what's there is usually on point.  And again, the artwork really is beautiful.  If you're looking for a simple little experience that won't tax you or your wallet, definitely give this a try.
