The Review:
The game has a number of game modes (Deathmatch, Team deathmatch, Capture the flag, Freefall which plays like Minecraft's "Spleef", Defend Which is a kind of PvE Tower Defence ish game mode, Wanted, Zombie and Build 'n' Destroy). None of these game modes are anything new though and with the weapon's system just feels imbalanced and clunky.
The game has an overarching Free 2 Play model. You spend real world currency to buy 'Tokens' or you earn P points from playing matches. The weapons range in costs and cosmetic items generally are only buyable with tokens. The real kick to it though is almost everything has as timer when you purchase it, for example a gun could cost 6k p points for 7 days or 600 tokens for 7 days. This just creates a stupid paywall and inevitable money leech for some of the 'best' guns. Especially since some of the higher shotguns/rifles I saw are 16k p points...
The build mode also featured in the game isn't really anything to truly praise, it's not bad and it works for the most part but it's just a multiplayer map editor essentially. Which I guess can be interesting but if I were playing it for the building aspect I'd prefer to play something else.
Overall I just can't really recommend it to anybody, there are better block builders out there, there are better building games out there and there are better 'arena' style shooters out there. So I fail to really see who this is aimed at or what it is trying to be...

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 is one of my favourite games, it improves on the experience of the first game cutting down the annoying actiosn required to obtain skills through instructors and also has much more content.
The Story is a fun and helps you level up in the early stages and without additional leveling outside of it can sometimes be challenging. There were a few spelling errors originally but they honestly made it more fun.
The gameplay really puts you in control and gives you the opportunity to create awesome combinations of skills and moves. Obviously though there is always going to be someone who just spams the same abilities over and over again giving no chance to retaliate or play the game but that is more a player issue then the game itself.
Online play is quite awful but if you can muscle through the horrific lag you can sometimes have a nice fight. I personally have met and enjoyed a fight or 2 against random players but being Australian never really helps with the lag. This is the main issue with the game, I would not recommend getting Xenoverse 2 if you are looking for online play.
Equipment is really fun to play with giving you the chance to maxmise the benefits of your playstyle. QQ bangs make this easier and also allow for fun costumes when you don't have to worry about their stats allowing for a theme between your playstyle and costume.
Races are very interesting and fun... BUT everyone chooses sayian. The variety in community is sadly non existent which makes it very interesting when even just seeing a majin or namekian walking around the city.
Conton City is a large enough hub world for all your needs and is interesting to explore for the first time. Once it becomes a bit more boring walking around you have the option to teleport to the area you wish to be at. This is glorious improvement from the first game.
Another improvement is the interactions with instuctors. Instructors are now very interesting and easy to learn their skills. The option to maximise your friendship with them is still a thing but atleast it isn't a requirement to progress to the next lesson anymore. Another fantastic improvement, making the game less grindy and lets you obtain the skills you want straight after becoming their student.
Parallel Quests are most of the time fun and give the chance to obtain loot within reasonable time. Sometimes you can get unlucky and might need to play it a few more times than you wanted for the skill or clothing set you wanted but it still lets you test out fun skill sets and combos during that time.
The Expert Missions however are a difficult and fun challenge that takes a few more tries then you would expect most the time (mainly Extreme Malice...). These give good variety when played between any PQs that you might find annoying.
The DLC is very fun and gives nice story quests and PQs to play. The characters are really cool (especially Tapion from the recent Extra Pack 1) and the skills learnt from instructors and through the medal shop are really fun for combos. Some of the DLC does feel like it should be in the base game though (like content required for achievements...).
This game has completely crushed the original game and has added so much more content then I originally expected. Xenoverse 2 is real fun.

The good, the bad and the ugly.
The good:
This game is interesting, and it is "EVE like", which might be a reason for some to give it a try, for others to turn away.
If you join a corp, and if they back you up from the start, the game might become more interesting for you through participating in organized PvP.
There are a lot of different corps in the game, before you join one, read the official forums a bit, to get more informations about them.
You can do harvesting, mining and assginments on Alpha 1 and Alpha 2 islands on your own, to get your first own money.
The developers team seems to be small, but at least filled with people, that are very dedicated to the game, something that is getting hard to find these days...
The bad:
It will take you a lot of real time, to get your hands on those Mechs you were allowed to test (there is your carrot...) in the tutorial.
You only get EP once every day, and you have to log in every 3 days at least to make sure to get that EP package for every day.
Harvesting, mining or assignments is boring work, but will provide you with NIC on your own, to afford your first Mech.
Buying a Mech means, getting enough NIC and finding someone that is willing to sell and transport it to your terminal... forget about transporting anything big on your own in the beginning.
Your first robots won't be able to transport that much, and depending on from where you have to transport your new items, you might run into trouble along the way and loose your robot and cargo.
If your new shiny Mech gets destroyed at some point, doesn't matter if that happens in PvE or PvP, its gone.
Some parts of your installed equipment might be recoverable, there will be a can to loot at the spot where you died, but you will only get a few items back, and those have to be repaired, before you can use them on another robot/mech.
But if your ending happened during a PvP fight, the "spoils" belong to the winner.
If you're part of a corp, you might get a replacement for your loss during "wars" with other corps.
You can of course insure your Mech, but there are costs for that and the outcome wont even cover the NIC you paid for your Mech empty... say thank you to players, that abused the insurance system a while back.
About assignments, you can only choose between "industrial/combat/transport", but all of them are more or less combat assignments, even those that are marked "industrial/transport", there are only a few different assignments, and be prepared to travel slow and far in the beginning to accomplish them.
The ugly:
Other players won't stopp at using any kind of exploit or bug they can find against you. That is of course something, you might find in any other game, but in a "full loot" game, the developers need to keep an very close eye on that.
Last but not least,if you want to get the best Mechs with the best equipment, you need a lot of EP, which will take a lot of real time.
And even if you take the "shortcut" over an EP booster, it will still take you a very long time to reach that goal.
Keep all of that in mind before you consider to buy Perpetuum - then why the thump up?

I would really like to see this game go on and evolve into more, something that is enjoyable for new and vet. players, and for PvE and PvP players alike.
But for that to happen, the developers have still a lot of work to do, sandbox or no sandbox, players expect more from games today.

EDIT: I wish I could leave this game multiple negative reviews. One is not near enough.
I'm sorry to upset the rabid comment raters, but this game does not deserve it's good reviews. It very much deserves this negative review. Anyone who enjoys this game is so blinded by the pretty TES art they don't realize the underlying game is boring, requires no skill, and is designed with no real care or intent beyond separating poor suckers from their money.
Cons:
- The hand size and magicka mechanic are to restrictive, far to often I have no choice in the plays I make. It's like the entire game is on autopilot. There is no choice or strategy to be had once the match starts.
- Over-time momentum in this game is horrifically unbalanced. If a player gets advantage, they can easily keep and build more advantage. Further reducing the skill required. Especially in matches with "Guard" mysteriously disabled.
- Probably the worst balanced 1st/2nd turn I've ever seen. Someone has a SERIOUS hard-on for going second on this dev team. No, but seriously, that 3 time use "compensation ring" gives you an unfair advantage. Player 1 gets nothing.
- The different deck "colors" are often much to disadvantageous to others, often deciding the outcome of the match the moment it starts. This is done to prevent any one from getting to good, but makes bad match ups matter WAY to much.
- The modes for this game are all awful. The story mode is awkward and teaches you nothing about the real game. The other single player modes are designed to burn through your abysmally small gold reserves, and don't even let you use your own deck. Online is full of $$$$$ spewing whales you can't hope to compete with for your first like, 50 hours of playing.
- The drop rate for cards and gold is disgusting, hours of gemaplay left me without enough to buy even one single pack of 6 cards that probably won't match my deck.
- Cards you already own can have their stats and effects changed after the fact, making your expensive purchases you were dumb to make even more useless.
- For how few cards there are, a lot of them are completely useless. It feels like there are just slightly better versions of the same card that are much rarer.... Kinda sorta making this pay-to-win, because they are far to rare for me to get.
- There is a lack of strong and unique cards, so no breaking up the monotony and over-easiness of the autopilot, rock-paper-scissors feel of the matches. Just ever-so-slightly better versions of the same card that are much rarer.
- The story and voice acting are worse than that of the average Skyrim mod. Mostly "Hey! Ahh!! Grrrrrr! It's time to duel!"
- The interface is really clunky and awkward. Cards zoom in and out constantly while performing actions. It's very distracting and aesthetically displeasing. Really wish they just stayed normal sized unless I right clicked them.
- The game seems to be very glitchy. Card timing seems to be buggy, they'll say they only activate after a specific point, but then active before it anyways. Or two cards reacting totally different to one another in the same scenario. In fact, the Cons bellow this I am not even sure they aren't just bugs.
- The game constantly changes the core mechanics, often without notifying you of these changes or their repercussions. When it does notify you, it's still not fun. Hours in, I am still not sure what the 'default' mechanics are.
- The game also seems to "disable" certain effects for certain duels without notification or explanation, rendering entire decks suddenly useless. "Guard" being turned off can render good cards into a total detriments to the user.
Pros:
+ The art's really pretty.
+ The "lanes" and "guard" mechanic is sort of fun when it isn't punishing you for expecting it to exist when it suddenly doesn't without warning or explanation.

The final acts, however, make up for the slow beginning, ending at the perfect spot, making me want to play the part 2. I only wish they could keep the story more homogeneous, in a way that the first parts doesn't feel like filler to the main story.
About the mechanics, the "spirit view" (not a spoiler, it shows up very early in te game) could take a higher role in the game, it doesn't feels deep, it reveals another issue that I will talk about later, and it could take inspiration on similar mechanics, like The Legend of Zelda on how to show paralel universes interacting, it's mostly an x-ray view and adds close to nothing
it has so much potential. The moral choices make a very, very small part on most of the game, which was a feature held high by the devs on their page. It's not bad, and shows up in a very interesting way, but again, it will make no difference during 90% of the game.
And lastly, the controls. It's pretty clear that the game was meant to be played on a tablet, and I had some minor issues controling the character and the camera due to that, If you click a bit over the spot you wish to go, the character won't do anything, not a big thing, but anyone can see it. The big issue is that I feel like the tablet plataform is what limited the "spirit view" mechanic, it could be very different if it was made to the PC plataform.
And that's it. Karma. Incarnation 1 made a great debut on the series even with it's issues. And I say that because I feel like many of it's problems could be solved in part 2, which is what I like about the "3 chapters" system. If part 2 pick up right from where part 1 left off and don't drop it, instead of reseting the story and slowing it down again, that alone will make the sequel a very good point and click game

It's hard to put my words regarding this title because of the high artistic nature of this game. It can be said to a lot of point and click games. Karma is less of a game, and more of an expereince, a surreal, psychedelic experience, certainly a unique and unforgettable one IF you can apprecaite it. Yup, a big "if" right there. Point and click is a niche genre, always has been, and even more so today. It's a genre of hit and miss, especially for a game that takes a more artistic path like Karma. So, the big question is, is it the point and click game that right up your alley?
First, let's talk about the strongest aspect of Karma, and that is it's art and concept. And it is gorgeous, absolutely gorgeous. It's vibrant and bold, every splash of colors are  implemented with a great deal of thought, and how can I say this? It's hard to do such thing, creating a psychedelic-esque universe with bright, vibramt, and even contrasting colors without giving you an eyesore and headache after 5 minutes into a game. In Karma, it just works, it works perfectly.
From the reddish/orange-ish that depict the strange-ness of the area, where the players first introduced to the game make the rather "normal" tribal cave looks 5x more alien than  it is, then moving on to the purple shaded area, that echoes joy and happiness, to the ice-cold and isolated area, and the green "industrial" area. It's something to be expected  in a point and click games, giving each area a distinct feel and look, something that has been a standard of a good point and cliick games, and that's playing with color to evoke a certain tone, mood, and atmosphere. Karma take a bold move by using a vibrant and strong colors, while most use a more subtle approach.
Karma's characters itself are some... things.. that come straight  out of your deepest nightmare yet somehow managed to be so cute and adobrale, it's almost like something that Tim Burton would create, so strange, unconventional, but "attractive" at the same time. As bizzare as the character looks, it has a strong aura of innocence, which fits perfectly with the overall art.
The story itself is pretty simple, you are a spirit whose beloved pink spirit is abducted by an evli spirit, and to defeat the evil spirit, he must reincarnate to a dragon, but instead he turned into a worm named Pip.
Karma's dialogue is told by an alien, incomprehensible language, and thus heavily relies on various speech bubbles that shows various icons and animations, and that won't work without a fluid, expressive animation, and by presenting the right visual cues. And that's what Karma excel. These elements is what carry Karma's gameplay and storytelling. The supppsedly kind of cliched, boring story is greatly elevated by it's astounding viusal narrative. Cute things expressing themselves with cute speech bubbles.
The gameplay itself is more simple than your typical point and click, it feels like most of the puzzles are there for the sake of making the game feels more..gamey. While the puzzle itself falls into typical point and click tropes, they are a bunch of puzzles that ranges from pretty straightforward to absolutely absurd, But the fact that Karma is entirely on 2D, made the puzzles overall easier, since you have far less dimensions to click around and the world of Karma is in a tight and rather confined  space. Sometimes, I just click around the various interactive objects, hoping something funny will happen, and it works at times!
As the name suggest, the gameplay mechanic that differentiate it from another point and click games is the karma system. In some occassions, you are given two options to deal with a problem, that's a good and evil deed. You'll grow spikes if you do evil deed, and that affect the story and how other creatures treats you. That gives the game an additional replay value. The other one is  astral sight, where, in a push of a button, everything around you become more surreal with all these funky colors and you'll be able to see whatever it is on the astral world, and interact with it. Unfortunately, it's under utilized.
As for the sound, I can't say much. The soundtrack, as the rest of the game is just strange but still really great to listen to, and the tribal feel to it fits welll. The characters' voices are funny, and the sound effects are well made. Just like the other aspects of the game, it fits perfectly well and adds even more to the whole strange yet charming atmosphere.
Karma inhabit the recipe that makes a great point and click games..well.. great, and also carry the same mistakes as the ones it borrows from. First, the more abstract puzzles, my biggest gripe with the vast majority of point and click, it feels like it's just a common rule for these type of games to include the kind of puzzle that made me want to tear my hair off, but thanks to the small 2D space, Karma managed to significantly lessen the frustration, to the point where it's actually quite easy, is it bad? Well, to an extent, not really, Karma, by itself is aimed to be a more casual point and click and it did it.
Second, is the story and character. As I said before, the story itself won't be that noteworthy if it's not because of the setting, art, concept, and how they convey it. And while, it ended in a good note, compared to other episodic point and click, they kinda failed to convince me that something grander is going on, though they do piqued my interest for the next installment. Finally, the weakest part is the side characters, due to the length of this game, to the design choices, it's hard to know, or pinpoint the characters, who they are,what their role is, their characterization, and so on. They feel like a bunch of creatures that Pip happened to pass by.And I hope this will be adressed in the next game.
Karma, Incarnation is not a game for everyone, it's a niche game within a niche genre. It's a beautiful, bizzare, and unforgettable experience if you can appreciate the game as what it is. It's biggest strength is certainly the bold and vibrant visual, unique character design, and it's smooth flow both in story and animation. For a point and click game, its puzzles' difficulty is on the lower spectrum, mostly for the better.And it succeed on making a compelling story out of an otherwise generic plot. All in all, Karma, Incarnation  is a game that is more interested in the "Experience" aspect on "Gaming experience", it's gorgeous,calming, and funny, and for the asking price, it's totally worth it.

Farcry 2 is a great game at first glance. Beautiful graphics, decently inteligent AI and plenty of missions.
But diving deeper into everything, it's apparant that it isn't really all that great. There is no autosaving from what I can tell; I just end up saving everytime I do something I don't want to have to do over, or if I spend more than 3 minutes doing anything. And when I forget to save I end up seriously regretting it, or I just quit for the day.
The storyline essentially consists of doing dirtywork for a bunch of forgettable characters that have commercial-like sped up voices as if they have no time to slow down and are on cocaine. And pretty everything the two major factions will have you do involves blowing up something that only one faction has because if we can't have it, no one can - why not just steal it?!? Luckily(?) your 'buddies' will offer up alternatives such as stealing something so you can move the explosion somewhere where it can blow up something else that also deserves being blown up. In the end, all you've really done is generally destablized a country just so you can gain info on some guy who is trying to destabilize the country so you can kill him - beacause he is a bad man... at least his hidden collectible tapes offer some interesting moral thoughts.
The graphics are beautiful, the fire spread mechanics are awesome. Unfortunatly it seems as though the developers thought they could get away with making the game so distractingly gorgeous that players would forget about things like plot and variety and gameplay and....
The missions are all very dull; blow up convoys to unlock new weapons to purchase, kill guys in suits to get diamonds, blow up stuff for factions to get more diamonds, blow up other stuff to help out your buddies(' egos), deliver passports to get malaria drugs.
Traveling in the beautiful world isn't super fun either. Your safest bet is to take a bus anywhere, but then you have to deal with loading screens and the possibility that it didn't really save you any time due to their not-so-perfect placement. The alternative is to follow the roads and run into checkpoints that are still full of guards after being cleared out, or stray from the roads and get your unimog stuck on a tiny rock (HOW?!?) and still have the chance of being chased by guards with grenade launchers or machine guns with extreme catch-up ability. I try to avoid roads and checkpoint at all costs, just because there is no fun in jumping out of your vehicle and quickly gunning them down; it happens way to often and feels like a chore more than anything else.
The enemies are pretty smart, taking advantage of cover to flank you and then unleash all their shotgun ammo on you. Snipers and guided rocket launcher equipped enemies have amazing sightlines and will take advantage of their distance between you to knock you down a few bars of health. It is possible to stealth with the camo suit and some silenced weapons, but once you kill someone, there isn't much you can do but hide.
Finding and earning diamonds is your gateway to new weapons, equuipment and upgrades, which all help substantially. It is worth finding diamonds that pop up while traveling or gunning down bases, but with all the diamonds you'll get from missions, it isn't really necessary to go hunting for the last few hidden stashes unless you just have to have every weapon.
The level design itself is very good, but they should have focused more on making the enemy AI and travel mechanics more player friendly. If I had looked into the developer's office while this game was under development, I'd wager a guess that the story writers and graphic designers were the serious driving force behind this game while the programmers just threw together some code without giving it a real playtest beyond looking at the trailer material. I'm giving this game a 65/100 mainly because it isn't as fun as it could be.

Guns you find lying on the ground are always rusted to hell, and guns get from the store (which gives you an infinite supply to replace yours with) are always in mint condition. Obulis is a very simplistic puzzle game - break the links and use physics to your advantage, to get colored balls in their respective goals. Progression is granted through achieving 'stars' - each level has a certain number of stars it awards, which you can use to unlock levels. The hand painted backgrounds are gorgeous, and keep me surprised: they're a part of the game, interactive and useable as props to bounce your balls off (get your mind out of the gutter).
There is a lack of punishment to 'failing' a level, which in and of itself is both a boon and a blessing: on one hand, levels become less about skill and more about retrying until Lady Luck is on your side. On the other, being punished for levels that you will repeat upwards of ten times would quickly wear a player out, and make this game a bargain bin discount.
And really, that's what Obulis is: a game that's a fun in it's own right, but you'd never pay full price for it. Pick it up on a sale if you enjoy games akin to Fantastic Contraption, Cut the Rope and World of Goo.

Waka Waka + Bullet Time + Crack= Pac-Man Championship Edition DX+
It's just your typical Pac-man... with a twist. Instead of moving freely around the map collecting pellets and avoiding ghosts, the goal now is to follow a predetermined path of pellets while collecting fruit/objects and racking up a long chain of ghosts along the way. There's 3 difficulties to choose from before (Easy, Normal, Expert) which will determine the speed you'll start the round with. The speed will also increase as you make progress without getting killed and decreases if defeated. Two new features are Pac-Man Bullet Time (Yes that's a word) which slows down time if the ghosts get too close and bombs which send them to the box in the center of the screen.

Score Attack (5/10 min)- Try to rack up the highest score in the set amount of time
Time Trial (Short)- A Challenge Mode of sorts trying to collect fruit in a short period of time
Time Trial- A combination of all the challenges with the same goal
Ghost Combo- Trying to create the longest ghost chain possible
14 Courses
8 Visuals + DLC
Achievements and Medals

So, going into this, I read a few reviews. I almost had my hopes up for a good discussion of depression,. But I was disappointed rather quickly.
Using mental illness as a quick one-stop way to culture "horror" is cheap, and only succeeds in making this one of the edgiest games I've had the misfortune in playing. If there was some sort of story that was supposed to be shown, I sure missed it, because any hints were vague and don't connect with any other part of this "plot". What was trying to be said? I couldn't really find anything that this game was trying to accomplish, besides proving that the creator had little to no understanding of what he was even doing.
To be honest, I felt nothing but slight disgust through the entire playthrough. Nothing was particularly funny, and the mundane tasks accomplished nothing to further whatever sort of storytelling that had been attempted.
I mean, perhaps someone who had no experience in depression would find this adequate and humorous. Perhaps furthering stigmas and using mental illness as a edgy trope in your horror games gets you somewhere, but it didn't even do the shadow of that for this game.
Putting together a hodpodge of "creepy" tidbits (i.e. eating your pet shrimp, eletrocuting a man that probably doesn't exist), does nothing but confuse the player and make sure there isn't a coherent order of events. They have nothing to do with each other, and even less with whatever leads the main character to commit suicide. Maybe if you had actually spent some time developing the character, it would have made more sense, and actually well represented those with depression (I deal with it, and I can assure you that this is the farthest from how depression actually is, to be honest.), while keeping the integretity of the project. If there was any integrity to begin with.
Now, I'm not sure what I expected out of a ten minute free game, but at the very least I expected a little something more than a borderline offensive little game that acts like it can make humor even in the light of the main character committing suicide. But hey, to each their own. I'm mad I wasted my time playing that game, and then more of my time to write this reveiw. Nonetheless, I felt like sharing my opinion.
Before I conclude, I feel like addressing the "Don't play if you're depressed" thing I've seen in many of the reveiws. While I appreciate the mirage of people caring about warning others who could be affected by such things, it isn't really needed for this game because it's actually just that terrible. It is less unsettling and more disgusting than anything in the way things are handled. Not that that matters, obviously if a depressed person sees something that deals with depression they'll "freak out". (That last bit was sarcasm, by the way.)
TLDR;
If it wasn't for the bitterly and terrible handling of the subject matter, which is written like an edgy middle schooler's self-insert fanfiction, and the complete breakdown of the general conventions of story-telling (like, actually having a plot), maybe this game would vaguely resemble a game that is worth considering to waste ten minutes on. Don't get your hopes up, since it only shows what happens what happens if you write about something you don't know absolutely anything about, like mental illness, for example. It's not humorous, accurate, or stirring. It's just a disappointment.
Nothing special even by free game or free fiction standards. A noble attempt that fell short.

Karma is a point and click adventure game where you play as a light thing. You're chilling in orbit with your love when suddenly this monster comes out of nowhere, eats your love, and goes down to the planet to devour it. It's up to you to beat the monster and save your love! Unfortunately, you're incorporeal, so you'll have to be born in order to actually interact with anything. Hey, that dragon's egg looks pretty sweet! I bet you could beat the monster in no time as a dragon! Oops, looks like the egg you chose wasn't actually a dragon's egg, it was a kind of a slug-like creature's egg. Looks like you'll have to do this the adventure game way, by grabbing stuff and solving problems.
As an adventure game, this game is very simple. You'll pick up objects (by eating them), and if you come across a place where you can use them, the game will let you know. Otherwise, the game will display a question mark that you can click that makes Pip shrug. I had to look at a guide a couple times (I usually do with adventure games), because sometimes it was unclear if I could click on something or not. For some sections, Pip will eventually get a lightbulb that you can click on that will tell you how to do the section you're on. IE, some creatures are playing music around a fire, with you on the drums, the lightbulb will tell you that you're supposed to click the drum when the fire's sparks make a picture. Otherwise, you're on your own.
There is a good/evil system in the game (hence the name, Karma), where at certain points you'll be given a good/evil choice, usually in the form of kill/let live. Doing evil deeds will change your appearance and apparently how beings react to you, but I haven't tried this out yet, since I went for a good playthrough my first time.
Another system is your astral site, which lets you see into the astral plane which will help you solve some puzzles.
The game's also a little buggy. It crashed on me a couple times, and one time I think a flag wouldn't trigger, so I had to play a section over again. But that was OK, because the game autosaves your current progress and has a list of previous section saves.
Also of note is that this is part 1 of a 3 part game, so while you do get an ending, the larger problem of saving the world still remains.
So, why should you get this game, which sounds kind of eeeeh? First, the graphics are amazing. The backgrounds are hand drawn, high quality and gorgeous! All the little colours and details are a feast for the eyes. The animations are fluid and just fun to watch. In every area, there'll be something irrelevant that you can to click on just to see an animation. Click on the snowman in the arctic level to watch him slowly shed his snow to find out he's a skeleton! The plant level has practically a million of these little things to click on. You can tell that a lot of love and care went into this game. It's really refreshing to have something smoothly animated and highly detailed after all the pixel games out there.
Second is that this game's style is really, really weird. Your main mode of transporting to different areas is a living elevator-like thing with many eyes on stalks. I mean, look at those screenshots! The nice thing is that it's weird in a good way, not creepy or disgusting way.
Definitely go give this game a try if any of that sounds interesting! Give the devs some love so they can make episode 2!
Beautiful looking. Good music and ambient sounds too. Pretty short though and there should be another episodes. Watch a more comprehensive review here

It's undeniable that Karma Incarnation 1 is what many would call, "Gamer Art" but what does that mean exactly? Is that just a fancy term for grandly illustrated/unique art? Does that mean lack of depth to gameplay? That there is a deeper message embedded in the game? Well, just like real art it is all of these things, but at the same time none of them. I know, that is a very Yoda like answer, but if you'll humor me lets break it down for you.
Let's start with facts, Karma is a point and click adventure style game. When I think of comparable games to Karma, titles like The Journey Down 1&2, Armikrog, Violett, Tormentum-Dark Sorrow, and the much beloved, Grim Fandango. Point and click games are a very prolific genre with all sorts of different styles, animation, stories, themes and gameplay elements. Karma is no different, with its captivating animation and psychedelic use of color. The control scheme is universal and just about anybody could play these games.
Karma is a love letter to Tim Burton, one can see hints of Beetlejuice and Edward Scissor Hands during their twisted trip though the worlds of Karma Incarnation. Personally I also see bits of one my favorite shows from the early 90's called, Aaahh!!! Real Monsters. There are grotesque smiles and our hero devours items, and sometimes characters whole. There are monsters and nightmares around every corner. At the same time, there is sort of an innocence to it all and something that is truly unique and beautiful.
The games main selling point is the art, you can't take your eyes off of it, and why would you?
Fans of the genre will see all the typical tropes of the point and click style game. There are puzzles; some abstract and others pretty straight forward. For the most part Karma takes a much easier path when it comes to puzzle design. I never really had to stop and think all that much and I always knew more or less what I was doing. Keeping you on track has been handled masterfully, despite the fact that the game has no dialogue by describing the entire story or what to do in comic book bubbles. This kept me on the path I needed to go, but I didn't exactly always understand why I was going there. I will touch upon this in a bit.
The things that Karma uses to differentiate itself from the heap of point and click offerings out there with are its moral choices and Astral sight. The sight, upon activation creates this bubble of funky colors and lets you peer into the spirit world. This helps you accomplish a few puzzles, and gather some achievements. While very neat looking, I wish this element had been played up more as this ability ends up being rarely used. There are only two times its use is integral to the story and the first is when you actually get the ability. It just seems like more could've and should've been done with this idea.
Other areas either could've been more explained or mechanics thrown in. At one point you receive a strange vessel/phone booth from Bill and Ted's Excellent adventure that takes you to other worlds. Upon using you zap yourself into another world, you pick up an old blind guy and drop him off. Why? I have no idea. This is just one of the random weird things this game just kinda throws at you and basically leaves you with more questions than answers.
The story itself isn't anything too complicated, evil spirit takes your pink spirit girlfriend. You, good white spirit boyfriend must find a way to restore balance, defeat evil and save pink spirit girlfriend.
It's simple but at the same time lacks definition in character development. I had no idea who anybody was. I know that the experience is more important in this instance but felt that I would've cared way more if the slightest effort to let me in on things was attempted.
There is an inventory system in the game but it currently doesn't play any integral part in the game. Items are automatically combined for you and the game lets you know when you are missing something to advance the plot. You can click on items and see a comic bubble of its possible uses. This was helpful at times, but personally I never used it.
The difficulty of the game is something I think will divide people, as it borders on being too easy. This isn't always a bad thing though. I have had to pull my hair out when playing games like Grim Fandango.
As you move through the story you are presented with "moral decisions" and are usually given one of two choices. These decisions pretty much always end up being kill or be nice. There are occasionally moments you growl or incapacitate someone but it took me a bit to figure out that these don't affect your morality. If you are inclined to pointless murder that is really the only thing that is going to change anything. What does it change exactly? You grow spikes, and people react to you differently, ect.  The story certainly learns toward goodness, as it is constantly giving you moments to redeem yourself and lose spikes. As this is the first of three parts of the story, I will warn you that story wise, there is no clear difference in destination by taking the evil path. You are rewarded with some end scene differences, but to actually "win" the game you need to play with a good alignment.
Another thing to note is Karma Incarnation 1 has that it has "1" at the end for a reason. The game ends on a "To be continued" and fades to black. This is hardly a problem for me as other amazing games like The Journey Down have taken similar approaches. Art, music, and game design all take money and plenty of time. They are worth the wait. Just something to keep in mind for factual reasons.
Other areas such as replay and innovation are not necessarily the focus. You can play the game twice, as a little meanie and as a hero, but you are going to get a maximum of six hours of  gameplay. As mentioned before just keep in mind what you get for playing the games morality to its darker side. The true innovation here is bringing such vivid animations to life. One area I personally would've love to seen a bit more improvement on would be transitions. The game tends to hang or re-adjust your character during moments of interactivity. You can especially see these from transitioning from one area to another in the same world.
I can say this a thousand times over, and the game has the awards to back it up, Karma is a beautiful game.
Musically the game is playful, its use of tones and rhythm are as intregal its use of color. I didn't regret spending any time with Karma Incarnation, I wouldn't of played through the game twice just for kicks. There are enormous amounts of detail in every single world you visit. Little interactions that serve no purpose to the story, make you feel that this universe is strange and full of wonder.
It is no small feat to take ones imagination, so vibrant and strange, and translate it with such skill and fluidity.
That is why people are drawn to these types of games, they are gateways into other peoples mind. Some other games can boast of having all sorts of intricate features and complex stories but sometimes, a picture is worth a thousand words. Karma Incarnation 1 bathes in these types of moments, where you just can't look away. Ultimately, your mileage is going to vary with this title, but that stands true for most point and click games. There is a fervor when it comes to these types of games, people still sing praises of Monkey Island, the hotly debated Broken Age, the recent revived Kings Quest.
Simply put, there is something that speaks to people when it comes to these types of artistic point and click games. Karma Incarnation is no different. It has its faults, but so do the other titles mentioned in this review. I personally cannot wait to see what wicked worlds we will get to grace in the next part.

I loved the first game but the second one is not only better but also has more things in it.
Pros:
A larger hub world with more things to do.
Sidequests that are worth working for.
The ability to transfer stuff from the first game such as skills, outfits, and more (Note: Some CANNOT be transferred over)
Better combat and smoother combos.
Visuals look the same mostly, meaning if you could run XV1, you can run XV2.
Level Progression and Money Earning made much better and smoother with the addition of Super Souls.
QQ Bangs pretty much make clothing stats obsolete, meaning you can use one and wear anything you want.
New characters such as Zarbon from the Frieza Saga among others.
Music actually sounds like it is from the show. Somehow the OST makes Metal Cooler.
Story mode does not have a mountain sized difficulty spike like the first game.
Being trained by a character does not require you to do something ridiculous a stupid amount of times. (♥♥♥♥ you Hercule)
Biggest pro: Character customization is at an all time high, making it a very fun experience of just creating characters or putting characters from other franchises into the game.
Cons:
QQ Bangs are pretty hard to make one perfect.
Unlocking every character is still hell.
Some skills require lots of fighting and levelling up and finishing the story (I hear getting Golden Frieza Form for the Time Patroller Frieza is not worth it in the end.)
Some of the voices for Time Patrollers are really bad, especially with the female voices.
The story of XV2 sounds very similar to the one in XV1. Time is being altered. However what they don't tell you is that it's almost the same. You go through every arc from Z and barely any of it is different. There are some major differences late game (Such as the part where Vegeta is in Hell, you then have to fight Janemba to get him out) and there are some minor differences that I think are really neat (Ginyu transfers his body into Vegeta and Trunks instead of Goku and, thank ♥♥♥♥, your character.) However, most of it is almost the same.
Biggest con: Making a new character requires you to also play the story all over again, unlike the first game where you can immediately do whatever with your new Time Patroller. It's a slow, sluggish process, and worst of all, you also can't choose your characters you made in the fight screen, and characters do not scale to your level. Better max up on all of them, because if you face someone who's level 80 and you're only 47, expect a quick loss.
Personal likes:
Vegeta's BADMAN Shirt is in the game.
A lot of skills and Souls are a lot easier to get.
Lots of ease of access, Quality of Life, and improvements on the old system of XV1
The fact that the game is still getting updated.
Personal gripes:
While this isn't the specific one, XV2 on the Switch is the catalyst for Dragon Ball FighterZ to be ported on to it (Hence why I call them Demandai Namco.)
TP Shop is pretty tedious and irritating because of it being available only a few days of the week.
Overall:
I'm not much of a fan of Dragon Ball. However, I can't ignore that this game is very fun, hectic, fast paced, and also pretty robust at making characters. There's some improvement needed to be made when it comes to some decisions (Why do we have to do everything again with a new character?!) but even then, it's a fun game.

Five good reasons to buy West of Loathing:
1) Sophisticated, earnest writing. The game knows when to be funny and when not to be. And while toilet-humor abounds (both literally and figuratively), the jokes are never truly idiotic, nor meanspirited.
2) Freedom of choice. Do you want to solve the puzzle or bypass it entirely? Do you want to engage in every subquest or barrel through to the ending? Do you want to kill every enemy you see or attempt a pacifist run? Anything is possible, although certain choices do have meaningful consequences. Different kinds of people will enjoy the game in many different ways and on many different levels.
3) Charming music, art and animation. And there's a continual stream of new stuff to see from beginning to end.
4) Cheap price. There's at least $20 worth of content in here.
5) Trustworthy developers. This is a small indie company with ~15 years of experience that actively engages with their playerbase. They want to generate DLC and make new games. Good sales will directly effect their ability to do so. If you, the consumer, don't actively support them, then no one else will.

Normally I don't write reviews, but I felt compelled to write one for Brick-Force because of the way the game changed after beta was over.
I found Brick-Force while browsing around back in 2012. Back then it was in its closed beta form, and looked very promising. I received my key to enter the game and I couldn't wait to play! I had an amazing time on BF and for a very long time it was the only game I played consistently day-to-day. I actually still have the playlist on Spotify that I used to listen to while playing BF. I play it sometimes just for the nostalgia.
Don't get me wrong, beta-BF had its problems, mainly lack of content and rented guns. The biggest deal for me was the complete lack of 'pay to win' in the game. The lack of content was no biggy (it was closed beta, so it was to be expected). If one played often getting guns was no issue at all. I believe that guns were rented on a weekly or monthly basis, with monthly being a better deal. I personally don't have an issue with guns being rented out, as it makes testing a gun before buying it long-term a much easier task.
So, I played BF and had a good time, then beta ended. The update came immediately after. This update cast a dark shadow over the citizens of BF. It brought forth a cash shop with weapons purchasable only with premium currency. These weapons were so ridiculously overpowered that even the most talented players on the game, including myself, couldn't compete. You cannot simply kill someone that has a rocket or a grenade launcher when you only have a rifle.
TL;DR Brick-Force was a balanced game with a friendly community before the final release, which turned it into a steaming pile of garbage.
IMPORTANT NOTE: I haven't played this game since witnessing the pay to win model I saw at final release. From the other reviews I've read I don't think it's changed much.

Vindictus is a fast paced game with a very good combat system which I will talk about below:
The combat system consists primarily of left clicks, right clicks, wasd movement, spacebar, and a combination of these. For the most part, left click is a basic attack and you usually build up your attacks by spamming this button. Then, after a certain amount of left clicks, you right click which does a "smash" attack depending on how many left clicks you've done. There're also a bunch of active and passive skills to play with but I personally believe these are sorted out quite well in comparison to other MMORPGs.
While Vindictus is a fast paced game and the combat system is amazing for an MMORPG, it does suffer from a flaw in that it is NOT free roam. For the most part, this game has different towns that you can explore and talk to NPCs, etc. However, the only time you can do combat is if you enter dungeons (on your own or with other players) which are repetitive (the layout of the dungeons is very repetitive, especially within their specific dungeon groups) and even if you want to "grind it out" by spamming a single dungeon for EXP, which you might have to do when you're stuck on certain dungeons, it's annoying to have to face a completion screen every time you finish a dungeon, especially if you're trying to gain EXP as quick as possible. Essentially, the combat system loses meaning because this game is not free roam (albeit it may be harder to program this smooth level of combat into a free roam MMORPG, I don't know anything about gaming programming).
The graphics of the game are excellent as well. While there are some visual "uhhhhh... what is this, a 2D game?" moments (such as some of the looks of the skill actives), the characters are stunning. I'll just say it but this is definitely a game for perverts. If you're seeking women, the girls all have maximizable breasts (albeit not monster sized, le sigh) and the physics on the jiggling is pretty good as well. Furthermore, you can purchase swimsuits or lingerie for them as under armor which is begging to be revealed when your armor is destroyed in a dungeon (which actually happens, when your in-game armor is destroyed it reveals their undergarments). If you're seeking men, the men of the game have amazing body structures and you can have any kind of man you want as long as he's buff and tough. Characters classes are gender locked.
That got a bit weird near the end there, but as you can probably see now, this game is amazing in terms of visuals but misses out in gameplay opportunity because it's not really a free roam, it's mostly just a 3d third person dungeon crawler which pretty cool skills and stuff. Unfortunately, the community is sort of slipping as well, which makes the game not as fun because a lot of the cooler looking bosses require 10+ people to fight it at once.

For this review I'm going to put in as much of an unbiased approach as possible. Needless negativity towards the game helps no one and reviews are meant to help people decide whether they wish to buy it. That being said, let's get into the stuff the game did right.
- Fighting Mechanics: In good conditions, this games fighting is fluid, intricate, heavily skill-based, and satisfactory. With friends or matches with decent connection and a decent human being this games fighting truly feels great. As you play more online you become better, learn the mechanics, learn when to strike, how to perfect block, etc. When you and another skilled player fight, the game truly gives a sense of every movement matters and I have fond memories with friends or others having a good couple matches.
- Character Customization: You can customize your character in a huge variety of ways, whether that be appearance, clothing, abilities, stats, you name it (except for aura color). The customization can truly make your character feel unique and the combos on each race and gender truly feel different and help diversify your playstyle.
- Attacks: Your character can chose from hundreds of attacks, leading to great variation. After you've learned how your character's combos work, you can create amazing combos that range from just causing insane damage, to flashy and stylish.
I've said some pretty positive things about this game so far. But there is a reason the review is negative. But before that, let's look at the mediocre content of this game.
- Storyline: The story in this game is just that, mediocre. Xenoverse 2's status as an RPG is laughable at best saying as you get two choices in the entire story and neither cause any effect. The storyline is almost directly copy and paste from XV1 with the final boss from last game literally in the game files.
- Optimization: The optimization from last game is noticable but lacking in many places. Many bugs still litter the game that only get patched till months after they are discovered.
So finally, let's get to what truly hurts this game.
- Fighting Mechanics: You might be saying, "Hey, he put this in the positive, how can it be negative too?" Well remember that I said in GOOD scenarios, the combat is great. Well sadly, bad matches aren't just common, they take up a majority of this game's matches. The game rewards defensive behavior, which in itself isn't bad, hell the top of ACTUAL SKILLED players are defensive. But this game's love towards defense makes it easy for people to abuse, essentially giving people that play cowardous just to win a easy time. This game's reliance on Stamina is so insane that it's if you ever want to play decently in the combat scene, you need to have a HUGE amount of Stamina. 8-10 bars is almost always a requirement just to even be considered for winning just because of Stamina insane ability to get out of basically any situation.
- Attacks: This game's attributes are very double-edged. Let's talk about basic combos. As a Male Earthling main, it's easy to see my fellow Male Earthlings abuse the broken status of this class. The recovery from Stamina Breaks, (not regeneration, the speed at which they can move after being stamina broken) is insanely fast for Male Earthlings. Not only that, but Male Earthlings have a easy stun within their combos which allows the ability to launch ultimates with almost no risk and a unvanishable Stamina Break which allows them to easily cheese. And the acutal moves. While there is a diverse and interesting assortment of moves in this game, there are a lot of moves that can be easily spammed with almost no way to punish them. And these broken moves are ususally left that way for months until they are finally fixed.
- Optimization: Unfortuanetly the game's optimization from XV1 can't be said for it's online. The servers for this game are atrocious, with the "lag-free" games coming once in a blue moon, if you wish to play online often you have to be prepared for a multitude of different moves and combos to simply not work, or somehow work just due to lag.
- Community: This community is full of nice people, however, not only are there less than 1,000 GLOBAL concurrent players, but the nice people are constantly overshadowed by the dark side of the community that makes GTA Online look like a community of cherry elderly people.
- Dimps: The publisher for this game is inept at best. They don't listen to the community and if they do it's months after a broken mechanic or move is fixed, and this fix usually brings in more broken♥♥♥♥♥♥ The DLC they publish is not worth the price they charge, with them adding 2 characters per DLC and every 2 DLC getting a short cinematic and 30 minutes of story. Dimps simply doesn't know what they are doing.
Conclusion: This game's core truly is good, and I wish that I could recommend this game but I can't. I've had an insane amount of fun playing this game and it's given me many great memories, but the negatives just outweigh the positives here.

I have no sense of humor whatsoever due to Asbergers and I still like this game. Even if I don't/can't understand 95% of the jokes and have never played Kingdom of Loathing, (it's prequal/spinoff/whatever), it was still a good RPG on it's own. It has puzzles, some of which are the standard simple RPG fare, and some of which require a lot more time, effort, and brainpower to figure out. It has a story that makes sense in the world of the game, and for the most part, what you need to do to progress is fairly simple.
This is a standard turn based RPG and the combat system doesn't do anything new. Not that it needs to. If you've ever played any turn based RPG you'll recognise this system. Combat is very simple. The characters with the highest speed stat go first, basic attacks are free, and the rest of your skills require action points, of which you have a limited number per fight, and action points reset every fight.
Interacting with things is easy and basically involves running up to whatever object you want to interact with and press 'e'. Sometimes you might need to go into your inventory and use an object. The actual interaction part is very easy. The actual steps you might need to take to complete some quests in a certain way is more difficult, but that's part of the fun.
Choices exist. There are multiple ways to finish quests, multiple ways to build a character (even if it's the same class), and many other choices besides. The game is directly influenced by how you do quests and which people you help. It is entirely possible to be locked out of some choices/quests if you kill everyone you see as a potential threat immediately. It is also possible and likely that you'll wind up selling off a load of junk and someone will ask for some of it later (not that you can't get more of it, but still.)
An exploration game where you go out into a monochrome 2d world and find things. There are set locations on your map, you go there and that area is rendered for you. There are random events as you travel between locations, but they don't have an actual area for your character to walk around in and find secret passages or anything. There are 'secrets' but they are usually fairly obvious from a visual standpoint, even if your character doesn't immediately have the skills needed to get into that area.
Forgiving in terms of optional puzzles. You can complete the main game and most quest chains in towns no matter what. You may not do it as cleanly or optimally as you'd like, but you can do it. It is, however, very possible to screw up several puzzles or very off-the track side quests (either by doing the puzzles incorrectly or by killing people you need), in such a way that you can't complete the puzzle or can't get the best ending for a quest. For example, minor spoiler in the first half hour

I don't think there are many people out there that haven't played PAC-MAN and most of those who have love it. Namco brings us all of our fond childhood memories back whilst making the game feel new and refreshed.
PAC-MAN DX+ is essentially the same PAC-MAN game you played years and years ago with a lot more re-playability and added content/features. For those who have never played a PAC-MAN game you play as PAC-MAN, a yellow blob with a mouth, trying to eat as many pellets/dots as possible before being caught and eaten by the ghosts who patrol the level and chase you down.
There are multiple different stages in Pac-Man DX+ and each different stage has a different difficulty and layout and well as multiple modes that can be unlocked as you progress. You'll start with basic time trials where you must collect 3 fruits within the time limit and once you complete these you'll open both new maps to play on and new challenges for your current map.
There are various different ways to play from Score Attack where you must compile as many points as you can before your time is up, to Ghost Combo where you must eat as many ghosts in a row as possible, to time trials where your goal is to clear a specific amount of pellets within a time limit.
In the main game modes rather than aimlessly collecting as many pellets as possible your aim this time to to clear the screen of all of the pellets to spawn a bonus fruit. When collected this fruit will increase the speed you move at (increasing overall difficulty) and spawn the next group of pellets.
The pellets are spawned into a formation for easy collection and are often surrounded by ghosts who will only wake up once you pass them and then they will begin to chase you down. Keeping true to the original Pac-Man you can still kill these enemies when you collect a super pellet as this will turn all the little ghosties on the level blue allowing you to eat them for lots of delicious points.
Whilst collecting pellets you'll also find yourself coming across a few bomb powerups that, in exchange for losing a few levels of speed, will allow you to activate at any time to remove the line of ghosts following you. Though these will be sent to the respawn point to immediately respawn it can save you the trouble of being caught out and having to respawn yourself.
The greatest part of Pac-Man is the freedom to change the design of your level (aesthetically) along with yours and the ghosts skin and the background music. It stops the game from feeling repetitive because combined with the vast choices of maps, you'll have the choice of looking and hearing different things. Though this is DLC and I am rather anti-DLC I feel the prices are reasonable for what you get and I managed to snag mine all on sale.
The only thing I feel is missing from Pac-Man DX+ is some form of online or local multiplayer. Games like this would greatly benefit from this, alas, no signs of it yet. Also the achievements are pretty basic and they can be 100%ed rather quickly which is a shame because the potential for challenging achievements was obvious. Neither of these actually detract from the game though, they are just things I would have liked to seen implemented myself.

Championship Edition DX+ is a updated and remixed version of the hit XBLA original, and further refines a arcade classic to something completely new and fresh. And it's Pac-Man. You should probably play it.
It’s easy to see why this game was a massive hit during the early XBLA/PSN days. It took the Iwatani-designed version of the original Championship Edition and went even farther with it. Despite the naming, it is a much more different game from the original Championship due to it’s much faster pace, brand new mechanics, and loads of new visual/audio features.
Pac-Man Championship Edition DX throws away the survival element from the 1980 classic, and instead incentivizes players to follow patterns and munch on hundreds of ghosts for the best score possible. Eating the fruit upon eating all of the pellets on one side will rotate and change the other side of the level into a new layout, repeating in the same order until the timer runs out. It's very now a score-em-up, with you earning the majority of your points from collecting a massive chain of ghosts, then eating all of them with a power pellet.
And this is the one major change that fundamentally redesigns this game as a whole. Various ghosts are now spread across the level layouts, and you can get them to follow Pac-Man, following his every move. You want these ghosts to chase you, as you’ll eventually be able to rack up insane amounts of points by picking up a power-pellet. But don't worry, because if you feel overwhelmed or are trapped, the game allows you to use screen-clearing bombs to push the ghosts back, which can be valuable to those who want to save precious seconds, or slow the in-game speed that rapidly increases while the game is playing. Basically, the game has almost a huge amount of new mechanics that's easier to show than talk about.
And these new game mechanics aren't the only major differences with CE DX. The game’s speed now ramps up even faster the more pellets you eat, there are even more levels, time trial modes for each level, and a lot more visual options to change. Because of this, Championship Edition DX ends up becoming a surprisingly fresh experience that introduces a different type of way of playing Pac-Man, albeit one that isn’t exactly going for what made Pac-Man work. It’s main challenge is now pattern memorization, rather than the effective movement + score hunting present in the original. But like the original Pac-Man, it doesn’t get old that easily!
Presentation-wise is relatively decent, although the game’s main menu is terrible in both its visual look and actually accessing things with it. The music is nothing special but is definitely well-made for the game, and the visuals for the game can be customized. You can change the game’s artstyle and music in any level, and it’s a really unique and cool feature, although some of the visuals are very hit-and-mess (Ghostly Adventures *cough cough*).
DLC is a bit of a mixed bag. While the concept of new levels and themes are cool, some of them were just done poorly (Ghostly Adventures *hack* *wheeze*). They’re better picking up when the game + DLC pack is on a absurdly good price, because otherwise I wouldn’t see myself buying all of this.
PC Optimization is relatively normal. It can probably run on a typical Windows Tablet since the original PC version was built off of that, so it’s definitely not a big worry. I wish there were more resolution options, however. Leaderboards are unfortunately quite the mess, so you can forget playing for the best score online since everyone has already blatantly cheated their way up.
There’s really not much to talk about when it comes to this game though. It’s Pac-Man. It’s Pac-Man, Championship Edition DX, a completely different and fun way of playing the game. And you should play it.

My Jeep had smoke coming out of the hood. It was driving slower than it usually did. I had just survived a brief skirmish with some trigger-happy hooligans, but with one quick grenade under their Jeep, the problem was solved. I saw a guard post up ahead.
"Piece of cake." they said. "Clear it with that shotgun you just bought." they said.
I jumped off the Jeep and pulled out my shotgun. It really was a thing of beauty, a work of art: it was ornately decorated with what looked like silver on an African or Brazilian wood with a reddish hue. The sound of it being fired was pleasant but aggressive, kind of like gangsta rap or heavy metal. It was brand new, and I decided to affectionately name it Ho Lee Schitt, after my adoptive father from China.
I sprinted over there. "YIPPIE-KI-AYE-AY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥S" I screamed, in my best Bruce Willis voice. "It's time to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥up!"
But then, I realized the harsh reality of what was coming. I had limited ammo, and no grenades or molotovs. I had the rapt attention of about five heavily armed people who I had just threatened. The fastest means of escape I had was a small dune buggy on the other side of the shantytown. Malaria struck me almost instantly, and I heard the roar of a Jeep's engine. I felt a sharp pain overwhelming the entire left side of my body as I lost my grip on Ho Lee Schitt.
"HO LEE SCHITT! NO!" I screamed. and then I felt myself get smashed to the ground by a heavy steel chassis, and everything went black.
But not for long! One of my buddies that I met earlier just came to pick my pathetic, lumpy body off the ground and save my life.
"Ol' buddy, ol' pal!" I was able to whisper to myself with all of my energy.
Everything went black again, but only for about five seconds, and I saw my buddy, courageously fighting off my enemies with a rusty old pistol like the independent woman she was.
But then I noticed her struggling. She left my body on the ground as she had to load her last magazine into the pistol. Odds were, one of us or both of us were going to die, and I was determined that if any of us were to die, it would not be her.
So I bit the bullet and looked at my leg. It was surely broken, but there was a bullet hole in it, too. I couldn't just leave this bullet there, so I performed a brief, gory self-surgery with my trusty machete. She noticed that I was coming to, and decided to give me the gun.
"Go!" I yelled. "Go into that house over there for safety. If one of us dies, it will not be you!"
I saw as a bullet was fired into my left arm, which I noticed was also probably broken. I shoved my finger through the bullet hole and pushed the bullet out, leaving a clean hole in my arm.
I collapsed to the ground, like some fat guy in dire need of doughnuts. I realized that I was going to die of malaria-induced lead overdose if I didn't get up, so I popped my last malaria pill and stabbed a morphine syringe in my arm.
I arrogantly belted out, in my best James Brown voice, "AND I FEEL GOOD! I KNEW THAT I WOULD NOW."
Then I saw it. Ho Lee Schitt was in the hands of one of my enemies. I was furious. I ran over to the dune buggy I saw, jumped on it, and ran him over. He was crawling on the ground begging for mercy. I crouched next to him, and shot him once in each eye. Ho Lee Schitt was mine again.
I ran over to the two remaining men, murder in my eyes, and my tongue stretching out longer than Ace Frehley's. They each had a clear shot on me, and i risked getting buckshot all over my face and the "PIMP" tattoo on my licker; however, their rusty shotguns jammed, obviously because the bullets were scared of me. A quick bang here and a quick bang there and there were two less idiots in the world.
"AND I FEEL NICE! LIKE SUGAR AND SPICE!" I continued to sing. The adrenaline was coursing through my veins, and I jumped up in the air and high-fived my buddy. We stayed in the air for a full minute, like the end of some Van Halen concert on MTV or the closing credits of literally every episode of The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air. I was Born To Run, and against the better judgment of my friend, I kept rolling on that Thunder Road to the place beyond that guard post: New Jersey.

Killer Is Dead is an anime-style unforgiving hack n' slash adventure rpg where you play as Mondo Zappa, a rad man with a katana and symbiotic weapon-arm. You will, from the get-go, be fighting a handful of enemies and venturing around levels in order to confront their bosses, and this game really turns it up on the bosses. The combat is ultra-fluid and very responsive, a mix of Shadow of Mordor and classic hack n' slash. You can sidestep, roll, backstep, and move as fast as you can think to. This is exactly how anime katana combat should feel, allowing you to counterattack and mix in other moves in order to fight groups of enemies. As you build combo, you do more damage and move quicker, so there's incentive to not get hit. When you parry an enemy, you go into a button-mash where you hack them up and build combo by smashin that attack button. The plot is fantastical and unexplainable, and very enjoyable.
Additionally, it's also an anime h-game where you go on dates with cute girls and do a fun minigame where you look at their boobies while they look away. 5/5

I have to say, I was looking forward to this game, being an Elder Scrolls fan myself; however, this game exceeded my expectations. The game takes quite obvious inspiration from Hearthstone, with the same "attack and toughness" kind of system as Hearthstone, as well as the increasing of mana based on your turn or cards that give you mana (Well, it's called Magicka here). The major differences that I see between the games is a total of two things - There are two lanes, adding another element of strategy to it. The second lane also cloaks your creatures for the turn they're summoned (unless they have guard) so you can't attack them for a turn. The other major difference is runes and prophecy cards. Basically, whenever you lose 5 HP under 30, you draw a card and it will break a rune. For each rune broken, you draw a card. If you draw a card with "prophecy" you can immediately play it to the field with no cost. I personally am a big fan of the direction that they took with this card game by sticking pretty close to Hearthstone.
I also like the direction they took in increasing your drops of play styles dependent on which race you pick. It means that you're not picking an avatar for looks, but for the strategy you would rather go for, adding a sense of extra choice in the game, and immediately progressing you further towards that playstyle of your choice.

TL;DR: Elder Scrolls Online is a very impressive card games with unique yet familiar mechanics and I look forward to where it goes in the future.

Championship Edition DX+ is a updated and remixed version of the hit XBLA original, and further refines a arcade classic to something completely new and fresh. And it's Pac-Man. You should probably play it.
It’s easy to see why this game was a massive hit during the early XBLA/PSN days. It took the Iwatani-designed version of the original Championship Edition and went even farther with it. Despite the naming, it is a much more different game from the original Championship due to it’s much faster pace, brand new mechanics, and loads of new visual/audio features.
Pac-Man Championship Edition DX throws away the survival element from the 1980 classic, and instead incentivizes players to follow patterns and munch on hundreds of ghosts for the best score possible. Eating the fruit upon eating all of the pellets on one side will rotate and change the other side of the level into a new layout, repeating in the same order until the timer runs out. It's very now a score-em-up, with you earning the majority of your points from collecting a massive chain of ghosts, then eating all of them with a power pellet.
And this is the one major change that fundamentally redesigns this game as a whole. Various ghosts are now spread across the level layouts, and you can get them to follow Pac-Man, following his every move. You want these ghosts to chase you, as you’ll eventually be able to rack up insane amounts of points by picking up a power-pellet. But don't worry, because if you feel overwhelmed or are trapped, the game allows you to use screen-clearing bombs to push the ghosts back, which can be valuable to those who want to save precious seconds, or slow the in-game speed that rapidly increases while the game is playing. Basically, the game has almost a huge amount of new mechanics that's easier to show than talk about.
And these new game mechanics aren't the only major differences with CE DX. The game’s speed now ramps up even faster the more pellets you eat, there are even more levels, time trial modes for each level, and a lot more visual options to change. Because of this, Championship Edition DX ends up becoming a surprisingly fresh experience that introduces a different type of way of playing Pac-Man, albeit one that isn’t exactly going for what made Pac-Man work. It’s main challenge is now pattern memorization, rather than the effective movement + score hunting present in the original. But like the original Pac-Man, it doesn’t get old that easily!
Presentation-wise is relatively decent, although the game’s main menu is terrible in both its visual look and actually accessing things with it. The music is nothing special but is definitely well-made for the game, and the visuals for the game can be customized. You can change the game’s artstyle and music in any level, and it’s a really unique and cool feature, although some of the visuals are very hit-and-mess (Ghostly Adventures *cough cough*).
DLC is a bit of a mixed bag. While the concept of new levels and themes are cool, some of them were just done poorly (Ghostly Adventures *hack* *wheeze*). They’re better picking up when the game + DLC pack is on a absurdly good price, because otherwise I wouldn’t see myself buying all of this.
PC Optimization is relatively normal. It can probably run on a typical Windows Tablet since the original PC version was built off of that, so it’s definitely not a big worry. I wish there were more resolution options, however. Leaderboards are unfortunately quite the mess, so you can forget playing for the best score online since everyone has already blatantly cheated their way up.
There’s really not much to talk about when it comes to this game though. It’s Pac-Man. It’s Pac-Man, Championship Edition DX, a completely different and fun way of playing the game. And you should play it.

What a wonderful game, but the sad fact is the community didn't stick around for too long.
Epigenesis is a very interesting title. It's a sports game mixed with fast paced parkour FPS. The goal is simple, you go to the center of the arena to capture a ball which you need to take to the opposite side of the arena and score goals, after each goal you get a seed which is used to set up boosters, defense systems and turrets to fight alongside with you. When you plant the final seed on the opposing hoop the game is instantly won.
The title looks alright for the most part and maxed out it runs almost perfectly, apart from some slight FPS drops when the action gets too fast.
The arenas are built so you have to jump around platforms to get to where you need to go and sometimes the jumping is really tough to control, sometimes you miss your mark and sometimes you go overboard.
The game has a single player mode which has five arenas to play through and you can choose how many bots are on the arena on your team and on the opposing team.
This game is great and is a ton of fun too, but there is one major flaw and that the game is completely dead. Unless you have a friend to play alongside with you except to play solo only.
The game alone is still pretty fun, but with people it would be even wore fun.
I would love to recommend this game to everyone, but unless you have a friend willing to play this with you, there's no point in buying just for solo play as you will play through every arena in an hour.
Final Rating:
5/10 - Buy it if you have friends who play it
