Epigenesis presents a promising take on the next few hundred years: no grim future centered entirely on war, no post-apocalyptic earth where Darwinian human instinct has taken over; instead, humanity created the most popular sport in history, some strange hybrid of Basketball, Soccer, and Unreal Tournament.  It's also an interesting case for why "e-sports" doesn't necessarily have to conjure up images of multiplayer battle arenas and first-person shooters, but that more traditional (albeit fictional) sports can exist in that space alongside the likes of Dota 2 and Counter-Strike. I really like what Epigenesis represents: it's an innovative take on traditional sports that still provides the adrenaline rush of something like Quake or Unreal Tournament, in a well-produced package that you rarely see in games fresh out of Steam's Early Access.
In Epigenesis, two teams face off in an attempt to plant a ball inside an enemy's goal more times in ten minutes than the opposition across a platformed ravine. The arenas aesthetically resemble something out of Tron but play like something out of Quake. Each player is given a non-lethal laser with two modes: rail (an instant, focused beam which pushes enemies back a small amount) and shot (a mode which fires a missile-like projectile which travels slowly but produces an explosion that pushes back enemies a lot).  The gun is a key part of both offense and defense -- pushing an enemy back and causing them to fall off a ledge or preventing them from landing on one in the first place spells instant death, producing a 5-second respawn timer. In addition, hitting an enemy who's in the air with your melee attack sends them straight downward, and if they fail to land on a platform? Splat.
In order to score a goal, a player has to pick up the ball from the middle of the arena, take it to the enemy goal, and toss it in. It's simple, but when presented with power-ups like "smokescreen" (which creates a cloud of smoke over a large area for a few seconds), along with arena-based hazards (like the desert maps' Twister, which pulls players it catches high up into the air), it gets complex and interesting. Upon scoring, a player is given a seed, which they can plant on one of the unoccupied platforms, which in turn spawns a plant, a kind of "turret" which produces effects ranging from firing projectiles which slow enemies, to creating a shield in which players can hide. In addition, each plant provides the entire team with a buff to either jump height or speed. Each player also has a gauntlet called a "meth-glove," whose use is two-fold: the first, called "methylation," allows a player to power up a plant; the other, called "demethylation," allows them to cause an enemy's plant to wither and eventually become inactive. It's here where the strategy of Epigenesis starts to shine: its rules are deceptively easy to learn, but when other humans are thrown into the mix, their collective strategies coalesce into something truly spectacular.
At least, that's what I assume happens.
You see, Epigenesis' community is dead. And when I say "dead," I don't mean "there are a few full servers," I mean there are two or three people playing the multiplayer at any given time. It's disheartening, because playing against the AI only provides a challenge until you're out-thinking and out-pacing them, and with a complete lack of single-player campaign, its appeal only lasts for so long before you're wanting something richer. I only got to play a single match against real people, and it wasn't even a full house -- there were four people (two on each team) with the other six slots filled by AI. I'm sure that if I'd gotten to play more of the multiplayer component I would have enjoyed Epigenesis way more, but unfortunately, that's what often happens with Early Access titles: people play them obsessively for a few weeks or months and move on, and then when the game comes out nobody is still playing it.
THE VERDICT
Epigenesis is a strong case for why e-sports doesn't necessarily have to be entirely composed of the likes of League of Legends and Unreal Tournament. It is, unfortunately, a product of the all-too-common disease I have taken to calling "Early Access Syndrome," in which a game's community is essentially non-existent on official release. I'd stay away unless you're buying the four-pack with the intention to play with other people you know, or are content playing against bots -- not because it's a bad game, but because the community just does not exist.

A strange arcade style puzzle brawler where you and three buddies cosplay as various disney and pizar characters from a handful of franchises. Sadly, "Universe" lacks many other franchises characters.
EDIT: Stars guage power level, and they apperently persist and stay with ther costume. I consider that an honest mistake because it's certainly not explained.
Gameplay is a brain-numbing objective based brawler where you do what the game tells you and beat up anything that gets in your way. Enemies are actually fairly sophisticated. They infight, they build traps, they steal objective objects and run away with them; This makes having a lot of enemies on screen extremely entertaining rather than irritating like other titles. Even though you won't see them the first time, there are models for every type of unit for every theme. Playing with a lot of friends will thus probably bring out the hardest enemies in the highest quantity.
Every area is composed of three stages. The third has a boss. There are three areas to a theme. You unlock costumes by completing each area, with many costumes being unlocked by simply replaying levels.
After awhile you start to get bored of the uniform design of the levels. While every level tries to introduce new mechanics some of them begin to get more intricate. I call it a puzzle brawler because that's what it is, you lack alot of mobility other such games have. There are jump puzzles, and they tend to be very irritating as some manuevers the game expects you to do often have a high chance of making you respawn. Even with a few deaths the game rarely gave me any better than bronze while solo.
Get it cheap, especially if you have friends that enjoy drinking. Buy a few packs of beer and drink every time you respawn, that'll make the game far more entertaining. The lack of real story and limited selection of costumes can be a drag, and the gameplay tries to be inventive but the core player abilities are just dull.

Ok, So I of all the new Disney games that were recently released on Steam, I have to say that Disney Universe and Epic Mickey 2 are my favorite so far with Disney Universe on top.
You start off picking from a very generous choice of costumes for your character, from Mickey Mouse,  Donald Duck, Tron, A Bug's Life, the Princess from Aladdin, Angelica from Pirates of the Caribbean and a bunch more. And you can find a ton more costumes throughout the game to add to your costume menu and use.
This game feels almost like your playing a LEGO video game but the amount of fun you will have here is intense.
The graphics detail is awesome and the sound fx and background music really gets you into the game. It's really good.
The cut scenes are really well done with a lot of humor and makes you look forward to seeing the next cut scene. Lot's of fun!
The gameplay is what definitely makes it for me. You run around beating up mischievous and evil little minions that are so bad they even do bad things to themselves. LOL. As you clobber them left and right, they drop mickey tokens that you will collect for unlocking the costumes you find throughout the game.
There are some moments that just cut right into the action when an arcade machine drops into the center offering you some kind of crazy challenge. Here is an example: I was fighting a bunch of minions with my sword having a hell of a time BAM BAM COMBO COMBO and all of a sudden an arcade machine drops from the air in front of me and I run up to it and activate it and it gives me a challenge to kill all the minions with a laser gun, arcade style. O.O
Oh hell Yeah! PEW PEW PEW. I was blasting them left and right! HAHAHA!!! xD
Oh and MOUNTS! Yes, you will find mounts everywhere from a cannon you can ride around and blast everything and ride animals like a sheep with a power slam or a pig with a toxic fart and a lot of other animals and things to mount and ride and find out what their skills are.
POWER-UPS! You will find power-ups all over. Some turning you into a tornado wiping everything out in your path or turning you into a jackhammer to drill into the floor and gather Mickey tokens or turning you into a snowman to zap and turn everyone into ice blocks. There are a lot of power-ups.
Also, you can level up your main weapon and every time you do it transforms into something else. I had a paintbrush and then it transformed into a magic wand and then a sword and when I got the Jack Sparrow costume, I soon after got a power-up that changed my sword into a parrot. LOL.
There are also a lot of other fun things you will find like throwable objects, bombs and water balloons and other fun stuff, and there are things that will turn you into a zombie. O.o
I experienced all this within the first 30 minutes of gameplay and I am still finding more and more fun power-ups, challenges, secrets, mounts and costumes and who knows what else will come.
This game makes great use with the 360 controller as well as Keyboard and Mouse and is a lot more fun if you have a friend come over for local co-op. It would have been so much more fun if it had online play but with the amount of fun I have with Disney Universe, I can't complain. :D
So should you get this game? Heck yea! This game is a lot of fun! xD

I have very mixed feelings about this game. I have played it through to completion only once on hard.
The world was interesting and the pacing was good. I thought the rpg system was pretty decent though it had flaws but no more than is typical. Some of the abilities were very interesting. I felt the lore was good but perhaps the setting could have been explained a little more. Some things were left a little too vague.
The combat however sucked for one severe flaw. I don't know if it was the difficulty I played on but the percentage to hit had no relation whatsoever to reality. By the end of the game I considered a 70% to hit value to be more likely to miss than not. Only at 80+% does hitting become likely. It made the game very difficult to predict and took out a lot of strategy. When your character can miss 9 70%+ shots (0.0009% chance of happening) in a row you end up reloading just off of bad luck. Then some spells don't work or are unreliable. Like mindwipe is meant to stop them attacking you but doesn't always, there is a charm spell that is also bugged. It felt like a buggy mess really and it sucked because combat in this game could be fun if not for how broken it is. Doing it again I'd play this game on easy, I didn't find it difficult but it is annoying so just set it low and breeze through the combat.
This game also has a terrible difficulty spike. By the end I had developed a strategy where I would generally not take a hit in battle using my shaman character. But the last battle just seemed really tough and frustrating because my characters couldn't hit anything. I never like that where the difficulty just zooms.
5.5/10 for me.

This game is a great concept backed with a deep in-game coaching system, and an excellent database editor, however it falls on its face mainly due to a plethora of game breaking glitches, and a poor English translation.
The game is largely text based, with you weeding through a series of menus, which is to be expected. The menus are easy to navigate, and it's a breeze to find specific players through the deep searching and recruiting system. However, these menus and some team objectives can be confusing sometimes, as the English translations don't quite make sense sometimes. The music and sound are laughable, as the menu music is 8 songs by the same guy, and the in game sound is literally 4 poorly done sound effects on a slate of awkward silence. You can manage one pro club and one national team at one time. There are tons of playable leagues to select from, with differing rules and competition formats. However, I've found that the game slows to a crawl if your simulation is less than 4 stars in speed. Managing the team(s) can take quite a good deal of time, as you'll be spending your time not only managing and coaching the team, but also dealing with finances and international scouting. The scouts are good for getting some ratings on players, however they seem to misjudge potential horribly, even with a five star scout. During the live simulations, you have the options of viewing the action in a 2D 2k simcast live-esque view, or a very janky and basic 3D view, which I actually preferred. You can choose from a wide variety of options for your offense and defense, and even run specific plays!
PBM2017 has many deep customization options available for the player. You can edit everything from players, to coaches, all the way down to the team's financial budget and what languages the player speaks. If you think of it, you can probably edit it, which is really awesome. However, I  found it a bit strange that to upload a custom logo, you had to do it thorugh some file digging, a peculiar omission when you can edit just about anything else you can think up. I found myself mainly using the editor to correct the weird translations to names. You'll be seeing a lot of "Dava Millur"s and "Carlas Boozars" for players with English names, partly I believe to avoid a lawsuit from NBA players. These tools are definitely use-at-your-own-risk, as I've discovered a bunch of problems that seem to have resulted from this tool.
Player interaction is limited to "scout player", "contract offer" or "add to tracking list". Players don't seem to have negative chemistry, and will stay happy if you keep the training balanced. Progression is really good, and you can definitely tell the difference when you train a specific attribute. I even boosted up a few players in my humble euro league team to the point they eventually got drafted by the NBA.
Bugs: As previously stated, this game is full of bugs, which unfortunately the developer has not responded to as of one week. I'm the type of person that is ok with a few crashes here and there, and other weird, funky stuff once in awhile. So here is a list of some that I've had occur to me personally with about a week and 60 hours played, and you can decide for yourself whether you want to chance it.
Game Breakers:
The Training Glitch- Basically, you can't train your pro players, and your players are constantly out of shape and exhausted, which makes the game pretty much unplayable by the time winter rolls around and you're dropping game after game due to exhastion and slew of resulting injuries. I think I triggered this by accepting a national team offer from Cyprus, as after their season started and ended, I still cannot train my pros.
The Competitions Edit Glitch-If you use the editor to look up a competition and subsequently click on that competition page, even if you don't touch anything, will cause that league to be marked as 'non-playable' for the remainder of the season. If this happens to be the league that you are in, you will be immediately removed from the team, and unable to sign anywhere until the next season.
The Created Teams/Players Glitch- Created teams will always have 1000 seats, even if you enter a higher number on the creation page. This can lead to you being fired due to lack of revenue. Furthermore, about 4 out of 5 of the generated players on that team were unable to be signed to any kind of contract, basically making them 1-year dummies. This happened when I first started my game.
Common Non-Game Breakers:
Players from the opposing team (and on a rare occasion, yours) will make a ridiculous full court 3 pointer before the end of quarter buzzer. This happens super frequently, as I've even seen it happen twice in one game.
Music will randomly stop playing in the menus after about 3 played games. Usually means the game will crash when you play your next game.
Constant random crashes, despite being well above recommended system specs. Be sure to save OFTEN.
Endless loading bar sometimes when entering a game.
Trying to add affinities to players in the editor will cause the game to freeze, and subsequently crash.
When signing or re-signing as manager, your (owner I guess?) will take control of the roster and make a bunch of really high offers to random guys. If they do sign before they re-sign you, you will have to pay off these bum contracts. They will also take the liberty of extending these ridiculous contracts for 1-2 more years at the same or higher rate. This can get you fired for bad financial management, especially when combined with an 1000 seat arena.
If you waive a player with an expiring contract with an extension before the offseason (usually because of the above problem) you will have to pay him off, then he will be back on July 1st and you will have to pay him off again. This can sometimes kill more than half of your yearly budget.
Can't extend contract for a player with an expiring contract that is on your team, similar to the Created Team Player glitch. Other teams seem to be able to sign them however. These players in particular seem to cause the absurd contract signings by the CPU mentioned above.
Euro League 3 has playoffs and a playoff format, but never has any playoff games.
Ex-NBA scrubs that have been playing internationally for years will not even consider offers from similar teams "there's no way Carlas Boozar will sign with a GL-1 team!" then proceeds to sign with Berlin afterwards.
A bunch of pro and national teams have no coach, despite me adding a bunch of them in the editor (without assigning a team) and most are still free agents.
National team prospects seem to be random, not based on actual ratings. A bunch of decent 3-3.5 star players were from Cyprus (the national team I'm coaching) and offered me a bunch of 0-2 star players instead. So my team was a bunch of free agent guys, one signed guy, and a bunch of 15-17 year olds, since you are unable to choose prospects freely as far as I know.
In 3d simulations at 4x speed, the ball will often get stuck in place. Your players will then play with an invisble ball until the next sound effect is triggered.
Simulation dialogue says "____ shoots it" and then "Defender commits foul", yet the ball is taken from out of bounds. This happens constantly, I would say at least 10 times per game, every game.
Can't extend contract for a player with an expiring contract that is on your team, similar to the Created Team Player glitch. Other teams seem to be able to sign them however. These players in particular seem to cause the absurd contract signings by the CPU.
Anyways, in summation, this game had huge potential that is spoiled by endless glitches and a poor English translation. If the developers had waited a bit longer and ironed out these kind of issues before launch I would give this game a 7.5/10. However in its current sloppy state, I have to give it a 4.5/10, as I don't think any game should have you worried whether your

Let me start by saying that I owned the 2015 version and Cyanide's football game (out at the same time).  I bought them together and was so disappointed with the products that I vowed to never buy another Cyanide game.
Fast forward 2 yrs or so and after researching the game for a bit, I hesitantly took the plunge.
I can honestly say that after 37 hours of game time, I'm very pleasantly suprised with this one.
The game world is huge (which for me is good and bad).  I love the depth but on the other hand, when you have to spread your efforts to do so much, you miss details.  Its the dilemma of either doing a lot of things good or a few things great.  I do think that they've done a lot of things good.  The other drawback to having a huge world is that the larger the world, the slower the sim time.  I'm playing NCAA and NBA and sim times are pretty slow.
I really enjoy the statistical history presented.  The only problem that I have with this, is it doesn't seem to go past the past 10 - 20 years and isn't completely accurate.
As mentioned, I'm playing NCAA and NBA.  The recruiting  process could definitely be tweaked a little and there basically isn't any difference between powerhouse programs and low end schools.
Navigating through the UI (user interface) is very frustrating and slow at times and the American Basketball leagues don't seem to function or be as realistic as some stand alone College or NBA sims that I have played but in this one game for about half the price of one of those games, you get the entire basketball world.  That's pretty amazing.
I haven't had any issues with crashing
Overall, if you are a basketball fan and enjoy sim games I definitely recommend you try this game.  (Never thought I'd be saying that after the 2015 mess)
You just need to do it with the understanding that the American worlds aren't as refined as some other individual games provide but you have (a very functional) basically an entire basketball world to become part of.
I am very much looking forward to updates/improvements and seeing what this franchise can become.
Also the steam workshop group seems to be very involved and at least 1 very detailed real world mod (Crowder I believe) is in the works.
There currently are 3 mods in the workshop.  I have subscribed to all 3 and have successfully pulled from those mods to update my playable database.

my biggest issue is the server stability, and times you have to wait when doing anything outside of a battle.  it literally takes up to 1 minute or more on a fiber optic (or equivilant) connection for any action to be completed, be it selling items or storing/swapping/equipping items.  be warned if patience is not something you were born with, this game will likely push you farther away due to this one simple variable.
seeing the server at its most optimal (instant responsiveness when dealing with anything outside of battle) , and then being forced to deal with 1 minute wait times on something as simple as getting rid of trash loot, make doing simple tasks multiplicatively take longer - completely kills it for me.  and it shows in game as well (less people online when server stability is compromised).  i play on East server in NA just so you know.
it is deffinately worth giving a try (assuming you are not in a location that is region locked), so play in the middle of the week if you want the best server stability (maintinence is usually wednesday mornings)
reasons to keep coming back:  gameplay mechanics and unique bosses
reasons to quit completely:  total lack of server stability the longer the week goes on without maintinence.
you have been warned...
edit: it honestly seems like random DDOS attacks, because the server lags uncontrollably sometimes at non-peak gaming hours.  patience is still key.
edit2: i found out that i had a free internet upgrade the week i posted this review.  come to find out some of the issues very well were on my ISP's end, but when everyone i am playing with is getting the same wait times, you know it's not just you.  this was often the case in the past.

I'm actually enjyoing this over Hearthstone, which I didn't expect.
It really feels like you can build a deck you enjoy and still do well, rather than just following the meta. This is because of the attribute system (Strength, Agility, etc - similar to colors in Magic), and also extra game mechanics like Prophecy cards (can be played for free if you draw one after losing a rune), runes (you burn a rune every time you lose 5 health, and then draw a card), support cards (effects persist across turns) and the 2 different lanes which sometimes have different buffs. There's so many combinations you can key off of for those mechanics, the variety feels endless.
I've seen some reviews mentioning RNG. I am not versed well enough in CCGs to know how this game fares against others as far as RNG is concerned, but I feel much more in control of what's going on on the board. When I lose a game, I in general feel like I made a mistake, rather than I got cheated by something cheap. No cards that I've seen so far seem ridiculously cheap (I'm sure there are a few, but I don't recall any.)
Also, one thing I didn't like about HS is that each class has its own level, so you can spend 1000 hours on Paladin, then switch to Rogue and feel like you're starting all over. I know the classes don't mean much in HS (beyond level 10), but I don't like feeling like I lost progress. In TES: L, your level persists no matter what deck you are using.
Arguably the best part of TES: L over HS is the solo gameplay. The storyline is actually really fun. The story is enjoyable, and each fight comes with some type of unique dynamic. In HS, playing the Adventures is just a grind for the meta cards (feels like it to me anyway), but I actually played the TES: L solo game just to follow the story and enjoy the different fights. If the story was 100 hours, I'd play all 100 hours. I don't think I could say the same for HS.
Solo Arena is awesome. You have 9 fights, including a boss, and your prize gets better the further you go. You also can lose 3 games before your arena is lost, which is nice. I expect to play a lot of solo arena to prepare for the ladder.
Ultimately, I felt like I wasn't accomplishing ANYTHING in HS if I wasn't playing the ranked ladder. I have played 0 ranked games in TES: L, and I feel like I've accomplished a lot in just a few hours.
Also, part of my enjoyment is that "Me Like" factor. Sometimes you play a game, or watch a movie, or try a food and just have an overwhelming sense of "Me Like". You maybe can't put your finger on it, but you know for some reason that you are being drawn to the game. I had that with this game the moment I opened it, and I've had that feeling about once every 10 minutes since. Something about this game is just drawing me in.
I'm not even a huge TES fan. I played about 60 hours of Skyrim, and piddle-paddled around in Oblivion and Morrowind for a few hours, but I'm not a big TES nerd by any means. But something about TES: L is making me have major "Me Like" syndrome.
Give it a play and see if you get the "Me Like" feel as well.

A great game. It takes all the good aspects of Hearthstone while dropping all the bad ones.
It's actually pretty skill-intensive, and not all that luck-based. It's pretty fast-paced and full of action, but it rewards smart play.

Rewards are fair and generous, and it's pretty easy to farm cards and gold to get a decent deck.
The game is still relatively recent, but it's been evolving in a great way, and with every new release it gets a lot more interesting.
It still lacks a bit of polishing, specially to make the interface more pleasing, and a couple of other improvements, but judging by the way the game is progressing, it shouldn't take long.
A definite must-play if you like card games. Especially if you're tired of Hearthstone and its RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.

My personal preference on pros and cons though I still recommend the game.
Pros:
Much more fluid combat and easier to perform combo strings as well as longer combo strings and they're even hidden combos that you may or may not come across.
For Saiyans, the SSJ transformations no longer consumes your Ki Meter, instead it's just a flat out transformation with the appropriate power boost. It's a nice change of pace to use SSJ at your leisure though you still need the required amount of Ki to transform. But you can no longer use your abilities at will like in XV1, so you still need to build up Ki to use your abilities.
Saiyans can now go beyond SSJ with SSJ2 and SSJ3. Values are still the same as they are in XV1, SSJ 1, 2, and 3 give you stronger basic melee and strike super/ultimates while Super Vegeta 1 and 2 increase the amount of damage your Blast Supers/Ultimates do.
Story Mode doesn't feel cheap like in XV1 where villains have Super Armor, so you can fight as you like though if you're not strong enough you will get taken out farily quickly but regardless, Super Armor for villians is out in Story Mode.
XV2 also introduces a very large open world HUB ( Conton City ) to explore and you can fly ( beat the Frieza Arc to unlock flight in Conton City ). So no more small 3 section TokiToki City with loading screens.
CaC is what it is, I just wish that females had more female-esque hair instead of varied short hair, also would've been nice to have females use the ponytail that males can use. But CaC does offer alittle more customization options this time around.
Cons:
If you're using a transformation during a fight in story mode and it goes to a cutscene, your character is suddenly in their base form and when the cutscene ends and puts you back in the fight, you have to transform again. in XV1, if you were in a transformed state your character would still stay in that form before, during and after a cutscene. Alittle nit pick of mine.
Hair still doesn't spike up when you go Super Saiyan or SSJ2. Again another little nit pick of mine.
Still can't color all the iconic clothing like Gokus Gi or Lord Slugs clothes.
They're no difficulty options for the CPU. It becomes very easy once you know how to use combos and the new stamina break feature.
Online is awful as always.
The developers created an Anti Cheat for those of us who decided to mod the game and play offline which is a very cold slap in the face. We're never going to see our CaC's get the SSG, SSB, SSJ Rage, Rose, SSB Kaioken, SSB KK x10 and of course Ultra Instinct transformations like you can with mods. The game is a shell of what it could be and mods have helped many of us give us that one DBZ game we always wanted.

+The graphics are decent.

+There is different types of vehicles, which we are able to fix.
+A good variety of weapons and upgrades, that we can unlock with our gems. The gems are gained through missions or searching.

-As I said earlier, there are some bugs that stop you from completing the game.
-Literally three quarter of the game consists of driving. The map is huge and you have to drive to everywhere or use the bus. But there is only five bus stops in the game. They are at the four corner of the map and one in the middle, so not very convenient.
-The story isn't that interesting. Classical civil war story. (I can tell because it is my second playthough, I played it once when I was younger)
-The voice acting is horrible. The accents are poor and everybody talks very fast without intonation. So it is a little bit hard to understand them, if English is not your native tongue or if you're not very competent.
-There is two factions in the game, where we get our missions from. We do missions for both of them but even the soldiers of the faction, that we currently do the mission for, attack us because " it's a classified mission." Well, I could say okay for a couple of missions but every freaking one of them is the same so it doesn't make sense and becomes annoying fighting the both.

I mean it is good because it gives a challenge but it starts to get on the nerves after a while.
As I said earlier, I recommend the game even though I couldn't enjoy it that much but I feel like everybody should at least give it a try to see for themselves. I really don't know why I recommend it. :)

Let me get this out of the way first, I am not a huge Basketball fan. I went into this game with very low expectations and I think it was for the best. Pro Basketball manager plays pretty much like a normal  game, you start out by customising your character and then you are given a team to control. Pro Basketball Manager 2017 has a pretty steep learning curve. You are not served everything like food on a platter.
Pro Basketball Manager 2017 introduces you to its mechanics as you make your way through the game and more options pop up. You can strategize the overall coaching style and are able to make minute changes while you are still inside a game. You are able to easily control even the smallest of things.
The UI in Pro Basketball Manager 2017 is clean and inviting to play. Pro Basketball Manager 2017 is a pretty solid management game if looked at what it offers in terms of gameplay. Not everything is good with it though.
For starters, I wasn’t able to play the game for a long time due to its horrible latency issues. The load times are very long and there is a horrible time lag between click and respond. Everything felt clunky and it was a pain to sit through that and try to concentrate on actual management of the game. That was when I was running it on a PC well above its given system requirements. Another word of warning is that despite it stating on the store page that it runs on Windows 7, it does not. Combine that with a myriad of bugs that plague the title and the constant crashes and the playing through the title becomes a frustrating experience. Another problem that arises with Pro Basketball Manager 2017 is its translation.
The game is set in French by its default language when you start up the game and that is obvious considering its developers origin. But the English translation of the game has many problems. The names of players are spelled wrong, common instructions and rules are difficult to read and understand sometimes.
This might have been a small issue had I been playing NBA or a game of such sorts but in a game where reading and managing is your main work, this does puts an obstacle in the path. If anyone reading this has played a game called “Ea Cricket 2007”, this game reaches those levels of problems with its translation. Overall, while Pro Basketball Manager 2017 is a solid management sim and it has its bright spots, it is bogged down heavily because of its latency issues and the plethora of bugs it contains.
There is nothing to much to say in terms of visuals in a management sim but whatever Pro Basketball Manager 2017 shows, it shows it neatly. The UI is fresh, simple and user friendly. It lets you in the steep learning curves of the game and does not get clunky even when there are a lot of options trying to clutter the screen.
Pro Basketball Manager 2017 is a solid management sim, there is no doubt about that. But it is affected by a huge number of issues which take the game from high to low. The horrible latency issues and the bugs are only the few to state. Pro Basketball Manager 2017 needs polish and a few patches to solve out its problems. But if you are able to run the game properly, you will find a good management sim with a steep but rewarding difficulty curve.

So it's a side-scrolling shooter with a match-3 mechanic bolted-on - that sounds like a bad idea UNLESS you like both genres AND it's done well.
Fortunately, I do like both and it does work well!  All that intense concentration you'd normally deploy avoiding hails of bullets is split into that and the need to clear your path (the match-3 aspect) in a way which just works better than I imagined it could.
It's one of those things which could have gone horribly wrong - but fortunately it actually hasn't.
My only concern right now is that it doesn't seem to have a huge amount of content and high-scoring is perhaps a BIT dependent on luck with layout as much as anything else - but right now, I have to say "It's a winner" because it works.
Note: if you don't like shooters or match-3 it's not going to convert you to either I suspect - but if you're open to the idea, you'll be pleased to know it works.

I’m old enough to have played the original Pac-Man when it was called “Puck Man” in Japan. Yes, I lived in Japan in the 1980’s. “Pac Man” has a special place in my heart. “Pac Man  DX” is actually a very respectable and fun gameplay variant on the orginal Pac-Man, has excellent production values, and I would have given it my highest recommendation, but....
... It has (apparently) NO ARCADE MODE! You can only play in short bursts, in “time attack” mode, and that is just not Pac-Man!!! You can play for five minutes, or ten minutes. No “next level,” and no cartoon intermissions. “Pac Man DX” only allows you a small time limit to play, on one level. Once the timer runs out, GAME OVER, no matter how well you were doing!
THAT’S TERRIBLE!
Pac Man (and just about all sequels and variants) is an endurance game; you keep playing until you lose your last life! Get to the next level, get the next “key”, see the next “cinema,”  keep going as long as you can.... that’s Pac-Man!
If you’re a fan of “Pac Man,” then sure, buy this, expecially if it’s on sale, but you’ll probably be disappointed (as I was). It’s a total shame, because this could have been a seriously good Pac-Man game if it had and endurance/arcade mode, especially if they added cartoon intermissions.

Pac-Man CE DX+ is a wondeful retro update to the arcade classic that's been around now for around 35 years, the object of Pac man is universally known but the aim is pretty simple, collect the dots in the maze, avoid the ghosts, win at life. Simple. however when a game like that has been doing the rounds for 35 years its going to get a little stale and theres only so many times you can remake the title with a slightly different map or add a small twist in an attempt to "Shake things up" before even that fails to improve the game, CE DX+ succeeds where previous attempts have failed in my opinion simply via the act of Variety. it offers a wide range of boards to play with several challenges including time attacks, survival modes, classic play and other features, the boards change colour based on whats occuring on screen and pulse in time to the soundtrack (This soundtrack can begin to grate a little over time but ultimately muting it for your own playlist is simple enough)
Gameplay wise the standard modes on this focus on traversing the maze collecting dots, with the added threat of "Dormant ghosts" who will sleep blocking sections of the maze, once you cross paths with them they will begin to follow you, the aim being to daisy chain so many of the ghosts that when you get a power pellet you can rack up a massive bonus score by eating the amassed ghosts. This is a really nice addition and adds a bit of tension to the time attack modes where you can either focus on racking up a high score or collecting the fruit allowing you to successfully complete rounds...This was a really nice touch that has definately added to the overall experience Add to this an online challenge mode, leader boards, and DLC that offer even more boards and variety and your looking at easily one of the most concise and reinvigorating appearences for this yellow icon for decades. Its definately one of those kinds of games you leave on your computer and break it out whenever your having a bit of a dull moment.

Recreating the feeling of the arcade classic fondly in your own home Pac-Man CE DX+ is a definate reccommendation from me, if it's going for a good price definately pick this up.

Recently there has been a lot of talk about what gaming can do to transcend it's boundaries. A key aspect that games have that other mediums such as movies and book is that we are controlling a character. Now it may be down a set line of events like this little gem is but that added feeling of controlling a character is a valuable tool in getting into the characters head. In this case the head of the character is depressed, I won't go into events that happened but having dealt with depression before and knowing what it feels like this game emulated those feelings to near perfection. To the point where I understood a bit more about what I was going through with the advantage of looking back from the outside at a happier point in my life. I fully suggest this game to everyone, especially those that deal with or know people that deal with depression.

Aside from the horribly short levels and tiny, tiny maps, you'll be spending most of your time in the "town" lobby picking up quests, trading them in for EXP and skill points, running about trying to find a party and crafting or repairing before finally "setting sail" in an unnecessary secondary lobby shaped like a boat in order to finally get to the core of the game- its combat. The combat is magnificent, and the endgame is grand, but if you're not up for a major grind to get there, then this game isn't for you. All in all however, Vindictus is an enjoyable experience and has some of the tightest and most balanced Player versus Player combat to this day. This game is more than likely to be more enjoyable in short spurts.

Edit: I have tried to include all of the different aspects of the game in here, so if there is something that you look for specifically in a game, then you can look through the categories to find what stands out to you.
If you like to play games for just the mechanics and gameplay itself, then this is the game for you, as it doesn't really attempt to do anything other than master those two aspects. I think that the best way to review this game is to review everything individually, as because it's so focused around one aspect you can see the short-comings of the game more clearly... so here goes.
Combat/Fighting/Action_Score - 9.5/10 I rate this a almost perfect score because I believe that Vindictus still has the best combat system of any action MMO that I have ever played. It is quick, deadly and punishing, and reminds me alot of Dark Souls with a bit more flashiness and speed. Where the combat is flawed is tied into the gameplay, as it eventually becomes less enjoyable when you have to participate in an extreme amount of grinding 70+; however, the repetitiveness I will review in more depth below.
Mechanics/Movement/Dodging_Score - 9/10 I feel like this piece of the game needs a separate review from the combat, because it is about the controls and flow more than the actual combat itself. This game is designed extremely well to fit a player's skill level, and isn't a game that relies on equipment (even though it's a very apparent factor when doing raids later on). It doesn't take a long time to get good at dodging and movement as you fight multiple hard-hitting bosses that you are pretty much required to dodge. The only downside of the mechanics is that no matter how good you've become you will need to reach certain gear requirements late game regardless of your skill level, as many of the raids late game require you to have a certain ATTK requirement. This became quite frustrating for me when I had to grind for hours to get enough gold for new equipment, only to join the raids, upon which I witness players who didn't seem like they had really grasped the dodging mechanic.
Graphics/Optimization/Requirements_Score - 8/10 This is another strong area for the game, as the game is optimized very well to allow people to play even on low-end computers with smooth fps. The graphics themselves are good too, and it doesn't take a beefy graphics card too make it look pretty sexy. To go a little deeper I would say that I thought that the textures were really good on max settings, and the meshes for different objects were decent too. I gave this category an 8/10 simply because the graphics are good, but nowhere near perfect.
Characters/Appearance/Custimization_Score - 7/10 The characters on this game are very beautifully made and are extremely good looking ( males and females -.O). There are two reasons why I rated this category as low as I did. The first - most major reason - is that the characters/classes are all gender locked, so right off the bat you will not be able to pick which gender you are if you like to play a certain style of class, and even though this doesn't really bother me too much, alot of people feel like this is a critical part of customization. The other - more minor reason - is that to really customize your character, you will have to spend NX. This is minor because it's pretty much the main purpose of NX aside from bonuses, making this game - for the most part - not Pay2Win, although it does suck that if you do not spend money they hook you up with this silly♥♥♥♥♥inner armor (underwear) that ruins the look of a majority of armors in the game. A way that I'm guessing they wanted to counter this fault is by creating the AP Shop, where you can buy inner amor and hair coupons that last 30 days; however, they cost over 1k AP , which is too much for someone who hasn't already maxed their skills to pay for a 30 day coupon.
Cash Shop/NX/Avatar Shop_Score - 6/10 As you may have noticed the categories are in a descending order, and I will continue like this until I get to the worst parts of the game. The cash shop on Vindictus (The Supply Depot) is slightly better than I see in most games. As I said before, this game isn't really Pay2Win, and this is the case because the things you buy in the Supply Depot are really nice bonuses to have, but the flow of the game is not affected or hindered if you choose not to purchase anything from the Supply Depot. The other shop that they have is the Avatar Shop, and it is a bit more dissapointing then the more basic Supply Depot. This is also because of how NX works in this game. There is prepaid NX, which you get from cards that you buy at the store (also the best to have), and then there is NX credit, which is a purchase that you make online with a credit card. There are certain thing in the Avatar Shop you can only buy with NX prepaid, as there are no restrictions on the prepaid NX that you buy from the store, and there is on NX credit.
Mercenaries/NPCs/Story_Score - 4/10 The story in this game - in short - is a snooze. I think that if you're looking for a game with a really good story then you should perhaps look elsewhere, as this game will not sastify you. For me I honestly really enjoyed the stories of the mercenaries you get when you pick your first character more than I enjoyed the different seasons' stories. I would have loved to see the stories of the mercenaries continued throughout the main quest; however, the main fault is that the game is just too focused on it's action to worry about anything else. The action is the very base of this game, and if you like action then this is a good game for you, but what the devs did was take the action of the game, and then they slapped all of this mediocre content around that base so that they could make it a better game. While this is respectable, they clearly rushed the story to fit the fast pace gameplay, which really didn't work. I read through all of the dialouge in the first chapter and then I just starting clicking through it because I had lost interest.
Community/Players/Guilds_Score - 4/10 To test the community I made several different characters and joined in some basic guilds by simply asking in chat. I'm not going to name any guilds in particular because I wouldn't want to hurt their rep, but there was only 2 guilds I found where the players weren't rude. This is of course all based off of my experience so it is a very rough estimate, and because of this I'm gonna say there is maybe a 50/50 chance you end up in a good guild when you start off. The best thing to do is to find a guild that you like that will accept alts, and stick with them on your multitude of characters. Finding that guild... that may prove challenging.
Now for the worst...
Grinding/Mobs/Repetitiveness_Score - 2/10 This is for me the worst part of the game. If there is even a small part of you that doesn't enjoy repetitiveness, you may want to consider something else. The only thing that makes this flaw of the game less severe is that it really isn't the biggest part of the game. Get rid of the Dark Souls-esque combat and you have a game that has generic mobs that you will need to grind for hours for better equipment, in order to meet ATTK requirements. I also noticed that later on in the game, even when mobs look slightly different, they still look almost exactly the same. For those of you that have already played Vindictus, the reason why this is so low is because I don't include bosses in this category, because I feel like bosses needed to be separated from mobs because of the quality difference. Bosses are part of my review of the gameplay and mechanics because of the fact that they are part of what makes this game great, and they deserve to be separated from the mobs. If at first you don't think something like the mobs or Batte Quests are repetitive, wait til you must grind them for hours on end.
Overall Score - 6.2/10

The thing that got me playing at all was the character cuztomization, This is a decent system and i like the diferent looks and possibilities however. Each class is gender locked which to me seems sounter productive. So if I want to play as a sorceress i must choose "evie" who is female. I can then alter her look however i wish. My question is why gender lock the roles? Now this doens't bother me as i like sorcerers and female avatars but i know some people would be put off by this. Such as if you wish to play the ranger class you must pick a male avatar. etc etc.  Pro: You can alter your character to look pretty much any way you desire, Con: Gender locking classes
Redundancy.
In order to do quests you have to get them from npcs of course then you must locate the battle board to select a dungeon you wish to do.  Then you either join a part who is waiting in the staging area. A rarity i am sure, or create your own party and invite whoever you like. Then you board the boat and see the same dramatic heroic scene reminiscent of soul calibur and off you go , each area has dungeons that look exactly the same. You may go through 10 dungeons that all are nearly identical but rearranged to fight red name bosses and win the day. then back to town. Rinse and repeat. This has become.. redundant.
Population, Seems very low. The starting area "colhen" looks populated but that's as far as it goes. If you decide to venture out to the other few areas of the game where high level players should be doing their thing you'll find a ghost town. This is a shame because now i feel put off form bothering. It appears that everyone just hangs out on colhen. There isn;t a whol elot to ehis game.
Raids. Seems easy to be called raids. I did a raid on the first available raid dungeon with two friends. They died relatively fast but i managed ot finish the boss by myself. Wasn't too difficult even on hard mode. Rewards weren't great either. I imagine these do get harder as you progress if you do that is.
All in all i am not ready to quit the game as of yet so I will keep leveling and seeing what else the game has to offer. mainly because i have nothing better to do these days. Going to recommend the game so more people play it because it seems the only major thing lacking is population. Seems to be a big trend with mmos these days. Shame really. TL;DR: It's a hearthstone reskin
which is fast paced and fun. Initially the game dumps money and card onto you, but the more you play, the more the progression slows down to a crawl.
ES:L is put quite simply, Bethesda's take on Hearthstone with some elements of Gwent. It's a fast paced, simplistic card game which initially feels insanely like Hearthstone.
I'll try and split the review into two sections, multiplayer and singleplayer, but I'll start with my overall thoughts. The game is very fun, especially when you first start. It slowly introduces its gameplay to you, while giving you a fair amount of rewards. The story was enjoyable, rather simple and a little dull, with some interesting mechanics and good rewards. Multiplayer feels relatively balanced and you could stand a chance in casual and early ranks with just a standard deck. However, As perviously stated, if you want to get anywhere, you'll pretty much be locked into one deck and play with that deck for a longgggggg time, since crafting materials and money are obtained slower and slower throughout.
Initially, I was struck by how fun the singleplayer is. You're greeted with the standard 2D yet voice acted card game cutscene, very similar to MTG games or Hearthstone. These consist throughout and there are qiuite a few, which is nice, especially since they're voice acted. Gameplay consists of (usually) 2 lanes with different missions having different effects for different lanes, although this usually consists of a stealth lane (where the played monster cant be hit for a turn) and a normal lane. Every mission rewards you with card/money/decks and exp and there are around 15 missions in the free campaign. By the end of it you will have 5 decks, around 100 cards and some card packs.
The plot (which I gave up on 5 minutes into since it was pretty boring) consists of you being a forgotten Hero who is now a gladiator. You escape a group of cultists with another gladiator named Tyr, then uncover a plot to sacrifice a city to daemons or something? The majority of the missions are just  you encountering standard mobs while  on your way to the city where you plan to warn the king(?) about the impending attack. Overall, it was very lackluster, not what I was expecting from Elder Scrolls. But hey, atleast it was fun and short (maybe a few hours?) gameplay experience with some decent rewards.
While the story itself isn't great, there are some very cool features that you experience through the campaign. Prehaps my favourite was the loosely RPG based choices you come across. At some points, you are granted with a choice between two options (Such as spare or execute someone), neither of which actually have any gameplay impact, but do give you access to some very powerful spells early on and are definitely a nice step towards diffferentiating itself from it's clear inspiration Hearthstone.
At the end of the day though, while it's not a great 'Story', it's still very fun. I binged the campaign and enjoyed all of it, there wasn't really any time when I thought "Just let it end!" Which is good and even made me want to buy the new expansion that was released (so kudos to almost getting me to spend money Bethesda).
Just as a side note, there are 3 single player modes. Campaign, Training and Arena. The first two are self explanatory, but the Arena is slightly different. You build a 30 card deck by picking between 3 cards 30 times. You then play against 8 Bots and upon winning all 8 games unlock the Boss Bot, however if you lose 3 times, You're out. The rewards can be very good if you can get far. Unlike Hearthstone, even beginners can get very far in the arena and get easy packs and gold, due to the games fairly decent synergies and card balancing. It very beginner friendly too, meaning that you could jump in with almost no knowledge about the game and still get a few wins.
If you came here for the story, you'll be dissapointed, but if you came looking for fun, you'll definitley find it within this game.
But lets be honest, if you're playing a F2P card game, you're probably playing for the multiplayer. In the game, there are 3 multiplayer modes:
The multiplayer arena is pretty much the same as the single player arena, except the bots are replaced with other players. This adds an extra level of difficulty and is a welcome change pace and just makes the game feel even more populated.
Exactly what it says on the tin. Just a standard 1v1 game mode. I used this mostly to try out new decks before I used them in competitive. One thing I have to mention is the insanely fast que times. Every single game I've played, I found a match within around 10-20 seconds. Not only this, but somehow the matchmaking just feels like it works. Every loss feels deserved and every win feels hard earned. There hasn't been a single match where it ended with me frustrated by the fact that the other player has put in 1000 hours while I only have a few.
Ahhhh ye old competitive. Prehaps the sole reason you're looking to play this game, or maybe it's just a benefactor of playing long term. The system is a standard card game one, ranging from rank 12-1. Personally, I'm not a fan of this rating system as it doesn't feel as if it accurately represent your skill group. Atleast Hearthstone had 25-1, which helped differentiate the ranks. I only played around 20 matches myself, with around 5-6 using a standard deck, and the rest with a 7k souls deck build. One thing that pleased me imensely was the balancing. Prehaps it's just the early ranks, but all the cards feel fair and there weren't any that made me rage or say "GG" as soon as they were played, much unlike Hearthstone and other card games. Even once I built my semi-decent deck, I still lost a few games to people using standard decks, who put simply, were far more skilled than me. And that's great, exactly how a game should be.
If I had to say anything bad about it, it's the fact that it doesn't feel rewarding. The rewards are no different to playing casual and I'm not even sure if you get extra rewards at the end of a season like Hearthstone. To be honest, you're better off just learning good card synergies and playing arena as competitive just doesn't give you any form of satisfaction, but hey- That's just my opnion.
There are a few things I want to mention on the side though-
- No matter how you cut it, it feels insanely like a Hearthstone reskin. But that's not terrible. The gameplay is different and fun enough that it's hard to really care about it.
- Very good interface/UI. It's very clear and simplistic, especially if you've played Hearthstone. There was never a point where I wasn't quite sure what I should be clicking or doing.
- The card art is interestingly stylised. It reminds me alot of Magic the gathering, yet feels alot more like Gwent's card art. It's very fantasy Esque, but isn't quite as realistic and 'High-fantasy'-like as MTG.
- On the same note, The card borders aren't very interesting. They're very plain with maybe some metalic corners. The different rarities don't look much different and none of the borders stand out. It's not a terrible thing, doesn't make the game unplayable or anything, it just leads to visual burnout pretty early on.
-On the other hand, the board (while static and unchanging) looks very good. It really captures the elder scrolls theme very well, but it's static repetitiveness can also lead to visual burnout.
At the end of the day the game is very balanced and fun. There aren't any major problems and nothing that really detracts from the game. The only advice I can give is to play in short bursts, as personally if you play it for anymore than an hour or so, you begin to feel visual burnout aswell as the gameplay becoming slightly repetitive. However, there is plenty of joy to be found in the simplistic yet detailed gameplay.

The game is simple and straight forward and I love it.
All of the cars are JDMs, but you can mod it and there are mods for other manufacturers, too. They do indeed have all the JDM engines and sounds. But it`s not a sim, so personally I don`t care about that.
Several tracks that come standard are pretty complex and interesting, you can have fun for hours trying to master the track and getting used to your car. There are also other tracks available through mods.
Talking about tuning your car - there are engine swaps and some basic mods you can apply. You can tune your car from ~100 hp to almost 1000 hp (probably more, haven`t really had a need to). You can set up your suspension however you want and that really is a cherry on top of everything, but I`m not really sure if it has any functionality (camber, etc). You can even change your power split between front and rear wheels. Basically you can have front wheel drive car and go out and try do "drift".
Visual tuning - Some cars have some basic bbody kits, nothing special. Most cars don`t have anything tunable visually exept for rims.
Driving experiance - I`m playing with keyboard and I`ve got used to it. You can use manual clutch, turn steering assist off and really test your skill, but that is impossible with keyboard. So it actually is pretty playable with keyboard. And I`m huge racing game fan.
Yes - I do recommend it.
PS. About unresponsive devs. After the infamous 2.5 update they listened and brought back old physics (as you can see in recent updates tab). That is, I think, awesome from them. I would love to see some new tracks or some new cars for the game from devs. Or maybe some new functionalities. Anyway - I hope the game isn`t dead.
Oh - if the devs are reading these - Cmon guys, give us achievements and trading cards (I`d love to craft a badge for this game).

I really like this game.
I found the single player story mode engaging and fun.  The story is delightfully goofy with charming characters.  Yes, this is a match 3 puzzle game, but new gimmicks are introduced with each new stage.  Adjusting your strategy to handle these gimmicks can sometimes be daunting, and the steady introduction of these gimmicks is what really made the game for me.  The puzzles do all have fail states, but I think that's what makes the single player work.
In addition to the story mode, there are a handful of infinite play modes - all of which have caused me to lose hours in a day.  I have yet to play the multiplayer (I need friends), but I'm guessing at least one mode is a race against your opponents to solve a set of puzzles.
A lot of the negative reviews have to do with the price.  I admittedly didn't pay the full asking price for this, but I've had way more fun with this than I have with some $60 games I'd purchased in the past.  Yes, it's $25 for a match-3 puzzle game, but it's a match-3 puzzle game with a lot more depth than you'd expect.  The challenge increases at a reasonable rate, and I frequently told myself "just one more try" when I couldn't solve a puzzle.  If you're judging the game solely based on the first two or three stages of single player (and thus, the first two not very innovative gimmicks), you're doing yourself a severe disservice.

"The first original action-puzzle game of the past fifteen years; completely reinventing the genre into a deep and cerebral puzzle solving experience."? Ehhhh....
Tumblestone is *not* a bad game. It's a mediocre, design-by-numbers puzzle game, with a decent multiplayer mode and a hyper-inflated price.
The story is mostly unfunny non-sequitur humor with a lot of pacing issues. The gameplay get's repetitive very quick, and the game lacks anything to remedy  this. It's sort of a mix of klax and bust-a-move; you pick columns, and always eliminate the bottom tile of the selected column, and you need to do this in threes of the same color. The challenge is to choose an order of eliminating columns that allows you to clear the board without  getting stuck in a situation where you cannot choose three tiles of the same color sequentially.
Weirdly the game has not mechanism to detect when you've painted yourself in a corner, and instead you need to either "kill yourself" by selecting a mixed-color trio, which restarts the level, or access the menu and manually restart the level.
tl;dr: At a lower price point, with some of the transitions sped-up and allowing players to skip story "cutscenes" (still images with mumbled non-sense to accompany subtitles) I might recommend Tumblestone, but as it is, you can get much more bang for your 23€

Like many, I see similarities to the board game 'Hero Quest' -- though it's a bit simpler than that even.
Move around a 2D tile map with 1-3 characters -- basically fighter, rogue, wizard -- fighting various critters, collecting loot, looking out for traps.
Especially if you are into game design, there's a lot to see here -- good and bad.
Good: simple point and click gameplay, and some neat, easy to use mechanics. Nostalgia, if you played similar board games.
Bad: A (near as I can tell) random "skull of fate" that, most often, costs you health or moves, very (very, very) rarely giving a benefit (point of health). There's not enough explanation of a lot of the gameplay, nor enough content to last more than a few hours. And one thing I'd change -- your movement/attack for the turn on each character is a single click -- no moving cautiously one square at a time or moving the path/distance you want before an attack.
Overall, though, I'd say give it a go -- especially if you can get it on sale.

Killer is dead, a hack n' slash packed with incredibly out of this world characters created by the famed Suda51 isn't exactly what I expected but is more than likely what I should have expected from the start. However there is such a thing as 'going full retard' as spoken in Tropic Thunder and unfortunetly Killer is Dead is an example of that.
Suda51 who is no stranger to bizarre imagery and storylines doesn't hold back here and fans will surely find satisfaction. But what we thought we were getting turned out to be bottled up teen angst stuffed further into a video game with just good enough gameplay for us to be a part of... As if we didn't get enough of that already.
Soundtrack
To start the sound by Akira Yamaoka whom I believe was the sound producer has given his weakest performance yet. He has done a lot of music for Grasshopper studios and I can confidently say that I've enjoyed his work more in the past. There were sometimes where I felt the tunes for the game hit the bill but overall it was forgettable.
Gameplay
Gameplay was something of a hit and miss for me. I liked that you could kill your enemies almost instantly with a touch of a button once you had filled enough of a meter for it. Additionally the combos you pick up on the way add a little more depth to the fighting. I liked that you could pick up gun variations but I found that the gun wasn't very useful unless you got a headshot on lesser enemies. I really enjoyed the fact that Mondo (The MC) began to pick up speed as you built up the combo meter. Unfortunetly it just doesn't build fast enough and often you won't be able to maintain it because it decreases. Making the game a very slow going hack n slash most of the time. I also did not like the fact that in order to unlock the gun variations you had to go through the date missions. Missions which I wish were less apparent in this game. They are pretty dam perverted and I ended up playing this entire game at night when no one was around partially because of how often I ended up doing them to get the upgrades.
Other than that the bosses were the best part of this entire game. They are incredibly creative and are more than just a damage sponge with the same moves which is too often typical in games.
The level settings in the game were another high point. You go to a lot of different locations and they are all pretty dam cool. The only unfortunate thing here is how linear they are. The extra missions were okay but just felt like an attempt to extend game time.
Story
The characters and story in this game are the absolute worst part about it. From the first cutscene you know that you are going to be listening to 8 hours of the most absurdly childish dialoge you have ever heard in your life. I honestly think I've seen parody movies with less cheesy lines and cringe moments than this game has. And it's all done with serious tone which just made it harder to listen to. You seriously will not be able to play this game around other people who are not open minded without being judged. It's no joke.
Graphics
Honestly I think the graphics in this game are god awful. The aesthetic choice fits all the ♥♥♥♥ing wacko characters but it's not really a shining example of even cell shaded games. Even the dated No More Heroes is easier on the eyes. Blocky but still didn't strain me eyes the way this game did. It looks like comic book style almost. I'd even say that it's like if you filled in Mad World with colors. It's not that bad but honestly the lighting and the color palettes are so poor.
Overall it was still an enjoyable game. It had high points and it had low points. You really got to come into this one completely unfastend and just play. If you're already a fan of Suda 51 you will probably enjoy it. If you've never heard of him and you're interested in the game it will still be fun to play I can assure you but how much you enjoy the experience as a whole might be limited to how much cringe you can handle.

I want to like Far Cry 2. I have not finished it, because I just can't. Please read on.
After playing the first Far Cry game and absolutely loving it, I was up for something along the same lines but also something that improved upon the first (graphics, story, and variability). I had read that Far Cry 2 was "the best in the series" according to Rock, Paper, Shotgun and after reading their reasoning, it made sense to me, even before playing. To my dissapointment, though, the game was a huge letdown. It was a huge step forward in some ways from the first installment but a massive step back in other ways, which I will get to later. I liked the feel of being weak and having the disadvantage instead obeing a Rambo strongman out to kill everything that moves because it makes the game difficult and also is a fresh breath of air i nthe midst oif other games like the newer Far Cry's, COD, etc... but for a game coming out at around the same time as COD:WaW (a COD masterpiece if you ask me, and no I don't love all of the CODs), Bioshock (probably the best game ever, if not top 5), and Dead Space (an instant classic with true replayability if you want a challenge), this game truly felt empty, confused, and lost.
PROS:
-Graphics were pretty good. The sunsets and lighting were nice to behold and for the time they were alright.
-Open world, sandbox style gameplay made for a alrge map with varied terrain and objects.
-Many weapons to use and vehicles to operate are always welcome in a FPS.
-The difficulty! Ah yes, the difficult nature of this game is truly a welcome aspect. Your guns jams if not replaced often, you wheeze and slow down after running too long, malaria strikes randomly, etc... These make the game hard but what else is a game supposed to be? Easy? These more realistic aspects mixed up the gameplay entirely and it was amazing to see how it felt.
-Element of choice in missions made me feel like I was choosing my fate or my play style at least.
-Destructible environments to small degree. Fire can spread to different areas, gas cans can explode, cars need fixing, and a few other things can be manipulated which spiced thigns up a bit.
-I liked the first-person animations, like reaching to pick up things, heal, etc...
CONS: Oh there are many of them but I will stick to the main ones.
-Story. I'm confused, all the time. Why am I here? Who are these factions? Why are they fighting? Why am I involved?
-Why does everyone shoot me? I get it, it's a civil war but why does every NPC kill me at first glance instead of occasionally letting me pass albeit susiciously? No love for the white guy?! Even in Far Cry 1 the enemies had a reason to kill at first sighting. Not in this one necessarily.
-The outposts are all the same, with the same 3 enemy types (clothes). There's a British guy, a black guy, and a darker black guy at every outpost. Even after killing them they respawn there later.
-Too much driving. The mechanics are horrible and for an aspect that takes up more than half the time of gameplay, it should be better oir more exciting.
-Gunfights are boring. Bad recoil, HORRID gun sounds (are we shooting cap guns or Kalishnikovs here?), and low ammo made me want to avoid gunfights altogether, which isn't good in a FPS.
-The soundtrack and sounds in general are really quite bad. The "danger music" (that most games have to alert you to the fact that someone has spotted you, that you are in danger, an enemy is near, etc...) is annoying and not very effective. The gun sounds are very, very weak and don't convince me I am firing a weapon that shoots actual ammunition. Airsoft perhaps?
-The missions are all the same and the worst part is they are all boring. By hour 2 I wanted the game to be 90% done so that I could spend another 20 minutes beating it and moving on to another installment, it's that bad.
-The vocie acting is sped up on every person. WHY?
-This game is a CHORE.
5/10 will probably not even give another chance. Overall this game is innovative for it's time in some ways but is just laborous and even then I don't mind harsh, tedious games as long as it's fun. But Far Cry 2 just isn't that - fun.
Go for Far Cry 1 or skip to Far Cry 3.

Galacide Review in 30 Seconds,
A puzzle shoot’em up that fuses the best parts of R-Type and Bust A Move.
You must multitask by switching between problem-solving and killing aliens. Destroy defense walls bit by bit with matching pieces you collect from enemies. If things get tough, brute force your way through with a bomb instead - just do what you have to do to keep the alien scourge at bay.
Play it solo or bring up to three friends along for a more hectic adventure. If you're burned out, relax with puzzle mode instead.
7 green men out of 10

Galacide is an odd hybrid of shoot-em-up and match-4, but unlike games like Puzzle Quest, it mixes the two genres into one functional whole, rather than separate elements in one game.
If you enjoy the two genres, or want more puzzling in your shooting, I definitely recommend checking it out. It's niche, but it's a very sweet blend.
If your'e into Shmups. One Word: Brilliant!

I’m going to try and refrain from making any more ball jokes than I have already, in the linked video. Galacide is a wonderful gem of a game that takes Galaga-like action and smashes it together with the puzzling aspects of Bejeweled or Bubble-Bobble. Enemy ships descend on your position constantly, and need to be blown up to gain scrap of varying colors which can be used to create combos. Decisions need to be made quickly since the screen constantly scrolls to the right, and getting left behind can have explosive results.
Thankfully, there are a decent amount of power-ups that drop after particularly large combos. The fact that the dropped upgrade depends on the color of the combo is extremely helpful, and serves to add yet another layer of depth. If that doesn’t sweeten the deal enough, there are also four ships with extremely unique abilities that allow you to customize your playstyle quite effectively, provided that you have unlocked them. Do you want to pull scrap towards yourself, or simply phase through it? By phasing through it you miss out on combos, but not dying is always a plus.
Boss fights are challenging, but after puzzling your brain out to avoid an untimely death it feels like a very welcome change. Fight mechanics are switched up relatively often, so the bosses are always something to look forward to. Unfortunately, Galacide does have some weaker points as well. I don’t particularly enjoy the music, and think the sound effects could use more work. The story is lackluster, with an absence of character development. The graphics are nice, but I feel neon colors contrast with the dark, sparse nature that being in space would imply.
These are minor issues, as this game is certainly carried by the puzzles. If it seems like something you would enjoy, please leave a comment on the youtube video mentioned previously and your name will be entered to win one of two Steam keys. Big thanks to Puny Human games for the review copy. I see myself returning to this game to get my fix of puzzling for a good long while. I also greatly look forward to watching Galacide’s player-base grow as it certainly deserves to. I can’t stop matching colors, unfortunately it won’t serve to improve ones sense of fashion.

I decided to try this game on a whim because of some of the reviews but upon further inspection i realize I may be late to this party. I rolled on the US East server, there were 3 choices, US East, US West, and Aus i think? Well here has been my experience playing to level 20.
The thing that got me playing at all was the character cuztomization, This is a decent system and i like the diferent looks and possibilities however. Each class is gender locked which to me seems sounter productive. So if I want to play as a sorceress i must choose "evie" who is female. I can then alter her look however i wish. My question is why gender lock the roles? Now this doens't bother me as i like sorcerers and female avatars but i know some people would be put off by this. Raids. Seems easy to be called raids. I did a raid on the first available raid dungeon with two friends. They died relatively fast but i managed ot finish the boss by myself. All in all i am not ready to quit the game as of yet so I will keep leveling and seeing what else the game has to offer. mainly because i have nothing better to do these days. You always have to remember that the world does not level at the same pace you do and sometimes the only viable option is avoidance or fleeing; enough hints are normally provided that you can suss that out before you lose one of your precious villagers.  I highly reccomend this to anyne who can enjoy a game where there is a real chance of winning or losing on each playthrough.
